lines.text: Savathûn really thought getting her old memories back would make her more dangerous. And… well… it did.
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Savathûn's Altar reacts to your presence, and the presence of others like Immaru. It might react to other meaningful things.
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: Failure is always an option. Don't start until you're sure losing can still further your agenda. Savathûn knew this, and so should you.
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: "I make the weapon mine. But I do not keep it… I use it as a lure."
The Altar raised more questions than it answered, but it did fill in an important blank about Savathûn's link to the Relic and the Enigma it shaped.
The Altar seems to have become an ever-shifting space, making it an excellent place to search for clues.
A new report awaits you on the Evidence Board. The Hidden have all but confirmed the emergence of a new access point to the Altar of Reflection.
With Savathûn out of commission, this chance to delve into another of her memories is too good to pass up.
Ikora wants you to bring the Enigma to the Altar and see if you can uncover any remaining psychic traces. The Glaive is the investigation's strongest link between the Relic and the Witch Queen.

In fact, it's the only link you have. If you're looking for answers to Ikora's lingering questions—why Savathûn chose to reappear over Mars, what her Ghost is up to, what they know about the Witness and what's to come—then the Altar is your best shot.
The ever-changing Altar has proven to hold some truths about Savathûn's secrets, namely her connection to the Relic and the Enigma it shaped.
Savathûn was talking about the Enigma. Which you shaped with the Relic, thanks to the fragment you found on her ship.

Your mind whirrs through the logic of Savathûn's plan. By converting to the Light, she lost her memories and her Darkness-borne magic. Thus, she needed a Guardian who could harness the power of Deepsight via the Relic.
And what better way to lure a Guardian than with the promise of a powerful weapon?
In other words, you can expect that the access point of the Altar will change—as will the tales you hear within. Still, if the Hive God of Cunning has more to say, it would be worth it to listen.
Bring the Enigma to the new Altar access point in the Temple of the Wrathful and see what you can uncover.

"She's been more responsive lately. You've been out there, protecting our people—even she has to admit that much."

"I mentioned that I've been working with Variks to track down more information about tonics. Eramis said she knew a couple of older Eliksni with knowledge of such things. If we could track down an apothecarist, it would speed up my research considerably!"

"In the meantime, Eramis also spoke of a Salvation enclave that might need our help. I sent Crow the coordinates. I… might have left out the part where Eramis gave them to us… I think we can trust Eramis to look after the interests of her own people. I'm sure Crow will see that soon enough."
"So much has happened… I can't believe the H.E.L.M. is gone. We must operate out of the Last City for now."
"Old Riis was suffused with the Light of the Great Machine. Some of these ingredients must have been too."
"But I know there's a solution here somewhere. I won't give up until I find it."
"Your support is many-armed, as always, Guardian! Thank you for representing my father as his Slayer Baron. I've left you something for your trouble."
"I'm glad the City allowed us to build Variisis Core near the Market District. With this new lab and workshop, I was able to make you all kinds of equipment."
"I wish I could focus on curing my father, but Fikrul won't stop until all Eliksni are turned. We need to support your battle against the Revenants."
"Along with your title comes a gift: your Slayer Baron Apothecary Satchel. It may be small, but it's reinforced and filled with ingredients. May it protect you as you protect us."

The final step of the formula seems to portray the familiar form of the Traveler, infusing the contents of the flasks with its energy. From a practical standpoint, this seems a bit hyperbolic.
An inscrutable list of reagents is scrawled upon the tattered parchment in a reckless, tilting script, followed by a rambling thesis on the nature of decay. Luckily there's a picture!
So far, we've been trying to study a gun without loading it. We need to actually chamber a round and let 'er rip… safely, of course.

I've hit it with every tool in my high-tech belt, and all I can say is… it's probably not hollow. That much I got from knocking on it.

lines.text: So the Light isn't enough for Immaru and his Lucent Brood, huh? That's as ambitious as it is worrying.
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: Calling it a 'schematic' is mostly just being polite. It's more like… like remembering how your grandma made pies.
lines.speaker: Agent JAI-701

lines.text: Anything you leave here, we can keep studying while you're in the field. Consider us your backup brains!
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: The Hidden have a list of Throne World weapons that can shed light on the link between Weapon Patterns and Osmic Fragments. Use that as a guide.

In other words, the Darkness energy infused in the Osmic Fragments from Fynch is compatible with the Relic. Those energy readings are strikingly similar to the Weapon Patterns used to operate the Relic. The Hidden think the fragments are essentially weak, incomplete Weapon Patterns, but they need more data to be certain.
Shape more weapons using the Relic to confirm this connection. By analyzing complete Patterns, you might be able to determine whether the Osmic Fragments are truly compatible with the Relic.

You confirmed that the Relic, when paired with Weapon Patterns, allows the user to reach through time, rearranging memories into weaponry. There's no telling what else it can do in the hands of a powerful entity like the Witness.

Ikora posited before that the Relic caused the temporal wounds on Mars's surface. You believe she's right, and that the Witness used the device to learn about the planet's Golden Age and Collapse, leaving Mars irreversibly damaged.

Your report states that the Weapon Patterns you used are essentially Darkness-infused "memory road maps" to the weapons the Relic creates. The Osmic Fragments are a weaker, incomplete road map—but with enough fragments, someone could build the equivalent of a Weapon Pattern.

The Relic is clearly capable of anything from creating weapons to tearing the fabric of reality. If Immaru gathers enough Osmic Fragments and finds a way to approximate the functions of the Relic—perhaps by using the runes you discovered in the Throne World—there's no telling what he might create.
In the meantime, there are other angles of investigation to consider. Check the other Hidden reports for more leads.
It's confirmed: the Osmic Fragments are similar to the Weapon Patterns, but much weaker. It would take many Fragments to add up to one Pattern.
The Hidden believe the Osmic Fragments and the Weapon Patterns used by the Relic might be related. They need you to generate data by shaping weapons.

Rummaging around a battlefield in the aftermath… it's definitely not pleasant work, but it does yield interesting results.
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: Scorn lines of communication? Almost nonexistent. Not a lot to eavesdrop; they're not exactly chatty. Easier to get info from the source.
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: Basic strategy, isn't it? Your enemy needs a resource, you try and control it first. Let's hope that's the only thing motivating the Scorn.
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: Leave your metaphysical souvenir with us. I want to run some more tests… Sweep it for bugs and scrying effects.
lines.speaker: Agent LAI-701

lines.text: You know the Scorn are after Immaru's runes, but you don't know why. Target challenging Scorn to intercept their marching orders.
The orders reveal a plan to use the Lucent Hive's "defensive" runes against them. Assemble a fireteam to thwart the Scorn's scheme at the Wellspring.
You peer at the burnt page. The Eliksni-adjacent scrawl is too charred to read, but at the bottom, you spot a crude, but unmistakable drawing of… the resonant Hive rune.
Now, why are the Scorn hunting down Hive runes? And why the specific kind that Savathûn's Ghost cares so much about?
You need to see the marching orders in full. Target Scorn elites in the Throne World to intercept their orders.
The Scorn's defense of the Wellspring has been upended. No Hive runes turned up, but you did find another Osmic Fragment.
The Osmic Fragment from the Wellspring seems to have a stronger pulse than the others.
Did the Scorn's temporary possession have an effect? Or is the resonance amplified by the nearby presence of the other fragments?

More importantly, do the Scorn know what Immaru intends to do with the Osmic Fragments? They must. If they know the runes are for some kind of Lucent Brood defense, then the Osmic Fragments are undeniably part of that.
It would help if you knew the runes' specific purpose. You glance at the Hidden's open query. No progress yet.
In the meantime, there are other angles of this case to consider. Check the other Hidden reports for more leads.
Don't underestimate the Scorn… especially considering their recent alliance with the Witness. They are unrelenting.

lines.text: Looks like we've got new intel at the Evidence Board.

lines.text: Good work out there. We've almost got a full picture of what the Scorn are up to.

lines.text: The Scorn are retrofitting the runes to… infuse Hive worms into living creatures. Must be a continuation of Rhulk's experiments.

Based on the reports from those who first entered to defeat Rhulk, it seems these ritualistic experiments were a holdover from the plans of the disciple himself.
One Hidden agent goes so far as to speculate that the Scorn Caretaker was itself the result of a successful worm-fusion.
Whatever the Scorn know of Immaru's plans, it's enough to motivate them to enhance their power further in order to counter his moves.

"Ah yes, good stuff, Qualichor. Except not good, actually. Very bad." Fynch nudges a small vial to catch the single, putrid drop your efforts have created. "Made from brain juice and nightmares. Yeah, it's liquid Deepsight, but brew it just right, and it'll 'bring memories into present reality.' That's what the Witches said, at least. Don't think anyone ever tried refining it like this before, though. Anyway, I know this place where the Hive used to store some great artifact. Why don't you head over there, chug this refined Qualichor, and help yourself to the memory of something nice. I'm almost certain you won't go blind!"

The Alembic bubbles and churns. Degraded strands of experience within—a thrash of pain, the smell of tears on hot stone, a Thrall's first breath—tickle your Deepsight. The brew smells like defiance and last words.
Savathûn's Executioners use the fluid Qualichor to access Deepsight and track their prey. If you concentrate enough of it in the Memory Alembic, you can uncover long-forgotten memories.

Now that you know Immaru's scheme, you can turn the tables on him. Take the Osmic Fragment to Queen's Bailey to use as a lure.
Immaru escaped, but his scheme has been foiled for good. Take the Osmic Fragment and the runes back to the Evidence Board and log your final report.
According to the Hidden, Queen's Bailey is the site for Immaru's shaping ritual. Take the Osmic Fragment there to use as a lure.
The Lucent Brood have taken the Osmic Fragment lure. If you follow them, they should lead you right to Immaru.
Now that you've officially closed the case, you should go to the Relic and find out what weapon Immaru and the Lucent Brood planned on shaping.
Immaru escaped in the chaos, but he left behind the Osmic Fragment and the runes. Retrieve the evidence to ensure that he won't be attempting this scheme again.
You believe you saw the Lucent Brood take the Osmic Fragment. Verify that the bait was taken, then follow them.
While some questions still linger, Ikora and her Hidden are now armed with far more answers than when they first stepped foot on the returned Mars.

Thanks to you, the purpose of the Relic has been revealed and put to good use, Savathûn's throne world has been thoroughly investigated, and the schemes of the Lucent Brood have been officially foiled.
And though Immaru may have escaped justice once again, the Lucent Brood won't be getting their claws on advanced weapons anytime soon.
Speaking of, there is one more mystery you can solve. You still don't know what weapon Immaru was so desperate for. What pattern lurks within the Osmic Fragments?
Immaru has ordered the Lucent Brood to attack. Defeat them so you can end this scheme once and for all.

Thanks to the data you generated, the Hidden have found that resonant runes are essentially a Hive-magic imitation of the Relic. Which means the compatible resonance of the Osmic Fragments are actually an indication of a Weapon Pattern stored.
Or rather, a piece of one. Hence, Immaru's determination to collect all the fragments.
Then, as soon as he'd make the pattern whole, he could use the runes to shape as many specialized weapons the Lucent Brood could ever ask for.
If only you hadn't gotten your hands on the fragments first. Without those, Immaru will have to improvise.
And he undoubtedly will. So, Ikora proposes a turning of the tables. According to the Hidden, the shaping ritual is meant to take place in Queen's Bailey.
After reviewing the case, the Hidden have a plan of action. Return to the Evidence Board in the Enclave for next steps.
Go to the Relic to shape your reward.

"Riven's last clutch, plucked from the void and saved from extinction. Maybe that bodes well for the rest of us."
"Thank you, Guardian. For everything. See you starside."
"It's no small feat, the things you've helped accomplish today."
"Riven was never truly an ally, but common cause aligned us in a way I had not anticipated. Relying on her was a risk, true."
"But there was a time when the Vanguard was averse to trusting me as well."
"Trust is dangerous, risky, vulnerable. But to trust is to hope, and what is life without it?"

"Expunge the Vex from the dreaming halls while Osiris prepares the Veil to forge a bridge to my brother. This will allow you to lead a strike force into the Traveler's Pale Heart and rendezvous with Crow."
"From there, it will be the fight of your lives. Steel yourself… You fight for all of us."
"Doing so will require a great expenditure of my power. The Techeuns will not be able to maintain my conjuring afterward."
"Which is to say… that the wish will be our farewell, O Guardian mine."
"What a strange life this has been."
"And though it was all Taken from me, in the end, my murderer set me free and ensured the future of the progeny my mate and I created."
"Now I will sacrifice my own lingering existence to ensure your future in return."
"Perhaps… I am more like Taranis than I would like to admit. He always claimed I was."
All your efforts have led you here. Use the Wall of Wishes to set the wish into motion.
The wish is made, Riven is no more, and Crow has begun his journey into the unknown. Mara Sov wants to speak with you about all that has transpired.
Crow remains uncertain about what the future holds—but not about his decision. He regards you seriously.
In securing Riven's clutch, you have averted the annihilation of a species.
Hope, she says, is what separates us from the Witness.
With the entire clutch now safely secured, the plan can proceed. Crow has parting words for you.
It is time to recover the final egg. Speak to Riven via the portal in the H.E.L.M.
Riven confirms that the time has come for you to retrieve the last remaining egg from the heart of the Confluence—and for Riven to fulfill her promise.
Riven looks about the chamber, musing about the journey that brought her here.
The bargain you have struck with the Spirit of Riven nears completion. Venture into the heart of the Confluence and retrieve the last of the Ahamkara eggs.
A custom pouch with attached Tonic Capsule for mixing various resources found in the field.
A gift for the Slayer Baron, in thanks for the burden you carry on behalf of all Eliksni.
May it grant you many-armed protection as you face Fikrul.
There are two great challenges we face: one kinetic, against the Revenant Scorn; one corporeal—my father's curse.
But Slayer Baron tonics may save us from both, as they did the ancient Eliksni during the beast hunts on Riis of old.

According to Crow's report, Fikrul's new breed of Scorn is made from our living flesh. He doesn't even need to kill us to turn us anymore. The transmutation sounds ontological in nature—just like my father's condition.
The original Barons used apothecary mixers such as this one to brew eclectic medicines. We'll leverage similar tonics as combat and utility enhancements in the field.
Before the Whirlwind, there were seven Eliksni scholia that informed tonic creation: Innervation, Conduction, Effervescence, Tenacity, Vigor, Euthermia, and Cognition.
All of which will be useful to us as battlefield treatments, provided I can get your help with fieldwork and experimentation.
Don't worry! I'm certain we can modernize these tonics to affect just your Guardian abilities and not your physiology. Mostly certain. We'll need every advantage we can find.

Fikrul's actions on Europa have made clear that he sees our people as transgressions. No matter the House, whether we are friends of humanity or not. Distress calls from Eliksni enclaves across the system are flooding public frequencies.
I implore you to win this war. Not to fulfill a prophecy, or secure a title for my father. To prevent our extinction.

lines.text: "The data suggests radiolite is how the Vex are iterating on their biological structure, or in this case, geological."

"Speaking of geological… I have another gift for you, Captain. Based on various surveys and previously restricted analytical data about Guardian armaments usage, statistically, you're going to like it."
"The Vex have assimilated these old Cabal planetary mining pistons to agitate the crust. But we can use it to promote the formation of radiolite and unearth more incubators."
"Some of these Vex were… less than compliant. There's evidence they were assimilated. But, hey, as long as they're dead—am I right?"
This is not regulation size.
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: "Captain, I am so glad that you and I are able to embark on this journey of exploration and research together, in the metaphorical sense. I will be with you in spirit, and through radio transmissions, and satellite telemetry data, but not physically."

"I'll begin my analysis right away. These new structures of radiolaria may reveal something about why Nessus, and the Vex, are changing. In the meantime, the radiolite's methodology for reformatting data has given me an idea for fabricating new fireteam equipment. More updates in the future."
"For now, we should figure this radiolite stuff out. The Vex have always been focused on changing what's around them to suit them, not the other way around."
First research project in the bag. We could keep this up forever, right?

"War always comes with a cost… but every day seems to bring a new one. There's never time to rebuild. When this is done, if we're still standing, the Reef and its people come first for me."

"Guardians complain of the nature of Ahamkara, that we hoard secrets like you hoard weapons. Then you understand us. Why demand a river flow uphill?"
"Now hear me out," he says. "If you go through the portal, there's no way we can send anyone in after you. You'd be out there on your own."

Crow's been thinking about Riven's revelation that only one person can enter the portal. And he's got a new idea to throw into the ring.

Zavala, your most recent correspondence came as a surprise; while I thank you and Ikora for undergoing the formality of lifting my exile, I had not expected any additional direction from Vanguard High Command—and so I have not read it.

The zealots that followed me to Mercury have proved themselves useful… twice now, actually. They possessed an artifact in their stores: a Hive fang. Look to the grooves that run along its root. They allow it to break away from the jaw so that another may take its place. The Hive bear resemblance to another predator I found in simulations of ancient Earth. I don't imagine you've ever seen a shark, Zavala, but you would admire their simplicity and single-minded devotion. They are creatures of predatory instinct. Pure, in a way, to know what one is and act on it. They are not unlike our enemy. Not evil, but driven.

You will receive a case. Within it, you will find said fang; it is of Xivu Arath, Hive aspect of war. In my travels, I found similar artifacts ground and burnt upon a shrine buried deep beneath Luna's crust. The shrine reeks of Hive magic, and it is obviously the site of a ritual. I fear that in reaction to our Dark visitors, the broken ranks, left leaderless after Hashladûn's demise, called out to be recommitted into the fold. It is time to act, Zavala. She means to test our vulnerability.
Do not wait in your office for the Traveler to guide you. The City looks to the Vanguard to lead us to something better than fear. Be that leader, and I will stand by you.
An occult kibisis holding a shed tooth of the Hive god of war.
"She acts in earnest, and so she acts predictably. She's betrayed her nature…"
"To be bound to that place would take me from one jailer to another."
"My sisters are now hollow. Blunted…"
"Guardian, the Sunless Cell lies open and reverberations of Dark chants can be heard resonating from its depths."
"We must not let Xivu Arath's plans come to fruition. Hit her first and disrupt whatever it is she is attempting."
Xivu Arath weaves a ritual to tear into my throne and steal away the Echo. Silence her, my Knife.
lines.speaker: Eris Morn

lines.text: Whatever spell the Witch Queen weaves is tied to Oryx's lineage. It is not dissimilar to how we bound the Echo with Akka's flesh.
lines.speaker: Eris Morn

lines.text: He conveys to us that his sister is attempting to steal him from Eris's throne—he can feel it and has no wish to be chained from one warden to another.
He bids us to stop her, if we are strong enough.

The Echo of Navigation, Oryx, has shared disdain for his sister's attempts, and has challenged you to defeat them. He believes his heir, you, will resist them, and if you are able to resist then his sisters do not deserve to take him. Let the sword logic prevail.
You will receive all rewards, regardless of your selection.
The Dreadnaught hangs in the cold dead silence of space, awaiting your attempts to subdue it. It is time.

Eris is known as the avatar of vengeance within Hive broods, and you as her Knife. Sloane believes that if we hit the Hive we can break their focus and delay any further assaults against Eris' throne.
Strike the Hive while Eris and Sloane research how to utilize the hilt of Willbreaker.
Your weapon is forged. Your allies stand by your side. It is time to launch a final assault on the Dreadnaught and slay the Resonant Knife.

You have a plan of action to move forward with. Despite lingering doubts from the Deputy Commander, you know that Eris is strong and can be trusted. Now your attention must be focused on the Dreadnaught.
You will receive each reward, regardless of your selection.
With a new hilt for Willbreaker in our possession, and Xivu Arath's plan halted, the Hive sisters regroup for another attack. In the lull, we have a moment to retaliate.
Savathûn's ritual has been prevented, and Oryx's Echo remains bound to Eris's throne world. You have secured the head of Malok—nephew to the Taken King, and Savathûn's son.

The Echo of Navigation is firmly in the grasp of Eris Morn and Deputy Commander Sloane thanks to the efforts of the Guardian. Now, the Vanguard moves to purge the Dreadnaught of Taken corruption, defeat the Dread, and snuff out this threat before it can take form.
You are tasked with taking a fireteam into the Sunless Cell in order to stop a ritual conducted by Xivu Arath and to steal away the Echo of Navigation.
Continue to stem the tide as the Vanguard studies the Echo for a way to quell this threat.

Vile forces lurk within the halls of the Dreadnaught and the Hive sisters scheme to tear the Echo of Navigation from your grasp. Armed with Eris Morn's guidance, Sloane's leadership, and Drifter's resourcefulness you are tasked with dismantling this threat once and for all. Meet with your team and devise a way forward.

Oryx has called us to council in Eris's throne world. Apparently, he has information regarding Savathûn's plans that he intends to share with us. His information about Xivu Arath proved useful, we should hear him out.

The Echo of Navigation, Oryx, is silent for now, waiting for an opportunity to present itself. Our plans have worked, but the next step is unclear. Continue delving into the Dreadnaught and thinning the opposition.

Your mastery of Taken power, the Path of Resolve, the Path of Ambition, and your triumph over the Echo of Navigation reflect in the polished obsidian of the Shaping Slab. Conquest fits you, Lightbearer, do not forget the strength you have gained here.

You were called and confronted by the Witch Queen. She laments the loss of her brother in the form of the Echo of Navigation, and makes it known that you are undeniably foes from here on out.
Xivu Arath has been thwarted. Eris Morn's throne is safe, but Dread, Hive, and Taken still surge across the system.

This report is assembled from the collected journals and accounts of Lightbearer participants of the Great Hunt, in which the Ahamkara were purged from Sol.

Wishes: A verbally expressed desire expressed within audible range of any Ahamkara. This wish is granted through invocation of something known as the "Anthem Anatheme," which appears to be a manner of subjecting reality to one's will, similar to a Lightbearer's ability to affect paracausality. However, little is known about how this process unfolds in practice.

Henceforth, the "wisher" enters a binding contract with the Ahamkara, though many Ahamkara will purposefully manipulate or misinterpret the parameters of this contract to draw greater nourishment from it, often causing calamity to the wisher.
Lightbearers are expected to refrain from expressing wants or desires in the presence of an Ahamkara.

"This will work. I've spent a year of study, counting each day. Felt time's weight. But I've spent it well."

"The time nears, Guardian. Riven's part is done. Queen Mara felt Crow's passage end. He has arrived. I've woven the Veil into their connection, and soon it will lock its alignment."

"Beloved acolyte," Eris says as she greets you in her Hive form. "Champion of violence, bearing tithes raw and sweet as bitten sores."
"Something is coming."
"I don't think you realize how lost you'd be without Savathûn's plan," he says. "Even dead, she's smarter than you."

"She had it all figured out years ago," he explains. "Take the Traveler, seal it away, keep it hidden from the Witness…. But you stormed the gates. Liberated your darling Traveler, and put it exactly where the Witness knew you would."
"The Traveler didn't make a mistake when it chose the Hive," he snarls. "It was fixing the mistake it made when it chose you."
"Empower her, Guardian," Ikora says. "Give Eris the strength she needs to reshape the entire Hive pantheon."
"And then, all we need to do is get out of her way."

"I'm gonna give it to you straight, Sunbeam," Immaru says. "I've run the numbers, and your gal Eris doesn't have what it takes… she's nowhere near strong enough to deal with Xivu. You Guardians came up short."

"Savathûn can stay dead for all I care," he says, shrugging his shell in indifference. "Ah, don't look so surprised. Sure, your Ghost would never abandon you, but there's one important difference between him and me: he's an idiot."
"There's no way this ends in anything but a bloodbath," he says simply, "and I don't plan on getting caught in it."

"The Witness will force the Vanguard's hand eventually," Savathûn says in the recording, "and they'll realize they need information only I possess. One of them will be open to a bargain… not Mara again, poor dear. More likely Ikora, or her gloomy little hanger-on, Eris. Give them any help they ask for—it'll all be worth it in the end."
"My aim in this grotesque conversion was to shoulder the risk myself," she explains. "But feeding from Ahsa's suffering… that is a line I did not think I would cross."
"I refuse to become something I am not."
"It is good to see you," she says. "I was taking a moment to prepare for the ritual."
"It is justice."
"So I will step again into the ritual space," she continues, "and as the vile power fills me to bursting, my thoughts will be only of the Hive sisters. Savathûn. Xivu Arath. Of my plans for them."
"It is then I find that sweet moment. And deep beneath my hideous mask… I smile."
"While we in the Tower gathered intel and debated over what action to take next, Eris threw herself into a dangerous ritual of her own devising," she says. "She was audacious, and she was right."
"It is done," she says. "When I killed Savathûn, I claimed her eons of stored power. For a moment, I surpassed even Xivu Arath herself."
"Instead of challenging Xivu Arath, I severed her connection to her throne world. She is mortal now, wherever she may be."
"But I am weary of destruction," Eris says. "For now, I would like only… tea. Tea, and silence."
"I will not deny them their dogma," she says with a grin. "I will embody it."
"Savathûn said if you ever got this far, I should play back one of her predictions," he says, and you could swear his voice is soured by envy. "She's almost… rooting for you."
"That's when things really start to get weird," she says with a grin. "I can't wait to see what they're capable of."
"There you go, a little pat on the head from Savathûn," he spits. "I know you Vanguard types thrive on positive reinforcement."
"Xivu Arath, god of battlefield filth! Savathûn, god of the false and polluted! You have forgotten you were born as prey."
"I will remind you."
"Now is the time, my acolyte, my Guardian," she says. "This will be our final tithe. Let it be glorious."
"This wasn't part of the plan," he warns, "and it's bad news for everybody."

"Savathûn's been hoarding powerful creatures in those summoning pits for a long time," he says, his voice tinged with panic. "If Xivu is able to take that extra power for herself? Forget it, we're all dead."
"You need to claim those tithes for yourself," he says urgently. "Time to get to work, 'hero.'"
"Eris has always been determined," Ikora says. "Now she has incredible power to match. I trust her to guide us through this… but I fear she may not know when to stop—or even want to."
"The only thing we can offer her now is support," she says firmly. "That is why I need you at her side."
"We are caught between the sister gods of combat and lies," she says. "We accepted an impossible bargain. Savathûn knew we couldn't defeat Xivu Arath. No one can win a battle against war itself."
"Guardian… be careful. We've lost so much to the Hive already. We can't let them take any more."

Most Ghosts will say that their Guardian has lived two lives: the one before their first resurrection, and the one they're living now. Some Lightbearers go by the number of times they've fallen in battle, knowing that the count doesn't end unless their Ghost is ended first.
Exos like Cayde-6, have it the hardest—which might be why he likes to keep everything in one place, between the pages of a journal.

His mentor, Andal Brask, exists only in his memory and the strokes of a charcoal sketch that Sundance claimed "looks nothing like him." So Cayde drew her too, agonizing over the precise angles of her shell and the special way her Light refracted at dusk and dawn.
There's a poem about all his Vanguard paperwork, and a disclaimer beneath it that he is not—and never will be—a poet.
Entire pages dedicated to half-remembered dreams of the Golden Age, and a family that he fears is only wishful thinking.

Physical mementos, too, tucked between the pages or fastened to them. A ramen ticket. A feather from the Colonel. A playing card stolen from a deck that he and Shiro once shared. Wild sage grown in the mountains outside the Last City, where he and Sundance used to escape when the Tower started feeling like a tomb. When Cayde rubs the brittle leaves between his fingers, they crumble into a mealy dust. Its smell makes his heart ache.

Crow does not ask Cayde how many lifetimes he's lived, although he's curious what the answer would be. He also does not ask where the journal came from, or why it might be here in the Pale Heart with him.
It's a question that would inevitably lead to others—and neither of them are ready for that conversation. Even if they both know it must be coming.
So he gives it to you. To hold onto.

lines.text: "Bluejay, huh? That's a heck of a story." Nimbus grins. "Jain had serious problems with authority. Makes me look like an Academy drill instructor by comparison. Big brain, though, and an even bigger heart. Once he learned to actually listen to others, he went from public enemy to public hero. Eventually became a Cloud Strider."

"The Cloud Striders maintain the original sim space he built way back when. It's technically in the VexNet, so we use it like a listening post. Problem is, with everything going on, it's full of Vex. Locked with a quadrinomial encryption sequence too. Nasty stuff. You'd need a Polymorphic Engine to crack it. And a ton of their Shellcode samples."
Awesome! Now that you have the Vex encryption data, you'll need a Polymorphic Engine to brute force your way past their lockout.

"So the Vex aren't afraid of the Occlusion. They want it, and they're tunneling into the CloudArk to find it."
Bluejay's files are a mess! Why are creative types like this?! Anyway, I've finally sifted through and found a lead for us. Come see me.

lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: The nuclear force that scorches anyone foolish enough to draw near… is the same force we harness to heal.
lines.speaker: Osiris

lines.text: No serious scholar approaches fieldwork without preparing for… unwanted interruptions.
lines.speaker: Osiris

lines.text: The quality of a study is only as good as its samples.
lines.speaker: Osiris

lines.text: Bring back whatever data you can. You never know what might prove valuable.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: The nature of Nessus's conversion may be imprinted in every rock, in every blade of grass. It is only up to us to interpret it.
lines.speaker: Osiris

lines.text: My historical records contain references to gold being some sort of regional tea? Query: who would drink this?
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: Shooting things is fun! Commence fixing more problems with bullets!
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: Did you know the phrase 'finders keepers' originated before the Golden Age?
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: I am eager to process any findings from your venture. Even the unimpressive ones!
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: I cannot decide which word is more amusing to my audio processors: spelunking or swashbuckling.
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: Show them the Arc.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: The only exciting shenanigans around here are gonna be mine. Turns out, my gun agrees.
lines.speaker: Cayde-6

lines.text: Don't ask me why these colors are better.
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: Ikora says the radiolaria fluid is not the Vex. I say to spill it anyway.
lines.speaker: Saint-14

lines.text: I've killed enough Vex to end a war.
lines.speaker: Saint-14

lines.text: "I would like it on record that if I ever need repairs, I would prefer the spare parts come from a non-Cabal source!"—Failsafe
lines.speaker: Also Failsafe

lines.text: Unless I get one of their big guns.
lines.speaker: Also Failsafe

lines.text: We got a live one!
lines.speaker: Cayde-6

lines.text: It shoots bullets, Saint. It's a gun.
lines.speaker: Shaxx

lines.text: Long-range kills are neat, when you think about them! You're over here, someone drops dead over there…
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: Whatever the Darkness brings, we can face it together.
lines.speaker: Osiris

lines.text: Void is the pull of gravity and the promise of entropy. It teaches us that emptiness is not nothingness.
lines.speaker: Osiris

lines.text: The deeper we go into Nessus, the more wonders we find… and the more dangers we face.
lines.speaker: Saint-14

lines.text: Bad news. These Fallen consider us acceptable targets for murder. Hoo-ray.
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: Hey, don't worry! The cave roof might not collapse on top of you!
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: Sure, they're big and mean. You're meaner.
lines.speaker: The Drifter

lines.text: Shadows grow darker in the presence of Light.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: We need to go deeper. I guess.
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: I never looked up, not once. I cared more about my findings than the tea cooling beside me.
lines.speaker: Osiris

lines.text: The manner in which your shots echo through the caves is evocative of the hollowness of existence and the finality of true death. Anyway, please keep shooting.
lines.speaker: Failsafe

lines.text: I can't explain the details right now, Guardian, but on your next run against an enemy operation, I'll need you highly visible to electromagnetic sensors.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: Heh… yeah, turns out they only count as supply lines if the supplies are still there when you get back. Go pick yourself up a treat!
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Okay, bear with me: I noticed that bombarding major cosmological events with extreme temperatures can make this, uh… let's call it a wobble in the fabric of the Ascendant Plane. So I'm thinking, maybe I can use that like sonar to do some scouting! Ha ha… yeah, don't ask me how I figured this out.
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Here's a thought: Do the Hive rely on infrared vision? Oh, or the Scorn? I don't know. Yet. I don't know yet.  But I know how we can find out!
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Sure, you can shoot goons all day, but we should also be thinking infrastructure. Maybe the next time you're somewhere sensitive, think about throwing around some of those big special effects. Y'know, see what breaks?
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: So, word in the Hive Ghost network is that they're readying a quick response to security breaches. If you go in, you gotta be fast, yeah? Hit 'em hard, then get out!
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: I have been meticulously crafting this list here, just for you, of all the worst scum in the Throne World. You take some of these down, and the universe is a happier place for everyone.
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Every time a commander goes missing, I get this small window of time to use their security credentials before they're deactivated. Which is handy if you know who's about to go missing, yeah?
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Look, I ain't checked out these Altars of Reflection personally, but you don't build whole monuments just to fill out your urban plan, yeah?
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Don't believe your eyes, Guardian. They only show you what you want to see at the best of times… and these are far from the best of times.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: If you're gonna be causing trouble anyway, how about giving me a heads-up? Yeah, maybe I can take advantage of it with a little warning. A little team-up?
lines.speaker: Fynch

"I must admit, it was a little unnerving to watch someone else operate the Loom. I've put quite a lot of effort into creating this and… I'm feeling a bit protective."
"That being said, it clearly worked as intended. I've gathered data from your production job—with enough information, I may be able to amend this technology toward some other purpose in the future."
"To that end, let's start another production run."
"I don't think there's much else for me to review with you. Please keep utilizing the Loom so I can compile more data—who knows where it will lead. And thank you again, Guardian."
"What is it that old saying? The ball is in your court now?"
"I'm not really sure what that means—but good luck, friend."
"This is Synthweave, a programmable matter more sophisticated than I've ever seen, significantly more advanced than Glimmer."
"Do the honors of trying it out. It should be able to replicate the physical appearance of some of your armor, though not the material or energy properties."

"I've used the BrayTech schematics to create smaller devices called Threaders—with these, you can convert Glimmer into the Synthcord that the Loom needs. We should verify the Threaders are functioning before anything else…"
"As far as I can tell, the Loom is ready for production. Let me give it a test run and see what we get, and if it passes quality checks, I'll explain the process."

"A dragon's mindset. But it has its time and place. Well fought, Guardian."
"You play a game with an absent opponent. There might be power in even these small rituals, but nothing waits to feed upon it."
"Yet we play on. In her memory."
"I cannot say for certain. Nonetheless, her bounty is here for you to claim, should you desire it."
"Riven has set you upon a hunt. A powerful enemy awaits you in the heart of Rheasilvia. Track it down, and claim your next token."
"I know Crow would have liked to help, if he could. I sense him still—like a distant vessel on a turbulent sea. Moving further and further away from us."
"That is, if its use were not constrained by the mechanism that houses it. It's been calibrated for Guardians, after all. The risk is minimal."
"Guardian. I have your instructions. I suspect you'll have had your fill of Queensfoil before you're through."
"We live such long lives. Even the greatest wonders can become commonplace. Yet others are fleeting, there and gone—known to us only because we happened to be looking at the right moment."
"Keep your eyes open, Guardian."
"Walk with caution within the realms of the Nine. They are too… vast for simple allegiances."

"Only Riven could retain some portion of her will, when she was Taken. For all others, it is a cold, lonely death of the self. A foreign will burrows into the mind. Strangles thought; shapes volition."
"I won't forgive. But I will move forward."
"Take what you can from Riven's hoard, Guardian. Learn what lessons serve you best. Leave all the rest behind."
"Something you're both all too familiar with. Good luck, Guardian."
"I hope this inheritance is of use, even if only to please you. With all that lies ahead, sometimes the best gift we can ask for is a measure of peace."
See you out on the stage.

lines.text: You've confirmed Fynch's theory about the Osmic Fragment and a Lucent Brood plot, but you've got a long way to go before you can close this case.

According to Fynch, this fragment is evidence of a sinister Lucent Brood plot. It pulses mysteriously. Submit it to the Evidence Board to learn more.
Ghost has picked up a promising signal in Quagmire. Searching there should turn up a sample for analysis.
The Osmic Fragment gleams in the center of the board. Ghost's scan established that this is made of Fundamental Osmium, a super-dense transition metal found in the Throne World.
You consider all this as you cast your eyes over the other Hidden reports, looking for more connections.
So far, nothing else stands out. Report back later for further developments.
This is the Evidence Board, the main hub of intel for the Hidden's investigations into Mars and Savathûn's throne world.
You scan the few reports posted around the edges of the board. Clearly, Ikora's agents have been working hard, but they haven't had much luck finding concrete evidence.
But first, you should confirm just what this fragment is.
You've seen metallic ore similar to this in the Throne World. You should find a sample for comparison. Maybe there are others with the same paracausal resonance.
Fynch checks the surroundings, his squirrelly affect shifting into a quieter, tenser mode. He whispers that he has proof of the Lucent Brood's shady schemes.
He transmats a strange, gleaming fragment in the air before you. As it drops into your open hands, it sends a slight but distinctly paracausal pulse through your palms.

Fynch explains that he swiped it from the apothecary wing in Savathûn's fortress. He isn't exactly sure what it is, but he's convinced that it's meant to play an important part in some twisted ritual.

"So I need you to restore Stargazer's records." Quinn's avatar radiates cheer. "All you need to do is sort of 'vibe' with Stargazer… the city's most famous explorer."

"The short version is, you must have tapped into some kind of connection with Siegebreaker. Emotional, experiential… something strong, whatever it was. So my theory is, to do the same thing with Stargazer, the best place to start is emulating them somehow, looking for that same connection. I could expound on the psychological and philosophical theories if you want. There's a lot of interesting research into the nature of consciousness, especially given the CloudArk… Maybe the city's belief in the Cloud Striders helped you anchor the memorial? Or maybe you're just that good at magic archaeology."

"Well, this is a mess," Quinn says, indicating the broken memorials behind her. "But at least you kept the Veil safely in Neomuna! You know, it keeps the CloudArk running; we'd be lost without it. And on top of that, we haven't even scratched the surface on what it has to say about Darkness."

"Most immediately urgent is the broken memorials. The battle with Calus brought CloudArk security briefly offline, and some anomalous signal patterns were broadcast unsecured, coinciding almost perfectly in timing with the activation of the Veil. The Vex broke in immediately afterward, and destroyed five specific Cloud Strider memorials before retreating. Clearly a precision strike, but the question is, why?"

"Go take a look around the Hall first, all right? Get a good picture of how this place is in the parts that aren't on fire, learn a little about Neomuna that doesn't involve sabotage or explosions. Then you can circle back to the memorials, do some scans, and hopefully blow my socks off with what you and Ghost can pick up."

Quinn is overjoyed to have one monument back, and that scientific mind is hard at work on the best ways to get you to reconstruct the rest. Between your Strand capabilities and her historical knowledge, she's pretty clearly hoping you'll be able to restore all of the lost records. There's a whole city invested in the history of their heroes, after all. And ideally in the process, you can solve the mystery of the Vex attack.

That was uncalled for! I'm refocusing on identifying the source of this change.
No, I'm analyzing the oscillating nature of the Modular Mind's shield to find weaknesses that can be applied to anti-Cabal weaponry. Why am I doing that?
"My knife returns to me, bloodied with vengeance. In this way, you honor my court and bolster our strength. Well fought, Guardian."

I define it as combining existing information to form new meaning.
Thinking is the ability to create. To work beyond the boundaries of what you already know. To envision something completely new and unexpected.
About an hour ago, I noticed my screensaver had been replaced. It now shows a breathtaking painting of a sunset over the Ejriksson crater on Mars. A gift from Rasputin.
I guess I saw this coming, but it was still a blow.
I arrived in the lab this afternoon to discover that Rasputin has discarded my communications protocols. He's replaced them with a system-wide program that he himself designed.
His voice is unlike anything that has ever existed. It is both haunting and lovely. It is also terrifyingly efficient.

He's also begun upgrading warsats with new capabilities of his own invention, and I'm not entirely sure what those abilities are. It's exactly the goal we were striving towards, this level of autonomous control, and I know I should be celebrating.
My work here is done. But it occurs to me that there's one existential concept I never taught Rasputin: trust.
And even if he trusts us… are we 100 per cent certain we can trust him?
Rasputin's designers made a mistake that exasperates me. They brought in linguists and neurobiologists, then tried to convert their expertise into rules for Rasputin to follow.
Way to faceplant, people. No set of concrete data can ever wrangle a human language. It's not math. Language is mutable, adaptable. For every rule obeyed, there's a rule broken.
Babies don't learn their native tongue through rules. They learn it through exposure, absorption. And until I roll up my sleeves and get to work, Rasputin is mankind's most expensive baby.

So far, so good… if you set your goals realistically. Forget Rasputin for a moment; that's something I'm just not good at. If you look at me with the tiniest shred of approval, I'll kill myself to please you.

I have some issues. So I am going to make Rasputin a breakthrough construct. I fed him—should be "it," but I don't care—I fed him digitized copies of every major work of literature as a foundation for language use.
Military history, he's been fed by the truckload. But then I started in with operas and symphonies. I don't want him just to think about things.

Humans don't communicate strictly through data. We also communicate through art, through expression. If Rasputin is to be the most effective communications device in the Sol system, I want him to feel things.
The best ideas start as jokes. Ask any psychologist. Jokes and ideas both rely on the unexpected.  The brilliance of both can be measured by the intensity of the reaction they provoke.
With that in mind, I've fed Rasputin comedies from Shakespeare right up to the present day. This morning, I asked him to tell me a joke.
Obviously, that's something artificial intelligence isn't set up to tackle, but we need Rasputin to be able to make that leap.

Here's a hypothetical: say Rasputin has to redirect a malfunctioning warsat, and there are only two paths for it to take. One will breach the hull of a one-seat planetjumper, instantly killing its pilot. The other path will disable a Venusian pleasure craft, leaving its inhabitants alive but certain to die of starvation before they can be found.
To my surprise, when given this problem, Rasputin actually rendered a verdict.
I'm not going to tell you what it is, because I want you to enjoy your next Venusian pleasure craft trip.
Rasputin continues to develop by leaps and bounds.

In a trial simulation, he successfully interpreted the meaning of corrupted, borderline incomprehensible data from a damaged warsat.  This is exactly the sort of function we need him to fill. But that wasn't the amazing part.
The mind-blower was that without proof, evidence, or conscious reasoning, Rasputin sensed which warsat was in trouble.
You heard me. Rasputin has developed intuition. I wish he could celebrate with me.
You can lead a machine to language, but you can't make it think. Well, you can't. But I can. My name is Ana Bray. If you want to insult me, call me a neurolinguist.
Not that it isn't a fine and noble profession, but neurolinguistics is about encoding language. I'm a psycholinguist. I study how language can lead to independent thought.
The computer we call Rasputin is the nexus of Sol system's defense network. It can process data at superluminal speed. It can uplink to the thousands of warsats that keep humanity safe.
But we need more from it. We need it to think for itself. And that's where I come in.
If Rasputin is to properly command our entire defense network, it has to learn a wide array of skills as it performs. Any wrench-banger can build a machine designed to solve specific problems.

But why conquer a task if there's no insight to be had from the victory? Rasputin has to solve problems currently solvable only by humans. It has to form concepts and to self-improve without supervision.

To keep us safe, it'll have to make decisions based on random intel we can't possibly anticipate. The lives and safety of every sentient being in the system depend on me teaching it how to do this. So, you know, no pressure.

We treated the ship like its name, like one of the Guardians of old. But I swear to you that Sparrows have personalities, even spirits. I know that sounds crazy, but I believe that. AA's name was cold, and the Sparrow was cold. You couldn't warm it up. But boy it could fly.
S: I'm looking for material on Io. Something different.

MC: Oh! I'll tell you something about Io. No, really. You won't find this anywhere. I remember once my partner and I were lost for a week straight in a canyon on Io—we weren't eying one another like turkey legs or anything, but it was close. We were running out of rations. Then we saw Vespulaser come in and disappear over the canyon walls. We knew it by those stripes, they make it look like some kind of dangerous insect. We knew it would be hours of climbing, but we hurried toward it immediately. Look it up.
Primarily used on the ice caps of Mars during the Golden Age.

I'd forgotten what this place looks like. It feels like only yesterday I had a badge and a desk. Not a lot survived, but somehow this old thing is still around. If you've come this far, we have a lot in common. You feel that same drive to see something through to the end, don't you?

I've never been the sentimental type, but at this point I'm a stranger to my own nature. It just feels right that I'm back, for now. By the time you read this, we'll have just missed each other. I've run the simulations, and I can't stay. Not yet.
Take care of her for me.

lines.text: Here are the locations, but there's some interference. I'm pretty sure those are Taken protections—curses, things with teeth. Be ready. And one other thing, Guardian—remember you're not the only one who knows about these. You took some from the Hive already. I wouldn't be surprised if you meet more resistance.
lines.speaker: Deputy-Commander Sloane

lines.text: "One day, we'll be shot of this mess," Sloane says tiredly. "Guardian. I have an additional scavenger hunt for you. More signals like those fragments you found in the first place have been popping up—all over the Dreadnaught. Maybe it's an excess of caution, but I don't like leaving them out there for anyone to pick up and use."

"Unfortunately," she continues, "we couldn't get specific locations. Just that they're here, and if me and my sensors can read them? Taken sure can. Probably Hive, too. So, get out there, find them, and…" Sloane shrugs apologetically. "Well, I think you can probably siphon their energy into your new weapon, but it's going to require some better control of Taken energies. Let's work at it a bit at a time. Soon enough you'll be a master."

"Hmm." Sloane hums with thought as she examines the Osseous Spine you've brought her. Briefly she closes her eyes. "It's definitely another piece for your weapon. It's a little warped… it wants to change."

"More complicated," Sloane amends. "The ones you found earlier were hidden by Hive rituals. These three — the trail goes cold hard, like it's cut off. Three different spots, same Taken energy signature overrides the one we're looking for. Probably some sort of protection…" She thinks about it. Síocháin whirs behind her shoulder, similarly thinking. "A curse, maybe," Sloane says. "Wards and curses are pretty much the same thing, to the Taken."

Good progress. I'm refining our search parameters using the multiple fragments you've acquired to help triangulate, and I have a few new candidates for you to track down. It's going to be trickier than before—hope you're up for it.
lines.speaker: Deputy-Commander Sloane

lines.text: "Strong readings of Taken energy, not surprising," she says. "Here's the interesting part. This—" She taps the fragment. "—has not one, but two specific energy signatures. Síocháin says it's in some sort of quantum-dyadic state. Two things at once, somehow. Apparently 'one thing hidden beneath the other' is a little too simplistic for how they're interlaced, but it's close enough."

"One last set of signals to track down, Guardian, and then that ought to be the last of it." Sloane sends you some data. "These were hiding. That makes them sound like they have a will of their own, doesn't it?"
"This piece is fast," she pronounces after a moment or two. "It wants to be an endless onslaught…"
"That's another piece of it, for sure," she says after a moment's concentration. "This piece is… blunt. It wants to crush."
Sorrow's Harbor is where I'd start. There's been some strange Hive activity there. See if they're hiding another fragment like yours.

"Hey, hero. You regret saving the world yet? They're gonna keep you busy till the end of time!"

"You ruminate on that little pearl of wisdom while you run around saving lives and all. Me, I've got contacts shouting down the comms—figure I can point you where you'll make a real difference to people that need it."
"And… I've got a favor to ask you. You know Moondust—Eris, I mean—has a habit of letting the hours fly by. You and I both know you can't accomplish much on an empty stomach."
"Besides, she's always on me about my ingredients. Just 'cause I can make do with alternatives in a pinch doesn't mean I don't know my spices!"
"Anyway, seeing as you're headed out there, will you drop off this meal I packed for her? It'll be worth your time. Trust."
"Drifter sent you here with… lunch?"

"The Drifter and I have been—cautiously—discussing the past. That is, we have been reflecting upon my tendency to cling to material remnants of years gone by… and the Drifter's reluctance to divest himself of his old reputation."
"…I would not wish for you to leave empty-handed. Please: take something. Consider it a fair exchange."
"Drifter has great admiration for you. He may obscure it all he likes with jokes and affected bewilderment… it remains plain to see. You are a part of this City in a way some part of him longs for."
"I, at least, am content to communicate that directly."

"Get your favorite Cannon ready—I have more work for you. Figure if they're going to put me in charge of this kind of thing, I might as well lean into it. Run you ragged. Really make you regret being so helpful."
"Got another delivery for Eris, while you're here. Tell her I said… well, never mind. Just let me know what she thinks about it, yeah?"
"…Perhaps someday, we might all share a meal together. If we can ever find the time."
"Until then, Guardian, please feel free to claim a gift."
"Been thinking… Yeah, yeah, no jokes."

"Thinking about old times. New times. Fact is, if we really aren't going to high-tail it out of here—and it does seem a bit late for that—I guess we might as well start to think of this place like home."
"…Bunch of other idiots here, too, of course. Anyways, look here: I made a dessert this time. Don't sneak a bite—I'll cook up something for you when you're not on the clock."
"You'd think the Sol system was getting sliced up all over again, the way people are hollering for help. Been hard to keep up."
"I'm practically doing the Vanguard's job for them! You'd think I like this place or something."
"Don't you look at me. Just go take care of business. And here: I made this dish special. Had to call in a favor to get the right ingredients. Don't spill it."
"Guardian, I wish to express my gratitude. Not only for the food, which has been… unexpectedly appetizing."

"I have enjoyed these regular visits. They invite recollection without sorrow. As much as I have lost, today I find myself in the company of those who will extend to me their kindness and their trust, and that is a great gift."

"We are not the same people we were even a few years ago. To risk connection is to be changed. And we have changed too much already to fear what the future may bring. I only count myself fortunate that, when I walk forward to meet it, I will not do so alone."
"…And please, tell Germaine that he is not fooling anyone. He wouldn't leave now that he's just begun showing off his culinary skills."
"I imagine he only sought to spite us all, in those early days. Prove us wrong. Fortunate, then, that neither you nor I are very good at backing down from an argument."
"Do you recall our entreaties to the Nine? Our communion with the entity we believed to be the Darkness itself? Those first, hesitant steps?"
"Drifter is right, I think. We make an effective fireteam."
"You've been carving your way through this list, kid. I'm proud of ya. Don't say that enough."
"…Then she'd run off into the thick of things again. Me, I'm great at relaxing." Drifter lobs the datapad over his shoulder. "Just follow my example."
"Not sure what'll turn up tomorrow. But… pretty sure I can count on you when it happens."
"I see that this will not be a… one-time occurrence."
"I have been reflecting upon power, of late. How it accumulates. How it can be bent to purpose. And… what becomes of it, when that purpose is fulfilled."

"A line of thought that flowed, inevitably, to you. To the role you have played in each of our lives. Your triumphs have altered the fates of entire stars. Today, I see the good you do for the City, and that, too, seems a sweet and indulgent vengeance."
"My gratitude, Guardian, for this gift. Perhaps something in my collection will suit you in kind."
"Hey, kid. Decent work out there so far. I've been kicking some ideas around. Got a new assignment for you, if you're up for it."
"Oh, and here: run this down to Eris for me?"

"We lost so much with the arrival of the Black Fleet. It seemed senseless to mourn my little garden on Io, at the time. But sometimes I think on how frightened we all were, in the face of a second Collapse… and what it meant to me, to plant a garden at the end of the world."
"The garden is gone. But the hope remains."
"Sometimes I think of the old Tower. I never saw it, but…"
"Anyway! City needs your help. I'm here to entice you with the goods. But only when you're done."
"Hey, partner. Hold up a minute."
"So I gutted that vending machine out front a while back… used it to stash some goodies I picked up after the Red War."
"Besides, there's something in there I think you'll like."
"I take it all back—I'm going to Neomuna. Gonna upload myself into that CloudArk of theirs, maybe become some kind of computer virus."

The Cabal I knew would have held your City, kept your Tower. “Through divine right,” I would have said, before my exile to the black edge. I’ve since learned there is no such thing, that there is only the end. What then, was the difference? Cultivation.

Your people have not triumphed over the Cabal because of the Light. We’ve fought the Light before you, and though it has assured you victory thus far, there are ways to defeat it without taking it. The Red Legion have simply forgotten how.

You and your Guardian-tribe are more disciplined, enlightened. You are the greatest fighting force this system has ever seen, and yet, despite your brutish predilections, you are… cultured, elite. With few exceptions, what you take you hold. And you thrive. True, the Red Legion managed to conquer your City. But in the end, you took everything from them, and you stand firmer than ever before.
A Shadow of your Guardian-tribe would be the ideal taskmaster to train the armies of the empire. To batter them to dust before making them anew, in your broad-shouldered image.
You’ve shown the Red Legion you fly my banner. I know that when the time is right, I won’t have to ask. You’re on my side.

I see it when your body becomes a weapon with which you obliterate your opponents, when your knuckles become a part of your foe’s countenance, when you smash them with your Light. And it is captivating. But Earth casts no Shadow. Not yet.
When you’re ready, you will be magnificent. A Guardian of Guardians. Shadow of Shadows.
I reserve the right to be last when the end comes, and for that, I will need you with me.

The Cabal I knew understood mental fortitude. I don’t speak of the psychokinetic abilities of the Psions, but the sheer force of will mustered by the foot soldiers who served me. Even my Loyalists have grown soft over the ages. We have fallen so far from enlightenment.
But when I look to your Guardian-tribe, I see glimmers of the Cabal I knew. Rushing headlong into battle, your bodies themselves weapons. Your kind dies over nothing. I’ve seen it.

Your deaths lack permanence, but does that make it any easier? As you’re shredded alive by a warbeast, or scattered to the winds by psionic projection? Even the best of you are regularly sewn together by your Ghosts. And you persist with the same fervor every time.
A Shadow of your Guardian-tribe would be the ideal teacher to bring this selfless state of mind back to the empire. I will ensure that my Loyalists are… willing learners.

The Cabal I remember were fierce hand-to-hand combatants. We learned and shared techniques from countless indoctrinated races. No longer. Red Legion training is like Red Legion weaponry—all bluster and noise. Ghaul was… acceptable. But Ghaul was special.
How we once delighted in throwing our bones into the soft tissues of our enemies. We devised ingenious ways to dance and weave to better throw them.  Just like you.

Your Guardian-tribe holds the delivery of personal combat in great esteem. It’s an art to you. I can tell in how you treasure each strike. You savor them. The sensation of your bones breaking bones, smashing vital organs.
The false empire will never have the Light. Not again. But a Shadow of your Guardian-tribe would be ideal to guide them, to teach them to move themselves once again. And throw their bones.

The Cabal I knew were natural leaders, with the ability to drive cultivation. That they excelled at war was the result of their gentility. Our debate chambers were glorified as much as our battlefields.

And look at us now. Who is this Valus that leads the Red Legion astray? His name already escapes me. Were if not for him, I would gladly accept them back into my fold. Perhaps I can redeem the Red Legion.
Before the Red War, the Cabal at least had their dear Dominus Ghaul.
More than ever, my empire needs me. And I need you.
A Shadow of your Guardian-tribe would serve to remind the Cabal of what they once were. Proud. Unbroken. Vicious in war. Civilized in peace. And all it would take is what you’re already doing.
Continue to advance. Drive them before you. Force them to change, or die.

lines.text: If the Vex get a foothold in Maya's Retreat, they'll be impossible to get out again, and the next step is the CloudArk. We can't let them get anywhere near the Occlusion—you have to stop them!
lines.speaker: Quinn

lines.text: The Vex are coming for the Occlusion! The Shadow Legion know where they are. Does everyone know more about this than me?! Time to fix that!
lines.speaker: Quinn

lines.text: "I guess it isn't too outrageous to think a Strider would protect anyone in need. Even a Vex. If the Occlusion wanted to hurt us, it could have. Instead, it just seems to like its independence and some quiet. And I know I like my naps, so I'm feeling a little connection, you know?"
"It must have hauled some information out of the Vex databases. Or… our databases? Both? Ugh. I'm going to be forever figuring out the rest. Still, hope that's helpful to what you've got going on."

"This… I must have made a mistake." Quinn's crisis of faith is obvious in her voice. "The Cabal data says the Vex are searching for a Vex Mind inside our network? But that would mean the Strider helped hide it and keep it secret, even from the Council! From me! Not that I was even born yet, but it still feels… personal. We're not supposed to be a city of secrets."
This Shadow Legion tracking data is all over the place, but I've got a more sophisticated system back here at my desk. Bring it back to me, yeah?
lines.speaker: Quinn

lines.text: "I guess it isn't too outrageous to think a Strider would protect anyone in need. Even a Vex. If the Occlusion wanted to hurt the Neomuni, it's had every opportunity for centuries. Instead, it just seems to like its independence and some quiet. And I know I like my naps, so I'm feeling a little connection, you know?"

"I won't forget everything you've done for me. And for the city. We owe you a lot, friendly space zombie. You're welcome here anytime. Oh, and here! Nimbus said you like weapons, so I dug this out of the archive for you. Don't worry—it's not fragile."

"A Vex mind! A VEX MIND?! It's completely cut off from the VexNet, and I don't even know how that works! And the Strider was helping it stay hidden? So much network architecture is built around it that pulling it out would be like pulling the bowl out from under your ramen. If the Vex access this, bring it into their hive mind… that would be bad."

The Vex. The Occlusion. Cloud Strider memorials. Time to figure out what brings them all together.
A Strider pushes forward toward their goal no matter what may block their path. You can feel this Cloud Strider's legacy within the cosmic web.
Neomuna's network is safe from the Vex tunneling attack. Now the city has some breathing room to decide what to do about their AI refugee.

Quinn wrestles this new discovery, but one thing is clear for now: You need to find and stop this Vex operation before they can re-establish contact with the Occlusion and bring it back into the hive mind. It would devastate the city, and the Occlusion itself seems to prefer freedom. Now that you understand what the Vex are doing—probing the CloudArk to extract one of their own—it makes their needs clear and limits the number of places in the city they could be hiding. That, combined with the Shadow Legion's tracking data suggests a large Vex operation is underway in the Thrilladrome.

The Shadow Legion have uncovered a Vex tunneling operation, but the comms chatter Quinn has been able to pick up hasn't been very specific apart from that. The Shadow Legion have been ordered away from the operation, but that still leaves many places in Neomuna where the Vex could be working, and the Shadow Legion might yet be in active retreat.

Sweep through the areas where Vex and Shadow Legion are fighting to rule out those areas, and collect encrypted data from them to analyze and further narrow down where the Vex operation could be. With any luck, the chase will help you bond with the Strider's legacy—but the defense of the city is the most vital goal.

"Happy Solstice, Guardian!"
"It brings me such happiness to see life thriving in the Tower. If we focus only on what we've lost, we can easily lose sight of the hope and beauty that surrounds us."
"Have you heard the legend of the phoenix? A mythical bird from pre-Golden Age folktales, it was said that it would burn within its own flames and rise anew from the ashes."
"That is the spirit of Solstice. Not one of sorrow, but of joy at the chance for renewal."
"May this gift remind you that, just like the phoenix, a bright future rises from the ashes of the past. Now go out there and celebrate all that life has to offer!"
Eva beams as you approach, gesturing to the verdant splendor that now decorates the Courtyard.
She folds her hands in front of her and gives you a kind smile.
Reaching for the table next to her, Eva picks up a neatly wrapped package and hands it to you.
"In Darkness I find comfort. I find peace."
"I have no memories of my childhood…was I once scared of the dark? What would my younger self say if they could see me now, greeting Darkness as an old friend."
"Let Light wash over me, let it grasp my hands and wrap me in its might, strengthen me in its resilience and lead me to victory."
"If I am to wield Darkness, let it be atonement for all the harm I have done with the Light. Let it be my redemption."
"I am awake but at what cost? In one moment, I am given the gift of life eternal and in that same moment burdened by the crushing weight of trying to make it all mean something…"
