The first day I called the storm was an end. The end of a journey, the summit of a mountain; but when you leave the mountain, you don't take it with you. How would I maintain the profound insight from the eye of the storm that unlocked my direct line to the hurricane?
Tempestuous peace. The calm and the storm. Where do I begin?
Questions rained upon me as I tried to put my thoughts into practice. The acrid stench of radiolaria reminded me that training was over. Was I ready for this? Did I have a choice?
Beaten, bloodied, I stared into the empty faces of my enemies. They were fearsome; they had taken much from me. But I've seen that which lies still amid cacophony.
Courage. The courage to face the torrent, to proclaim peace in the face of violence. Courage is the only call that the storm will hear.
Thunder rumbles and lightning strikes. Wind blows and rain pours. My enemies are no more. But peace… peace never left me.

I watch them frolic blithely beneath their oblivious god.
I am among those assembled to witness their training. They wish to become stronger than the Cabal. Than Xivu Arath. Than the Hive.
Their ignorance of their true enemy is overwhelming—they cannot even put a name to it. I am choked with rancid ambrosia.
Two men now remain in the artificial battleground. Their movements are simplistic: one charges blindly ahead. The other rolls to the side, fires a shotgun, and his opponent falls.

The victor turns to the crowd and removes his helmet. Oily fluids bead on the flesh of his face. He bears teeth that squirm with microbial life. He throws his arms upward in jubilation and the masses cheer.
I do not join them—this form affords me some dignities.
Behind the creature reveling in minor triumph, sacrilege: A perfect being materializes. It gathers meat and offal from the ground and reassembles it. An unfathomable gift is given.
The crowd has seen this miracle countless times. It has lost all meaning to them. They see it as a resource.
I look up into the blank white face. I feel its Light on my cheeks. It no longer burns me.

"You are marvelous," he said to the Arkborn. His eyes drank in the flickering light, reflecting nothing. "You will cast a glorious Shadow."

Statesman Tha'uul ran, and the Fulminator followed him. He was a minor diplomat who had played a part in the coup against the emperor. She wasn't certain of the details. The social dynamics of organics were difficult to grasp and she found them consistently irrelevant.
He had no idea she was still there. He thought he had outrun her, but the Arkborn knew that bipeds rarely look up.
She hovered far above her target, specific limiters on her armor disabled so that Arc could flow freely and lift her to the heavens.
Below, the statesman had chosen a brightly lit street that led to a dead end on the left turn in front of him. She descended.

Jarus's fighter soared like a blade into the throat of the Dominus's command ship. They hoped it wouldn't matter. Jarus died on impact. The Shadows burst forth from his shattered vessel, the Fulminator leading the charge.

Every limiter on her armor was undone. The unrelenting fury of her being loosed onto the bridge would permanently disable her. She would still exist, but couldn't anchor herself or manipulate anything around her. She would scatter to the winds.

Navigation displays exploded in a shower of sparks as she passed. The storm she had become reached an apex of intensity, and she reached out to scores of Cabal and swallowed them and she felt them die. She wrapped Ghaul in her light, enervated him in bursts of flaring Arc. She was fading. He would die. Wouldn't he?

I think it is only fair to warn you—I mean to reincorporate the Red Legion. I am their rightful emperor, and I shall offer them forgiveness. All they must do is repent and submit to their reeducation.
I feel like it's only fair to make you the same offer. How does "Primus of the Red Legion" sound?

Your reassimiliation into the empires is likely to be cause for concern. You'll understand that it will come with some preconditions. After all, we can't have it appear that I've played favorites. But there's no cause for alarm; your reeducation is merely a formality.

While I may forgive you, the rest of the empire will need some time. It's important to show the people how you have changed. It won't be forever, just however long it takes to earn your place at my side once more.
Are you just a phantom in a mirror?

The charred husk that was Statesman Tha'uul had revealed several things before he expired. He had mistaken her for a "warrior of the Light," one of their "storm bringers" who apparently bore a resemblance to the Fulminator. She wished to see one of them. No biped was ever anything like her. She felt something like regret when Tha'uul said his people were mobilizing to annihilate them.

She made other reports to Calus, pertaining to the locations of Red Legion armories and fleet movements. He only cared about one. Now that the military was in power, in Calus's absence, military parades on Cabal worlds were commonplace. Ghaul's flagship would take part in one such celebration, on Resignation Day, in the fringes of the Sol system, in honor of a mythic Praetor.
That was where the Shadows would kill the Dominus.
The Fulminator noticed a difference in her fellow Shadows as they prepared for war.
The usual bickering, fostered by the multispecies makeup of Calus's enforcer group, vanished overnight as they faced the task they had gathered to complete: kill Dominus Ghaul.

Calus had recruited them through bribery or promises of wealth and resources for their homeworlds. None of them expected to survive their mission. The might of the Red Legion had grown vast. This acceptance brought them together.

The Fulminator didn't understand, or care. As long as Calus left the Arkborn to their interstellar conduits, she would do what she had done since the day she came aboard the Leviathan: destroy the enemies of the emperor.

I think perhaps I am finally ready to forgive you. There's no point in carrying around this hate forever. I think about who you were, and who I was, and the end seems inevitable. How can I blame you for the poisonous ambition that the Consul poured into your ear? You were merely his instrument.
In the end, it has all been for the better, has it not? Your betrayal is the first chapter in the story of my ascension.
Sometimes I stare into the abyss of space, plagued by a terrible fear. In this waking nightmare, everything you said to me and everything you felt for me was a lie.

But what was the nature of these lies? Were they manipulations wrought by ambition? Were they hateful machinations of vengeance? Or, worst of all, were they self-delusions? Did I merely ascribe to you words and feelings that were, in fact, my own?
Calus gestured towards the crackling Arc storm before him. The energy mass shivered, tethered to a golden spindle in the center of the chamber.
A panel on the wall lit up in Cabal: THIS SHIP IS TINY.

Ghaul once served at my right hand. His even temper and disciplined mind proved a useful foil to my passion and force of will. And so, I leaned on him for all of my important decisions. It always felt good to talk through my ideas. He had a way of reflecting them back to me sharper and clearer.
I see the same wisdom in you, my dear Warlock. Perhaps—when the time is right—we might discuss my ideas.

As a Vex simulation plunged the Last City into darkness, the Vanguard turned to the Eliksni Splicer, Mithrax, for aid. In return, Ikora offered to shelter House Light within the City's walls—a controversial decision. With Mithrax's help, the Guardians learned to delve deep into the Vex network. There, they discovered the true mastermind behind the Endless Night: Quria, Blade Transform.

After defeating Quria as well as a treasonous Vex invasion of the Last City led by faction leader Lakshmi-2, the Guardians successfully lifted the Endless Night. Mithrax and House Light remain in the Eliksni Quarter as allies of the Vanguard.
Go beyond the Light and wield the Darkness.

After Saint-14, Crow, and the Guardian raced to the Dreaming City to confront Osiris, Savathûn revealed the truth: for months, she had assumed Osiris's identity, sowing distrust and chaos within the Vanguard and beyond. After a confrontation, the Witch Queen restored Crow's memories of his days as Uldren Sov. Now faced with his past, Crow retreated into solitude.

Queen Mara Sov struck a bargain where, in exchange for being freed from her worm, Savathûn would reveal the secrets of the Darkness. Intent on lifting the curse from the Dreaming City, Mara planned to kill her nemesis, but just as the separation ceremony completed, Savathûn escaped, her whereabouts unknown.

Humanity's ancient foe has returned. As the Black Fleet fills the sky, a strange power pulls friend and foe alike to the ruins of Europa, and a new Kell wields the gift of Darkness to unite the Fallen.
Work with the Exo Stranger to stop Eramis, Kell of Darkness, in a new story campaign. Master Stasis subclasses and unlock the secrets of the Deep Stone Crypt raid.
Caiatl, Empress of the Cabal, led her fleet to the Sol system and offered a deal to Zavala: swear fealty, and defeat the Hive together. The commander refused.

The Guardians undermined Caiatl's attempts to form a war council, defeating her champions in ritual combat. Cabal renegades attempted to kill Zavala, but Crow foiled the plot, revealing his identity in the process. Zavala and Caiatl agreed on a truce.
As planets vanished, Xivu Arath, the Hive god of war, moved to seize power. Osiris walked a dangerous path to learn of this plot; his Ghost, Sagira, paid the ultimate price.

The Guardian met an unexpected ally—Uldren Sov, murderer of Cayde-6, reborn as Crow; a Guardian in the Spider's employ. The Guardian foiled Xivu's plans and bargained with the Spider to buy Crow's freedom.

Desperate. My lovely Baron of Shanks was the most desperate Shadow I ever recruited. He questioned every order I gave, to the point that Valus Nohr required my personal appeasement to prevent the severing of his head.

Every second Humankind was left alive in this system he saw as an affront he demanded I rectify. Had I known how delightful encountering Guardians would be, I would have abided immediately. But those were the days before my dear Dominus had embraced the Light. At that time, what was Humanity to me?

Sekris was so like you. Barring the Light, of course. The absence of the Traveler in his people's lives has marked them like a scar, and they cannot forget it. His people—they envy you a great deal. When I think of him, and the hate he had for your homeworld and the benefits the Traveler bestowed upon it, I am reminded of the passion you have for its defense.
Be like Sekris. Don't share his weakness, his questioning of my authority and right of way. But consider taking up his mantle.
Give the Fallen something else to be jealous of.
Seek me out and grow fat from strength.
I promised Sekris a greater power than the favor of your Traveler. He died at Ghaul's hands still wondering what that could possibly be.

In later days, my disguise could no longer fool him as it fooled others. His skill in designing and modifying mechanized life-forms was unparalleled and he made it clear he knew I was not what I appeared to be. I made it clear that, either way, he would continue to serve. But I think he guessed that my form and my strength are inextricably linked.
Sekris's skill with cybernetics and Servitor mechanics allowed him a far greater lifespan than most of his kind. One of the reasons I picked him to Shadow me, and his peers were left to languish.

The Baron of Shanks could even recall a time when the Traveler had blessed his people. He rarely spoke of it, even to me, and I didn't press him. When one knows what Calus knows, Traveler-lore is meaningless. But I mention it only to say that he despised your kind with a particular ferocity that most of his people could not muster.

Sekris, the Baron of Shanks, wore this last. He was the most venerated warrior-priest of his era; Taniks, the Scarred and a whole generation of mercenaries to come patterned their brutality after his early, worlds-burning deeds. But I reached out, and he disappeared from history when he ventured into the deep black, following an offer he could not ignore.
"Vex structures on Venus and Mercury predate the Golden Age, and possibly Humanity itself." —Sister Faora, "Theories on the Vex"
"Multiple analyses confirm: the milky radiolarian fluid found in Vex chassis is organic in nature." —Sister Faora, "Theories on the Vex"

The Bladedancers deride us as slow. The Gunslingers say we lack precision. "How is that better than a knife?" "How is that better than a flaming pistol?" Well.
My boots sink inches into the ground with every step. My rebreather filters the stench out of the air, but my eyes sting like I'm showering with battery acid.

This vile marsh opens to reveal a black cave's maw. Inside, an infinite number of little green eyes flicker like bad stars. CRACK! I fire a single bullet into the air and the horde in the cave shrieks and runs out.
Now there are Orbs of Power everywhere. Eat, my friends. Eat.
No one remembers who the first Arcstrider was. Hardly anyone remembers the Arcstrider at all. Time vanished us like it does memories.

But in the darkest days of the Dark Ages, when humanity was utterly defenseless, Arcstriders disciplined their bodies to let the Traveler’s energy flow through them, to call lightning itself to hand and wield it like a staff against the Darkness.

The Kell is screaming three inches from my face and its breath smells like two corpses in summer and I have to blink my eyes against the spit. One of the less obvious perks of being able to pull a flaming gun out of the air is enjoying moments like this—alien fist around my neck, feet kicking in the air, not two seconds from death—but ready to laugh at the expression on that Kell's four-eyed face as its mandibles click for the last time and its body turns into fire.

The giant creature pulls back its other fist and its steel muscles bunch. I reach for the Light and get… nothing? Huh. Right. I used my flaming gun on those three Taken outside the obelisk. Gotta learn to count.

lines.text: Amanda Holliday's voice crackles over the comms. Reed-7 glances at his Ghost, then pulls up alongside Holliday's Hawk and gives her a nod. He falls in behind her, with Shayura and Aisha following behind him in tight formation.

Ahead, the beam of light extending from the Traveler is brighter than the sun. Instrumentation goes wild in its presence; astrogation systems don't know what to make of it and register the beam as a star. His ship tries to steer him away. Reed flips off autopilot.

The Witness is nothing more than a sliver of dark shearing through a field of white, but even at such a distance, Reed can feel its eyes on him. A chill jolts down his spine the moment the reticle locks on. His Exomind throbs with the sense-memory of a migraine.
He immediately knows something is wrong. He turns to his Ghost. His Ghost looks at him, but it's already dead. The world separates into slices.

I should've paid more attention to you, Ikora. My brain usually checks out when the words have more than three syllables. Who would've known you can't shoot your way out of a Vex teleporter? When I get out of this mess whaddya say you lay some Vex schooling on me?

They say the Cabal are not a subtle people. We have fallen so far.
The Cabal I knew were better. We understood that there is power in subtlety.
And that’s what it’ll take to recover the throne at the center of my homeworld. The seat meant for me.
And a Shadow of your Guardian-tribe would be the ideal instrument of assassination that will take it for me.
You’ve shown the Red Legion you fly my banner.
I know that when the time is right, I won’t have to ask. You’re on my side.
I see it when you relieve our foes of their skulls. When you embed those tiny, edged trinkets into their hearts. When you pierce them with your Light. And it is captivating.
When you’re ready, you will be magnificent. A Guardian of Guardians. Shadow of Shadows.
I reserve the right to be last when the end comes, and for that, I need you with me.
The Cabal I knew treasured knowledge above all things. Of course they did. I was their model.
We kept vaults of artifacts and texts in the great athenaeum worlds spread across the mother system.
Texts about the exalted history of the Empire, and its eclectic people.
Texts about the vast ennead, trapped and reaching out.
Texts about the feats of will made possible by Light and Traveler-lore.
Texts about… well, theorizing about the dark. So little is written, save for that which was recorded from the dreams of worms.

The vaults housed technology and weapons gifted from countless indoctrinated worlds. And judging from their absence in this Red War, Dominus Ghaul’s Legion has either forgotten or lost them all. The athenaeum worlds required learned guides to navigate: guides loyal to me. I’ve not heard from them in a very long time.
A Shadow of your Guardian-tribe would be the ideal treasure hunter to plunder those repositories and take from the false empire the secrets that rightfully belong to me.

The Cabal I knew valued marksmanship. In this way, and only in this way, do the Red Legion resemble my people. But the elegant, precision weapons of the past? Gone, save for the limited Psion arsenals. Replaced by Red Legion bluster.

Even the weapons and technology left for my Loyalists aboard the Leviathan are Legion issue and standard. The Cabal have lost so much in my exile. Only when I have reclaimed the athenaeum worlds in the mother system will we see the likes of rightful, classical Cabal weaponry again.
Until such a time comes, and I pray that it comes before the end, a Shadow of your Guardian-tribe would be the ideal, civilized sharpshooter to fight the false Empire in the place of true Cabal.
The Cabal I knew commanded ships that spoke to our affluence and cultivation, forged from the crucible of war so that we might never need to fight again.

But what did the Red Legion deploy in place of the glossy, magnificent fleets that I remember? Warships. Carriers. Interceptor squadrons. Harvesters. The Almighty. Blunt and base tools of war, like the soldiers who use them.
The Cabal fleet that I remember shocked with its allure and refinement. They would never threaten. Our power was such that our threats were unspoken. And always present.

A Shadow of your Guardian-tribe, with your raw instincts and reflexes, would be a perfect navigator of these vessels. You’ll guide them like blades past the throat of my homeworld’s planetary defense force.
My homeworld... I can’t remember its name. Perhaps I’ll give it a new one.
Open war is for savages. Pit fighters. The Red Legion. There shall be a day, long before the end comes, when that throne is mine again.

She tells you Osiris has been returned as promised, and her Techeuns have fully verified his identity. Moreover, Mara shares that she has Savathûn's exorcised worm in captivity. A point in our favor, she contends.
While the Dreaming City remains cursed, Mara Sov believes the curse can still be broken. For now, she advises you to look after Osiris and think on all you've learned on your quest to rescue him.
Aid Queen Mara Sov and her coven of Techeuns in exorcising Savathûn's worm.
Saint promises he will see to Osiris's care until he wakes up. He wants his face to be the first Osiris sees.
He thanks you for all you've done, and for not losing faith. He assures you that when Savathûn shows herself, she will meet judgment.

The time is now. Everything is in place, and the stars have found their proper alignment. Mara Sov and her Techeuns await you in the Dreaming City to perform the exorcism ritual on the Witch Queen's worm. Xivu Arath won't stand by and let this happen. A confrontation is to be expected. All that remains now is for you to join the ritual and play your part.
Enter the Dreaming City, fight your way to the Exorcism ritual, and defend Queen Mara.
“Sword.” In a flash, the blade appears again, this time at the student’s throat. Both pairs of eyes widened. One aghast, one aglow. “Say it with me.”
A blade appears in each outstretched hand. A pair of wings form on each Warlock’s back. Two Warlocks take flight and vow to never again look down.
The stillness of the hurricane's eye prickled my skin and brought with it realization. We don't have to choose between the calm and the storm. In fact, to have either, we must have both.
That was the day I first called the storm.

The streets were chaos. We fell under Cabal bullets and blades; red was the color of the day. Everywhere, red. Darkness found me three times that day and each time Ghost woke me, I woke to ever more red. I looked to the sky, but even there I saw nothing but the red reflection of a civilization burning to ash. Hope faded with the last of my Light; this was where I would meet my final death.

A flash of violet pulled my eyes from down sight. A Cabal ship careened out of the smoke, burning black-indigo. And I saw her, riding the wing, but she was gone in a blink as the ship smashed into the earth. She reappeared in the middle of a legion, and in a second half-heartbeat, rose into the air and dropped an explosion of void the likes of which I’d never seen.
I had believed I was a Voidwalker… until I beheld Ikora Rey.
The most effective way to defeat a Champion is to stun it, but elemental abilities provide additional tools to defeat them.
The most challenging fights will require you to take advantage of elemental surges, overcharged weapons, and the unique effects inherent to your elemental abilities.
Titles are collections of Triumphs, which when completed give you a Title to wear above your head. Titles are accessible from the Journey screen.
Some activities, like raids and Nightfalls, require you to play with friends. You can use Guided Games to find teams willing to help you get through an activity.
Unstoppable Champions will relentlessly chase and attack you unless they are stunned.  Ignite,  suspend, or  shatter them, or use weapons with  intrinsics to stun them.
Barrier Champions will summon an unbreakable shield at low health. While shielded, they will quickly regenerate health. Weapons with the  intrinsic can pierce this shield.
Overload Champions will constantly regenerate their health and use their special abilities unless they have been  jolted,  suppressed,  slowed, or disrupted by weapons with  intrinsics.
The Melee, Grenade, and Super stats decrease the cooldowns of those abilities.
Stat points above 100 instead increase their damage.
Synthcord is a special material used at the Loom near Ada-1 in the Tower to create Synthweave. You earn Synthcord by completing Armor Synthesis bounties, also obtainable from Ada-1.

Ghost mods have a variety of effects—gaining experience, tracking, as well as obtaining materials and other activity reward modifications. Ghost mods can be acquired from many different sources. Check your collections to find out how to acquire your favorite mods.

Ghost can help you pinpoint the location of some hidden objects or points of interest. Listen for the noise he makes, and look for the Ghost icon in the top right corner of the screen. When you take Ghost out, he will also look toward the object's location.

Ghosts can have mods applied to them now, just like weapons and armor! They can be Masterworked to increase the quality and quantity of mods—grab your favorite Ghost shell from your vault or collections and start today!

Badges are earned when collecting all gear and cosmetics associated with a particular theme. Collections are accessed on the Collections tab. You need to collect the gear from only one class to earn the badge, so why not start today?

The Collections tab is where you can view every weapon, piece of armor, emblem, shader, Sparrow, Ghost, and any other cosmetic you've ever acquired. Most can be reacquired for a small cost from the Collections, in case you dismantled it.
Synthstrand is a material used to purchase Armor Synthesis bounties from Ada-1 in the Tower. You earn Synthstrand by defeating combatants across Destiny.
Unsure what to do next? See your Guardian Ranks progress from the Journey screen for your next steps.
Some features are locked behind Guardian Ranks progression. You can view your progress from the Journey screen.
Armor archetypes, such as Brawler or Grenadier, can help identify which armor pieces are the best fit for your Guardian.
Armor archetypes determine the two highest stats on each piece of armor.
Hover your cursor over the archetype icon while inspecting a piece of armor for additional information.
The tertiary, or lowest, stat on each piece of armor is selected at random.
There are several artifacts to choose from, available on your Character screen, which offer a variety of perks. Your equipped artifact is included in loadouts.
Barrier Champions are vulnerable to  Volatile and  Unraveling Rounds, as well as gunfire, while  radiant.
The Weapons stat improves weapon handling, reload speed, and damage against non-boss targets.
Stat points above 100 instead boost damage against bosses and Guardians and grant a chance to gain extra ammunition.
Unstoppable Champions are vulnerable to being  blinded,  suspended, and shattered.
Tier 5 armor will always have the highest possible total stats, and a randomly selected Tuned stat that unlocks additional stat mods.
Higher tiered armor will have increased total stats. All armor pieces at tier 5 will have the maximum possible stats.
Tier 4 and 5 armor will have a higher energy capacity than lower tier armor, allowing additional mods to be equipped.
From Best Dressed to Playmaker and beyond, award commendations to show your support for your fellow Guardians.

Increasing the Masterwork tier of armor costs Glimmer, Enhancement Cores, Enhancement Prisms, and Ascendant Shards. The cores and shards can be purchased from Banshee-44, or earned in various activities.
Each armor piece has a Masterwork tier, which provides additional stat benefits when upgraded. Increasing the tier becomes more expensive each time.
Ada-1 has Armor Synthesis bounties available every week. Pick up and complete a bounty to earn Synthcord.
In need of a fireteam? You can locate other players through Fireteam Finder in-game, on bungie.net, or on the Destiny Companion App.
Creating universal ornaments through Armor Synthesis requires earning class-specific Synthweave. You can also purchase Synthweave Templates, good for any class, from the Eververse Store.
Triumphs are bite-sized records of your achievements. They can be related to your character, specific destinations, activities, lore discoveries, and more.
Overload Champions are vulnerable to being  jolted,  suppressed, and  slowed.
The Class stat decreases the cooldown of your class ability.
Stat points above 100 instead grant a temporary overshield whenever you use your class ability.
The Health stat grants healing from collecting Orbs of Power and reduces flinch from incoming damage.
Stat points above 100 instead grant extra shields and increase the speed shields begin regenerating.
Armor and weapons can be infused with other similar pieces of gear, gaining the Power level of the infused piece, for the cost of Glimmer plus one Enhancement Core.

Each piece of armor—helmet, arms, chest, and legs—has six associated stats that affect your overall game performance. When you get a new piece of gear, review its stats to see whether it is valuable to you.
All armor pieces have mod slots which can be equipped with a variety of armor mods. Mods can have subtle or drastic effects on your combat performance, so choose carefully.
Some mods are energy-aligned and will affect all of your weapons of a particular damage type. Pay attention to the damage type of your equipped weapons when choosing your armor mods.
Using two pieces of armor, from each of two different sets, can sometimes fit your goals better than a four piece set perk. Experiment with what works for you!
Armor set bonus perks are activated by equipping enough pieces of armor from the same set.
Each set has two perks: one for two pieces, and one for four.
Elemental abilities provide a wide range of effects against Unstoppable, Overload, and Barrier Champions. Equipping new Fragments can give you access to additional effects.
Activities that use Seasonal Artifact weapon overcharges also feature bonus damage from Kinetic weapons when your subclass matches an active surge element.
Overcharged weapons are available in some challenging activities. Some overcharged weapons are unlocked on the Seasonal Artifact; others are always available in certain activities.

lines.text: "I love making people laugh. And by 'people,' I mean me. Haha!" "Haha! Me!"

He quietly giggled as he stood blocking my exit, almost as if to taunt me. I start to push my way past but the blasted fool pulls hard on my ear, swiftly takes a step back, and presents his rump in a jesting dance. Not willing to get pulled into his game, I ignore his blatant attempts at a farce and continue forward. Abrupt shrills of frenzied laughter break out as I feel the full force of his boot on my backside. I cannot ignore his flagrant mockery. I reel around, take hold of his collar and clock him full force. Behind me, in the distance, I hear hysterical laughter. Confused, I whirl my head back to see a jaunty man skipping off. I look back at my hands to find them empty. That jester has taken me for a fool.

"Keep it clean. Your body. Your mind. Your armor. Weapons. Gear. Ammo. CRS #1: Keep it clean. Clean equals function. Clean equals focus. That's where it all starts. Skill matters. Training, practice, experience. All key ingredients. All valued assets as you balance death and glory on the battlefield. But once you're trained and ready for war. And once your gear is up to the standards of a proper, respected, walking, talking war machine. What comes next?"
"That's right. CRS #1177: Ammunition is your best friend. So what do you do?"
"Load. Up. Get yourself a weapon that spits unending fire and stock up on ammo until your shoulders slump and your back aches. Because each round is a war all its own."

"O, lion! Stretch your wicked claws toward the stars and rend a hole in the sky itself! Let the stars cascade down around you. Leap high and tear again at the night! lines.text: "Is it weird? Yeah. Maybe. Science fangs and space magic. But I've seen enough strange out there to understand normal ain't the norm. Anyway, the Warlock called 'em 'Bio-Conductive Trouble Breakers'. I call 'em 'Doom Fangs' 'cause of the fang, which is obvious, and then there's the doom we tend to inflict on a situation.

lines.text: "Must you all be so dark? You're too focused on the horns. Look, I have died hundreds of times hunting the shadowed killers in Murder Row. I spent years mulling over Toland's and Osiris's discourse on thanatonautics. I have dabbled a bit myself and saw what lingers immediately upon all death. What I have done is found a way to channel the Void to draw that essence in before it is lost to the ether, to return it to Light so it can be properly bestowed back on our enemies. Death does not need to be final; it can, in fact, be recycled. What's so dark about that?"

"Commander, as best we can tell, they're all gone. Somehow the Legion found their outpost, and the Hunters say Centurions still hold the ruins. This was the last text transmission we got before the signal died."
"And now we stand at the end. May history remember the Forge. Remember the Hammer. Remember the Sunbreakers."

In order to explain this, I need to explain Kessler Syndrome. As an Exo, I feel a duty to the machine to convey its original purpose. But first: ACD stands for Active Contact Defense. It is not an AC-DC Feedback Fence and it is not named for any work of pre-classical music. I am not winking. That is a malfunction.

Kessler Syndrome occurs when a planet's orbitals fill up with fast-moving debris, which strikes other debris and shatters it in a chain reaction. Soon you can't put up a satellite without it being shredded by a swarm of junk. To protect against debris, Golden Age warsats are shielded by a kinetic superconductor that transforms a punch into a charge.
Thanks to enemy action, we have a lot of downed warsats. With some tweaking, we can peel out the superconductor and produce a personal defense system. Like so.

Peacekeepers once patrolled the City before the Red Legion's attack. They were Guardians, but their interest was in protecting our core, our home. Most understood the value in exploration, but the peacekeepers were old guard, born in the aftermath of the Iron Lords. They lived through the Faction Wars; bore witness to what damage internal strife could bring to a fragile society. They vowed to keep the factions in check and stood at the gates as our walls expanded and our city became a home.
Now, nothing remains of the order. Yet their legacy delivers a harsh truth: the Last Safe City was never truly safe.

The science is inexact, but what is known is that the bio-matter becomes aggressively protective once linked to a worthy host, forming an organic shell that can amplify the host's own strength when immediate threats are detected.
Near-gods must believe in greater gods. But every power is finite, every life shorter than it wishes.

Only an astonishing mind can truly appreciate just how tiny it is when set against the known universe; and how insignificant the known becomes when it is devoured by what isn't seen and can't be comprehended.
As darkness begins to claim their ragged souls, you look ahead to find a great power pouring out of you—a face of fire and golden light.
That blazing wonder, a gift from the great-eyed god, is their salvation. Or are you?
Hello. We understand you require Real-Time Combat Instructives.

This is a BRAINVAULT Sigma-ACTIUM-X Cranial Dreadnought (Invictus Type). It is a fortress for your skull. Your skull is now a mighty bastion. You can break anything with your skull. The only limit is your spine. Relax. The lights will speak for you. Your hands are your eyes now. Look around. You find hand-to-hand combat relaxing. The lights will attract the enemy. Help them to relax as well. You will feel the effect of a CAREGRAVER Gamma-LYSANDER-IV Health Enforcer (Frontline Variant). Your enemies do not have a skull fortress. Their skulls are like meadows. Play in the meadows. Gather the flowers from the meadows. Gather them with electrokinetic trauma. Smell the flowers. Isn't that nice?

Okay, yeah, I got a problem with Scorn hanging around, because everywhere those little zombies go, the Hive follows. Then they start flipping over tables, and then my stuff is a mess, and, oh yeah, I'm exposed! So I need you to just, like, get rid of basically everyone, 'kay?

lines.text: These Lucent Hive might have the Light, yeah—but! That doesn't mean they like the sun. You can't change instincts like you change your gun.
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: We're encountering unique physical phenomena on Savathûn's throne world that are rendering our sensors useless. My Hidden need tissue samples from the residents to recalibrate their equipment. Lucent Hive would be ideal, but even the Scorn have been here long enough to be of some use.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: These Scorn, they got no respect for a Ghost's hard work! They—they're tearing out my surveillance devices! Look, I need you to send 'em a little message, yeah? Show 'em what happens when they start doing unlicensed electrical work!
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: The Lucent Hive, they—they used me. The Scorn kicked me around… even the big guy was ready to turn me in! You're the only person that ever believed in this little Ghost, y'know? So I need you to go show them all you're not to be messed with!
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: It seems the Scorn naturally emit ionizing radiation that disrupts our comm systems. A high-gravity burst should repolarize the effect and get our system back online.

lines.text: I know what you're thinking. 'Big explosion? That'll bring 'em running for miles!' Yeah, well, maybe that's what we want? We want 'em watching you make trouble so nobody's watching me get what you need!
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Fire fixes all our mistakes.
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Yeah, I like the part where you mush 'em into little gobs of goo with your mind. Is that—I mean, I feel like that's creepy to say, right? Eh, I can live with that.
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: My hands—I mean, if I had hands, they'd be shaking. Are your hands shaking? How are your hands not shaking?!
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Hi, yeah. I, uh… I kind of lost an important data drive to a scout patrol. I need it fried, but I couldn't tell you which Lucent Hive guy might be carrying it, so… maybe just zap a lot of them, and we hope for the best?
lines.speaker: Fynch

lines.text: Up until now, we've only been able to study the interaction of Light and Darkness from the perspective of Lightbearers. If you can turn the Darkness against the Lucent Hive, it could fill in a few holes in our understanding of both powers.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: Further developing your Deepsight means mastering your connection to the Darkness in general… particularly if you can bring it to bear against beings affected by Darkness themselves.

lines.text: I've been reviewing ancient Earth lore, and apparently, we're supposed to kill undead things by shooting them in the head. But you've been shooting them, like, everywhere. So, yeah… do you feel comfortable shooting someone in the head to test a theory?

"My Hidden have been tracking a series of temporal distortions moving across Mars. Everything seemed benign until they stopped near an old Seraph complex in the northern wastes."
"As you can see, that Seraph complex then sprang back to life, for the first time since the Collapse, no less." Ikora looks stern. "We'd be fools not to take that as an ill omen."
"I worry about him hurting himself. I would have denied his request to be involved at all if Ana wasn't sure this was important."

"I was wondering when we'd see the Sol Divisive again. After the destruction of their Undying Mind, I'd hoped they'd slink back into the Black Garden forever… but the Witness has other plans for them."

"The Seraph complex you cleared wasn't just a prison, it was a treasure trove of Golden Age data, weapon schematics, navigational charts, and I'm sure much more." She chuckles to herself. "I'm sure our Foundries will be tripping over themselves to claim and print Seraph weapon schematics."
"Ana's pulling together a fireteam as we speak to recover and transfer it all to the Tower's archives. Whatever it was the Vex were looking for, we'll find it."

You've completed the "Spire of the Watcher" and foiled the Sol Divisive's plans… but perhaps more importantly, the data gathered from your adventure may provide some clarity to Osiris's cryptic visions.

We were in the Rathskeller. If you don't know what that is—I didn't at the time, but it's a sort of restaurant and bar underground, not far from the bookstore. Hundreds of years old. This wasn't Beijing, back then we lived in Australia. Sydney. And I had gone to have lunch with my dad at the university where he was teaching.
So I'd brought all this information about looking for colleges. I remember we had holograms floating all around the table while we ate pizza and it was a great time, you know?

Anyway there was this TV playing. And that was the first time we saw it: drone footage from the edge of the solar system. Something had come in that no one had expected. My dad looked up and he just froze, like his mind just flipped on and he was lost. He would get like that.
That was the first time we saw the thing that everyone eventually called the Traveler.

Anyway, my oldest daughter was applying to the university and we had flown in from our home in Sydney, to visit. We had lunch with some professors and afterwards we visited one of the dorms. Just over there. It's not there anymore. Thank god. It was an old dorm.
There were protests all over, that day. The Moon X cults were in full force, calling for all governments to combine.
I took the call in the drone we rented for the day. They wanted me to cut the visit short but I refused. They wanted me to be gone for a year and a half. They could wait until morning.

The day the Shadows died, Feltroc sat in a perch high above the fighting, among a sea of glittering rounds. There was a Red Legion corpse for each shell on the engineering deck of Ghaul's ship below. When everything in her field of vision was dead, she took aim at the enemy's airborne rounds, the ones meant for the Shadows still in the fight. She had hit several by the time the Red Legion managed to fill the air shaft around her with a neurotoxin.

Feltroc pitied your kind for your reliance on the Light. Prove her wrong. Show this universe you can open your mind and accept new horizons, as she did. Your predecessors have sought to understand other sources of power, to control them. None have embraced them like I have. Like you could.
There is an entire spectrum of power left untapped that your Light prevents you from realizing.
When the time comes, seek me out. I will teach you to grow fat from strength.

As a Psion, Feltroc possessed the uncanny ability to slow her breathing and steady her motion with a layer of telekinetic manipulation. Before her passing, she had long sought a seat on my Psion Council, to help maintain the nightmare realm I reserve for prisoners and punishing wayward Loyalists. But she proved to be too valuable an asset in the field.
The life of a Shadow is sometimes a life of disappointment, and it pains me to say so. A burden I will carry until the end comes.

As with the Fulminator after her, I gifted Feltroc with a second skin—a battle harness that allowed her to stride with the physical dimensions of the average bipedal Loyalist. I had intended it to be an asset to her, a means to faster preparation with her armory of weapons, a place to store additional tools, and allow her to enter combat with the ergonomics of a "standard" soldier.
She told me she preferred it because it gave her enemies a fair shot at her head. I enjoyed her company immensely.
Feltroc, the Skull-Piercer, wore this last. A gun in her hands was a guarantee of victory. Whispers that my Shadows could kill from anywhere, as quickly as a spoken word, drew from her deeds.
There is a tribe among Guardians with similar penchants for surgical strikes, is there not? Perhaps one of them could take her place.

She trusts you will retrieve what they stole and deliver justice for their crimes against the Reef.

"Ah yes, Archie came through not too long ago. What a good lad. He kept watch while I brewed some tea, then darted away claiming to have seen a bird made of light… and I think he took my favorite mug, the little scamp."
"Yeah, Archie ran off again. He insisted it was teatime. Sounds like he went to go see Devrim, if you ask me."
"Oh yeah, I saw our little friend. He took off in the direction of the Skywatch. Barking about a cave."

"That dog is really starting to worry me with these escapades. Archie's been gnawing on this bone from the Dreaming City and weird things have been happening, so I took it from him. Figured you'd know what to do with it."
"Hmm? Oh, yes. Archie was here. He wanted very much to play fetch." Eris pauses for a moment. "I managed to divert his attention to the railgun."
"I think Archie's finally tuckered out. He was really excited to leave this last gift for you. Said it would be an eternal symbol of his affection."
"Archie is gone? Have you checked upstairs? Archie seemed very interested in noodles."
"I really don't have time for this, Guardian. Yes, Archie was here. I don't know what he was up to, but Archie was yapping on about someone being trapped in a well."
"I promised Ana I'd keep an eye on Archie, but that dog ran past here with three green eyes on his display. Could you check in on Eris on the Moon for me?"
"I hope Archie didn't cause you too much trouble. He left this for you. I… think it's expired."

"I still don't know how Archie gets to these places and at this point I'm afraid to ask. Last I saw him, Archie was barking up a storm about clouds and skyboards. Sounds like a visit to Nimbus is in order, Guardian. Hopefully this is the last time."
"Such a bleak place, the Moon. So… haunted. At any rate, Archie brought something back for you. Archie seems really excited about it."
"Seems like Archie got that tea, after all. Even brought you back something of Devrim's. I won't tell him if you don't."
"Archie's run off again? To the Dreaming City? Better go see Petra."
"After last week, I told Archie to let me know where he's going, but all Archie said was something about becoming a cosmonaut. I bet Shaw Han will know what's going on."
"How did Archie even get to Old Russia? Do I even want to know? Archie told me to give this to you. People might look at you funny if you wear it, though."
"Oh hey, Guardian! I bet you're here looking for Archie, huh? What a fun pup. He asked about using my hoverboard. I, uh, told him it wasn't safe—but that he could check out the rest of my stash."

"Eris did something truly kind for me, however, in those final moments. When she found me strung up, I saw her clutching the trinket I had made her—the one she'd rejected—tightly against her chest. I never forgot that. She'd made sure in that moment that the fire in my heart didn't go out. Made sure I knew I wasn't alone. The fire in me raged. What I would've given to stand with my fireteam one last time and burn those heathens to oblivion!"
"Eris's words rang in my ears as the Hive tore my Light from my soul."

"The resilience of Eris Morn—her greatest strength and her greatest weakness. To see the Heart of Crota peel my Light away and feed it to those disgusting little maggots and yet do nothing to stop it… She made the right call. 'Else the fire in us both might've gone out that day. I'd never blame her."
"I felt my spirit leave my body through my Light. And then—only darkness."
"There is a mystery here," Eris says softly. She turns the tablet around in her hands. "A memory stirs. I think…no."

"The worst part about what the Hive did to us wasn't the killing. It was the separation. Splitting us up made us weak. They dragged me deep below the lunar surface, through a wall of endless doors. Strung me up. Made my Ghost, Karsys, watch as they tore my Light away, like stripping muscle from bone. Then they killed Karsys in front of me. Sure would've been nice then to have had some of that hope Eris had been peddling."

"It was hard to see the point of a single fireteam taking on Crota, but it was easy to understand how retribution had driven us there. The names of everyone we'd lost in that needless disaster were etched across the walls of the Last City, each and every one a reminder that they were gone and we were not. So when Eriana-3 came knocking, it was a simple decision. From top to bottom, we'd avenge every one of those names. A fire burned in all six of us. We were gonna make sure Crota knew it."
"I am sorry I couldn't save you, friend. In life, you may have been unable to escape their grasp. But you will have your vengeance yet."

Savathûn. The Witch Queen. Hive God of Cunning and Lies.
After the death of her brother Oryx, Savathûn went into hiding.
Until they tried to take on the Guardians.
Not out of fear, of course, but out of strategy.
The Relic is of the Pyramids, there's no doubt.
In times of crisis, people look to their leaders for answers.
Secure the camp!
They believe themselves so much more than that.
These things don't see themselves as gods, no.
All of them. And when they get here?
If only we'd known the flood she was holding back.
Savathûn is solely responsible for her own ruin.
This new power it's able to lend us here may be the key.
But maybe faith in the Traveler is exactly what we need.
The Traveler is fighting for its life—for all our lives.
The Witness sees itself as the god it wishes the Traveler was.
But not even here will it speak. It only screams.
And it illuminates what the Witness wants most.
The Traveler is weakening. It cannot hold back the final shape alone.
I emerged, and I think a part of me expected the Traveler to say something to Ophiuchus… to comfort its child.
You don't understand—we've got to get to the Veil!
Well, good! There isn't a moment to lose.
Not all of us have lives to spare.
I understand what's at stake, Lightbearer… far better than you.
Calus, sworn disciple of the Witness, was charged with securing the Veil.
The Veil, a powerful artifact at the heart of the Witness's ambitions.
We set out to put a stop to Calus's plans.
There was no predicting what would come next.
And it was left for anyone to find.
But we could do nothing, and they would still die.
We are connected to the weft and weave of the universe.
That everything they could become dies with them.
Our gifts were meant to defend against impossible threats.
Those who need us have never needed us more.
W—What if what I want is to stay here?
The final shape awaits. The Veil is but the next step.
My forces are locating it as we speak.
The Neptunians won't pose much of a threat with their tawdry technology.
Ah! This calls for a toast, does it not?
Find the Veil so I can move on from this drudgery!
Saint and Osiris are attaching to your fireteam for this investigation.
Whatever it is, it ran aground on Nessus.
We don't know what to expect. So we're sending our best.
You should come and kill them. Like old times.
It tempted us. But our friends kept us standing tall. And we prevailed.
And an old friend made contact, looking for help.
Visit soon!
It spoke through our Ghosts and offered us salvation if we submitted to it.
Together, we have united against our common enemy.
But in turn, Osiris gained access to hers.
In an unprecedented move, the Traveler left Earth to confront the Witness head-on.
We have done so through the strength of our community.
Since before history, there's been this raging river.
We believed we were the champions of the good because we wielded the Light.
In the story, some try to divert the river. Others try to build a dam.
Yeah, it's a story we tell kids on Neptune.
The domain of the Light is the domain of the physical.
I think I know of a place where we can find some of that power.
For so long, we saw Dark and Light as antagonists.
The Darkness… then is revealed in many facets.
The nature of Strand confirms this line of thinking.
Like the Light, it is a powerful tool of paracausal energy.
The Darkness is not what we first assumed.
Come see me for some important assignments, Guardian.
With help from Guardians like you, we have come to a greater understanding of the truth.
"Bravery inspires sacrifice."
"And sacrifice…"
"Devotion inspires bravery."
Brought on by the separation from my power.
I won't lose another soldier in this war.
It was an honor to serve the Last City with you.
The children of Sol cry out for salvation.
You will storm the Witness's monolith and strike where it is most vulnerable.
Micah-10, who comes to us with bold ideas.
Misraakskel rallies his House of Light to save their Great Machine.
You will shatter its hold on the Traveler.
I've brought our allies to help you land the final blow.
The full might of Caiatl's empire stands behind us in this endeavor.
The Hive, ravenous worshippers of death, came to feed their infernal hunger.
The Black Fleet closes in, edging us toward a second Collapse.
Guardians know that when they stand together, they are stronger.
In this city, humanity lived peacefully in all its forms.
Though in the end, we came together. To rebuild. To heal.
And we launched colony ships to settle worlds beyond our own.
Invaders from beyond our system arrived in droves.
The warlike Cabal came for our territory and resources. For conquest.
The Traveler was pursued by an ancient enemy.
And now, new threats use our own powers against us.
And the Awoken… a people touched by both Light and Dark.
When the Traveler arrived in our solar system, they called it many things: a ship, a planet, a god.
Pirates called the Fallen came to scavenge the remains of our Golden Age.
And the Vex, strange living machines, came to recreate our world in their own brutal image.
The Warlocks, mage-scholars trained in the arcane arts.
But like all golden ages, it was doomed to collapse.
Immortal warriors gifted with the power of the Traveler's Light.
And the Hunters, bold adventurers gifted with cunning.
Lightbearers took an oath to protect the Last City.
We will tell the most cunning sibling of a cataclysm.
Not great, partly my fault. Lesson learned. Let's not dwell.
I woke up here in this body. Alone. No Ghost, no way to use the Light.
And what it's doing out here has a name too.
Like we were two cards shuffled back into our deck. Whole again.
But we talked it out because we're adults.
Because we got bigger problems. Bigger, weirder problems.
Somebody's up in that monolith with their hand on a knife.
Crow said this was all inside the Traveler but… I already knew.
He seems nicer these days. Yeah, pretty low bar, I'll admit.
Ours was a world of prosperity and peace.
In the wake of loss, Eramis rebuilt a life.
Eramis, like most, was left consumed with rage.
They're going to attempt a link! We have to stop them!
I've been pondering the Veil's paracausal effects on Ghosts.
Pain is not a hindrance. It simply reminds us we're still breathing.
I know I haven't been the easiest guest in your city.
Whatever that thing is, we gotta take it down.
They'll remind us that unity is our greatest strength.
Osiris and I will return to a dream we thought we'd lost forever.
Secure the Veil.
It will not succeed for as long as we remain in existence.
We must begin our search in the pieces it has left behind.
But it proved to be his final mistake.
But their newfound god never spoke to them.
Before you can confront the Witness… you must understand it.
But they came to realize that it could bring ruin… just as easily.
And when they found it, they arrived to claim it.
Their scholars discovered that the Gardener shared a connection with another entity among the stars.
A power that was shaped by thought and consciousness.
The Witness's first victims were once like you.
They called it "the Gardener," their deity of life.
And though they lived in paradise, they came to crave a greater purpose.
How it could bend the laws of the universe and create life.
They brought the Veil back to the Gardener in an attempt to strengthen their connection.
It lavished them with gifts, but not with guidance.
By studying the Veil, they came to know the Darkness.
The paracausal bond he shares with his twin sister will guide us safely through.
Our enemies wielded the Light, shaking our faith in what we once thought we knew.
But we soon learned even that was more complicated than we thought.
It brought the people of Sol to the brink of extinction.
That's our role: the tip of the spear.
A terrible calamity caused by the Traveler's oldest enemy.
Joy was his purpose and his strength, he said.
A chance to become greater than he'd ever been.
There was nothing he would not sacrifice for his own salvation.
Instead, he caught a glimpse of something more.
If we don't stop him, he'll make sure it's the end for us all.
And when the Witness came to him at last, Calus faced what he had run from all along.
I thought he'd shrivel to nothing in the void of space.
I should've killed him then. But I thought exile more fitting.
To angst over edicts and enemies was weakness.
We could not do it alone, so I turned to the Guardians.
My Queen commanded me to slay a beast.
The Guardians killed Riven and ripped out her heart.
We had to find a way through the portal.
The physical world, with its natural laws, is the domain of Light.
In the end, we could not prevent the Witness from reaching its goal.
And we had no tolerance for its ambivalence.
We, too, once looked to the silent god for purpose.
Your Traveler had no tolerance for such vision.
More than a protector of Neomuna, he was a true Cloud Strider.
He cut his years short, so that the whole of humanity may thrive far into the future.
Today, we suffer… so tomorrow can live on.
But knowing its intent was vital to protecting the City.
This enemy has taken so much from us all.
I have the tools to make you understand.
I only want the one that is real.
Somewhere was another us that made the right choices.
I still dream of what we could be.
Or has fate made other choices for us?
I experimented to find the words that would make you understand.
But for you, the cost was always too great.
I do not know what that version looks like.

"Is this what I have done? Once, she looked at me with adoring eyes. I was her world, and she my stars. How have I made her into this? Have I been so blind? So selfish? What have I done?"
"It hurts. It hurts. It hurts. It hurts."
"I should have killed every member of the old guard when I had the chance. Mercy was my greatest failing, and they used mercy's edge to cut me down to my knees."
"…and here, you see, etched on the bell? That is when I attained the title of emperor and began a thousand years of peace."
"Cut it away. A knife through memory's flesh. Peel back what I was and replace it with scalding gold. I do not want this. I do not want this. I do not want this."

"Once, I stood out overlooking a vast plain. Wildflowers and nettles blossomed at my feet. The future was full of promise and potential. Yet I upturned an overflowing chalice of shame at my feet, and let it puddle into rot."
"I beg you, don't do this."

"You were born only to suffer, because I could not set aside that which I knew was a trap. My curiosity is a poison flowing through my veins, curdling my heart, rotting my mind. And yet, I do nothing to stop it."

"For once in my life, I do not feel shame. I feel the caress of a thousand hands, hear the comforting hush of a thousand voices. 'Do not be afraid,' it whispers. 'We are your salvation.' Yes. Please. Save me from myself."

"I defiled them. The remains of countless dead. Honored servants of the empire, extended members of my lineage. I ripped their tombs open to harvest their genetic information… to build an army of unquestioning soldiers. What have I become?"
"Her memory curdles in my chest. Her first laugh, her first steps, her first kill. Poison. Poison. Poison."

And most of all, I want to see my Queen again.

My folks tried their best. But… the road's a dangerous place.
Even killed a Captain before they shot her.
Long as I could remember, my family had been walking toward the Last City.
I never had powers like the Guardians, or a Ghost to resurrect me.
I'd heard tales of people resurrected. Chosen for immortality.
But in the cockpit, I'm every inch as tough.
When the House of Winter attacked, my momma fought 'em off best she could.
When I finally reached the Last City, I knew my momma was right.
My momma told me we'd be safe there. She said that was all that mattered.
Your chains are showing. All that power, wasted serving false gods.
Look what I've done for you. No more Light. No more Dark.
Come then, pawn. Show me what freedom has given you.
The only thing we have to break here—is you.
Search the buildings. Find it.
My friends. We are all in great danger.
I've seen terrible things born out in the darkness.

It's just… we keep coming face-to-face with Darkness, and every time, we fail to stop it. We're just so… powerless.

Its power, a path to inevitable violence and grief.
It promised power to all those worthy of it, in the form of Stasis—setting off a race to Europa.
But there were those, like Elsie Bray, who understood that what we call Darkness is a neutral force.
Like the Light, it could be a powerful tool for good in the right hands.
We could never have imagined what awaited us on that frozen moon.
Many of our people feared that a second Collapse was imminent.
We wield it in defense of the Last City.
And amongst our closest friends, old enemies lay waiting.
Darkness is a part of our universe, a natural force.
Where once we saw only eternal foes, we discovered allies against a common threat.
Hidden away in the Last City, the Hive god Savathûn prepared her greatest trick yet.
We challenged many of our assumptions in the days that followed.

It had a Ghost, Ikora. Same as any other Lightbearer.

I understand completely. It's not like Savathûn to allow herself to be seen so easily.
The very parasite that once plagued the Witch Queen herself.
Do not delay us with pleasantries. This parasite knocks at death’s door.
This parasite is an opportunity—to learn from humanity's greatest failure.
For most, yes. But for the Queen of the Awoken...
What use do we have for Savathûn's dying worm?
It requires strength and a new host to survive, to divulge its secrets.
Now… we prepare for the Witness and stop the next Collapse.
Guardian! I just got the message: the Traveler is back in the Last City. Is it done? Is Savathûn… ?
Good work, Guardian. You did the right thing.
So did you, Guardian. So protective of your Traveler… that you wouldn't let me keep it safe.
Good enough. Hold your position. The Hidden are coming to secure the remains.
But the Witness is coming. The game is yours to play now. Yours to win… or lose.
Xivu Arath draws strength from our conflict. She believes her logic absolute.
I devour the free. I conspire with my vengeance.
I will grasp it and contravene its power. There is no other way.
I will take what I need. The words in my throat are the weapon in my fist. Aiat, aiat, aiat!
I am the many-mouthed hunger. I am the knife-edged truth.
Do not be afraid. Bear witness to my sublimation.
Bring me your tithes.
I’m so grateful to you for reminding me. For telling my story.
Incredible that I could forget something like that, isn't it? Such a storied life… erased.
The Light offers us a fresh start. But if we don’t know where we came from, how will we know where to go?
Her scheming led to something we once believed impossible.
With the Witch Queen involved, nothing could be taken for granted.
Our only hope was to uncover just how Savathûn had stolen the Light.
Lucent Hive, raised by Ghosts, now wielded the Light against us.
The Voice in the Darkness, and the architect of humanity's Collapse: the Witness.
Armed with this vital secret, we now had a fighting chance.

A powerful artifact known as the Veil was hidden away on the planet Neptune.

Whatever the Traveler's motivations, in the end, we had to rely on each other.
With Savathûn off the board, the Witness would soon arrive to launch its assault against the Traveler.

"They acted like they wanted to trade. Got close and killed the Ghost first, as if they'd done it a hundred times before. The rest came down like a swarm of locusts; stripped the fresh bodies." Tiga tugs down the neck of her coat. A wicked knot of stitched skin curls into a scar under her collar bone. "Stuck me to the ground with an Arc spear and ripped apart anyone with fight left… Spear jolted my heart on the way out. Got me breathing again. They left me like a clean bone on a picked carcass. They weren't soldiers either."
"They say that, but I bet when Fallen breached the walls they didn't stop shooting."

"Many Eliksni are still our enemies. Many of them only know violent lives, but if Mithrax and his House are willing to pledge to the City, to the Traveler… We serve the Light; its servants are our allies."
"They're clinging to existence. I can empathize." Tiga pulls her gloves tighter to her fingers. "Still doesn't mean everyone under the Traveler's an ally, Titan."

"Mark them." Siegfried looks at the suspects being escorted through the crowd and let free. He commits their image to memory. "No one even screened them. Tiga, is there a way I can pass through the streets unnoticed?"
"You?" She asks reluctantly, looking at his armored bulk. She recalls the smooth Stasis erasure from the Splicer temple. She bends under weight of Praxic duty. "Follow me."
"They're going inside." Siegfried turns to Ogden. "Where are we?"
"Sub-sector 4-2-9-1c, Botza District," says Ogden. "Purified water storage."
"It's an Ether reservoir," Tiga corrects, "We repurposed a handful of cisterns."
"I've seen what Dark Ether does. We end this now."
"Aunor was right to send us here. This place is sullied by Darkness."
"Right you are. Radiation consistent with Stasis is still present, sir." Ogden faces Siegfried. "I shudder to think a Guardian did this. Most uncouth."
"Let's not jump to conclusions."
"Something's been shielding the interior from scans since that last group moved through. Stay out here… just in case."
"From here I can see the radiation is quite high," Ogden chirps. "I'm sure the ruffians inside will be gobsmacked by your arrival."
"Far fewer hostiles than anticipated…"
"A Dark Splinter…"
"Praxic dog. Don't you know the Dark is rising? Look to the sky and see it brewing." Rain pours through the timber under abyssal cloud-churn. "It eclipses the Traveler."
"So are many of your brothers and sisters. Can you even be called Lightbearers anymore?"

"The Endless Night is a call to action we must defend. The Light brings only death. The Darkness brings only Salvation." He laughs to himself. "Lakshmi's rhetoric provided a convenient guise for our mission and brought so many to our door who wanted to strike against the House of Light. She gave us the ability to wield their fear."
"I'm glad you came, Titan" the man continues. "Your sister's Dark gift is almost spent."
"All fires will one day extinguish." The man delicately grasps the Splinter. Blood vessels burst in his fingertips. "So too will yours."
"Sir? I saw the bolt… Siegfried?"
"I'm here, Ogden. They knew I was coming."
"My name is Aunor Mahal. You're no longer being held here and may leave at any time, but I have questions first. Some you may have already answered."
"Ikora Rey sent me. I'm a friend," Aunor says, sitting down and leaning forward to unclasp the Eliksni's restraints. "What is your name?"
"Halt!" Siegfried thrusts his palm forward. A holographic Vanguard security sigil projects from his breastplate. His helm display pings firearms under their jackets. "Ogden, 'mountain keep.'"
"We have a runner. Door to our right around the tanker."
"Runner's mine."
"I am fleeter-footed."
"Y'also hold up better to gunfire." Tiga knocks her hand against the barricade. "Draw some for me?"
"Ogden, guard these degenerates."
"Tiga, you shot me."
"The Endless Night is here. The House of Light cannot stop it!"
"Guardian." The man turns to Seigfried. "There is a schism on the horizon."
"What is wrong with you?" She stands. "You could have set it off."
"Do you worry about me when we're apart, old friend?"
"Not at all, sir. You left me alone with four angry terrorists."

Siegfried peers out of a second-floor window overlooking a crowded street junction at the edge of the Eliksni Quarter. Large time-worn walls, once hardened fallback points in case of invasion, separate this district from the next. Dozens of City security officers oversee the only open crossing.

Tiga leads Siegfried and Ogden through damp maintenance sub-levels beneath the streets, making sure to keep sight of the suspicious group's feet through drainage grates and sewer accessways. Finally, they stop at a narrow alley flowing to the rear door of an industrial-looking structure. They pry the door up, widening a gap of dug out earth beneath it, and slip in one by one.

He inspects the interior of the temple: a space removed, like the edges of a hollow cube. Siegfried runs a hand against the wall beside him. Smooth as glass. His eyes pour deep into their gemstone stratification. The ceiling and floor reflect his image infinitely like a dark mirror. It is a moment captured in time and removed from existence. Surgical.
Voices outside the temple building. Siegfried notes a Human and makes his way to the exit through a petrified brick doorframe. Two Eliksni and a Human stand in heated conversation.

Infrequent drops of rain tap on Siegfried's armor. Praxic Inquisitors had squeezed precious information from last night's arrests. He looks upon an old timber-roof pyre hall, built before the walls turned mass cremations into memory. Intel states it is a staging ground for a burgeoning cult: radicals by the name of the Trinary Star. They congregate at the pyre hall and cross into the Eliksni Quarter, stoking unrest. Rot in the heart of their City, marked not fifty yards from the Wall.

He is to storm the hall and apprehend them—alive, for the Inquisitors desire more intelligence. Siegfried considers the effortlessness of Thundercrashing into the lot of them and purging their vile stain from the streets. Their hatred. Their corruption. But this place is an extrinsic arm to their operation. More interrogations would reveal their leadership, and he would cleanse them with Praxic fire.
Siegfried laughs. The pyre hall is as still as the surrounding burial yard.

He crosses an empty evening street and places a hand on the hall's entry doors. A burst of Light snaps the chain locking them and propels them open. Scattered showers seep through gaps in the roofing timber. Water trickles down stone walls, into floor channels sticky with old oil, and wells in several stone-carved burn pits lining the ground. Within one cleanly cut alcove sits a motionless armored form rippling in dim azure penumbra.
Siegfried enters, closer to the form: a moribund Guardian. Dangling in the air above their chest is a thin sliver of black-plated crystal. The air aches around it, a manifested need drawing him in.
He advances with static crinkling in his ear.

Siegfried stands over the Ghostless body and reaches toward the Splinter. Numbness stings his fingertips. He feels something ravenous, rapturous, familiar. It pulls deep against the Guardian's core. A source of paracausal power.

The thought occurs from outside himself. Not a voice, but a pull. A feeling. He gazes into the prismatic abyss. It is a Splinter through the fabric of reality—to be dug out. A tumbling sensation fills the still air. Rain drops slow until he is deaf to them.
A dull thud behind, like a heap of dry clay crumbling on stone.
The air turns stagnant. Siegfried recoils from the Splinter, spinning toward the door as a canister collides with his chest and detonates.
He is numb and dazed. Ogden crackles unintelligibly through his commlink.
His helmet is wrenched from his head. Brittleness climbs his flaxen braids as Stasis encloses his neck.
A man stands over him, armed with a large weaponized launcher that hums with instability.
Thickening raindrops crash against the twilight cobblestone of the hall.
Siegfried bridges his Light with the dead Guardian. He anchors himself in their paracausal remnant and draws upon it.
He sees too late that it is not the Light the Splinter fed on, but an innate Darkness now free to cross his open connection.
A latent attunement is awakened. A dark mirror reflects within.
The hall is awash in rain. Currents flow through it.
Siegfried twists the Dark to his will and calls the lightning.

A violent umbral bolt screams through the Endless Night and coils around him. Fulguration blind whites out the hall, shattering the Stasis crystals in earsplitting bursts and cascading electricity across the stone.

The heat of Siegfried's lightning obliterates everything around him. It turns the stone underfoot to glass and leaves ozonized steam billowing from gaps in his armor. Black scorch and ash marks are all that remain of his attacker, and their Dark host. Timber burns overhead.

Siegfried stands, free of Stasis. The Splinter lies waiting. He can no longer afford to look away. It had not corrupted him, nor tore his Light from his bones. It gave him the strength to save himself. He plucks it from the glass and holds it until the silence of the room shakes him into the present.
Siegfried slips the Splinter into his belt pouch.
He refits his helmet, and Ogden's voice pipes through stronger now.

Dim, temporary lights flicker over an Eliksni's head as she sits alone in the holding box of a small security station. Just outside the door she can hear a faint argument over the hum of distant generators. Power comes and goes, rolling darkness over her, the Quarter… the system. Elders spoke of the Whirlwind as if it were an escaped past. The past recurs when allowed.

Voices raise, obvious with anger. The door opens and an unfamiliar woman enters, robed in thick blue-flame colored cloth, trimmed with maroon stitch. She was conventionally unarmed, but the Eliksni could feel the pressure of Light coiled tightly underneath her armor. The Warlock looks the Eliksni over and shuts the door. They place a small metal device on the table between the two of them and press a button.

Siegfried crashes through the alley door into a large room. Dust swirls around him, Ogden close behind his pauldron. A half dozen reservoir tanks and piping over metal grated floors fill the space in two parallel rows flowing away from him. Between the rows he spots five figures spinning around to the shattered door.
The leftmost figure whips a pack off his back and throws it to the figure standing farthest from Siegfried.
The four remaining figures draw shoddy handguns. Two shots ricochet off Siegfried's armor before he slams a barricade to the ground.
Siegfried forms a tempered flashbang grenade in his hand. "Go," he says, tossing out the flash.

Siegfried marches through his barricade to make short work of the four stunned gunmen. He sears the guns from their hands with forked Arc bolts, lunges, grabs, and spins to throws the first gunman into another. He stamps out their vile intent with ease. The metal of his gauntlets leaves them bruised or unconscious. He binds their wrists with strands of Light. Three Humans and an Awoken.

Siegfried dashes into the central refinery, Tiga ten paces ahead. Steel-grate catwalks suspend them over a massive filtration basin. Ten paces more: the runner is down, clutching a crudely fashioned device and a burn hole in his leg.
I hear her voice… Can you hear it too?

lines.text: "I can now confirm," he says grimly, "that every Exo frame in Maya's lab once held the consciousness of Maya's wife, Chioma Esi, each a different version of her pulled from the Vex network."
"Uploaded, judged… found wanting, and eliminated."
"It would have broken me," he whispers. "And I think it has broken Maya. One capable of such horror has defiled the concept of love."
"Do not forget what you are dealing with."
"The Conductor awaits at the core of Nessus, working to awaken the planet and consume us in a flood of radiolaria… all in the name of her Golden Age, where she reunites with Chioma."
"I won't put another life in Maya's hands, not after what she's done. But if anyone could make her understand, it would be the one Chioma she's been searching for."
"One way or another," Ikora says, "the Conductor's search ends now."

"Greetings, Captain!" Failsafe says cheerfully. "My planetary scans reveal that the Vex machinery within Nessus is dormant once again. Perhaps learning the truth about Chioma caused Maya to question her own judgment and halt her plans for galactic domination!"
"I was part of a crew again, and now it's over," she says sadly. "I don't like goodbyes."
"See ya around, Captain," Failsafe says. "Thanks for everything."
"You, Guardian."

"The other Saint, he died alone. But I met you, after Osiris sent you in to find me. You gave me hope in my darkest time. I fought to live up to your example—that is how I survived. And slowly, I found I was no longer living for you… but I was living for me."
"But Osiris says all Mayas are scientists, and we can see her thoughts in her experiments."

There's a hidden little nook in the Hangar, great spot for watching Sparrow maintenance if that's what you're into. Comfortable too. Good place to get away from the noise. He breezes in and out, rooting up a cache he left there a long time ago. Never could get out of the habit of keeping emergency stashes.
Anywhere else he needs to stop off before he leaves for good? Maybe… maybe.
It's a short hop from there to his ship.
Probably it'd be something deep and meaningful. He doesn't have the heart to think it up. He steps into the other room, moves around the table covered in books and relics. Almost trips on the rug.
Getting out in the woods could clear his head. Maybe he shouldn't go after all.

He lingers in the entryway. It's the sort of lingering where you pretend nothing's changed—and it doesn't have to, as long as you never go in. Eris will always be just out of reach, but at least there, real in the apartment she barely used, in the City she defended but rarely saw.
It's a fool's dream. But what is he if not a fool? So he stays a little longer, sick with wishing.
He swears he can see Eris leaning against the railing, a sly little smile barely turning up the corners of her mouth. He can't stand it.
He goes into her apartment this time. Not to look through her things, really, just—prove it to himself. She's not there. She won't be. He's got to remember that.
He brushes his fingers along a side table and tries to imagine what she'd say to him.
He sees himself out, mouth stinging as he takes the stairs. That's it, then. There's nothing for him here. And he was a fool to think there was.
Cold out here. Reminds him—in a bad way—of that Light-forsaken planet he nearly died on.

He scuffles around the campsite. Pathetic, he knows it's pathetic. Even if people hadn't been through here, the storms would have blown over any footprints. Any lost trinkets would long since have been found or buried deep enough that he can't hope to find them.
Looking out on the desolate expanse doesn't do much for him, just leaves him alone with his feelings. Not a fun place to be. He moves on.
Sometimes it makes a guy feel better to make fun of someone way worse off than he is. He knows it's a mistake soon as he sets eyes on the giant robot face, though.
Maybe somewhere else. He turns and goes, ignoring the dramatic monologue already kicking off behind him.
He swings by to let the man in charge know he's going to be out of town for a while. Guy'll understand. And it's a new level of responsible; Commander should appreciate that.

The place is empty, though. He wanders around it—sets the beads to clicking against each other, prods the gold figure on the side table until it falls over, meanders past books and blinks at the cat perched on a shelf over his head.
Nothing. He's restless. The longer he stands still, the longer the grief has to get its hooks into him. He mutters a curse into the silence and sees himself out.

There's a little cliff that overlooks the cove's water. He settles there a spell. It's quiet. Not a lot of combat, few enough reasons for Guardians to swing through. The quiet doesn't so much remind him of her as make him wish she were there.
Everything's just going to keep doing that, huh. He can be honest with himself about that.
