"Containment is key here. We cannot allow anyone into that vault. Not the Hive, not the Dread, and certainly not Savathûn herself."

"As dangerous as it is, there's power in it we may be able to use. Rhulk forged a connection between the Chisel and his own ship. Affecting the one may affect the other—or so my Hidden have suggested."
"If you can glean anything else from Rhulk's ship, do. And please be assured that nobody unauthorized will be getting in anytime soon: the Hidden are setting up a perimeter as we speak."
"Well done, Guardian. The Vanguard's faith in you has never yet been misplaced. And if I may say… thank you for coming home safe."

"I'm asking you to take in your fireteam. My agents will remain on the scene for backup, but you're the tip of our spear. We need you in there, doing what you do best. Find out what the Dread are doing—and take what countermeasures you find appropriate."

"Did you… bake this yourself? REALLY?! That's amazing! Never had a 'home cooked' Neomun-Pie before though. I bet it's better than the ones in the vending receptacles."
"I'll enjoy these later, when we're not quite so busy," she says. "Happy Dawning!"
"Thank you, Guardian, from the bottom of my, heart—shell—core… that's the one. Seriously, it means a lot that you thought of me like this. My OWN cookie!"

"Tell you what. Bake anymore of these, and I'll wake up the big guy for a treat, assuming he can behave himself. Not when you're around, of course. Maybe he'll have a change of heart after he tastes your baking!"
"This is something I'll never forget."
"A lot's happened since the last Dawning. Eva's right—this is a good time to say thanks. From me, from Glint. For everything."
Ada-1 examines the gift skeptically. Eventually, she looks up and thanks you, but she still seems perplexed by the exchange.
Saint-14 opens his arms to you when you arrive with his gift. He accepts the cookies, sets them aside, and then clasps your hand warmly. He wishes you a happy Dawning.
Eris takes the gift from you, looks at it a moment, and then smiles very faintly. She thanks you and wishes you well.
Variks takes the offered gift carefully in one of his lower hands. "It is good to be your friend," he says gratefully.
Shaw takes the crumbler from you and grins. "If you've got time for baking, things must be going well for you in the Tower," he laughs.
When you instead place the delicate apple tart in her elegant hand, her eyes flicker, and a wide, guileless smile threatens to break across her face.
She stops, then takes a slow breath and shakes her head. The Queen of the Reef becomes once again the picture of composure.
You nod and turn to leave… but not before noticing the care with which she cradles the tart in her palm.
The Exo Stranger takes the bundle of brittle cookies from you with gratitude.
Brother Vance holds out his hands and accepts the gift. It's hard to tell his expression beneath that blindfold and hood, but you catch a hint of a smile.
As you place your gift at the golden statue's feet, it swivels its head to look at you and opens its mouth. The Emperor laughs, deep and delighted.
Crow accepts your gift with a grin, but he looks thoughtful a moment later.

Can be exchanged for an Enhanced Keycard in the Tharsis Bazaar.
Spider generously offers an exchange service for risk-averse Guardians to trade in their Deathmarks.

"Where one Kell sees detritus, another finds opportunity. And there is so much detritus borne from the territory war you've started." His shoulders shake as he chuckles. "Let's see what my scavengers have found you. As long as this conflict goes on, there's profit to be made."
Spider has promised you rewards for your effort. Let's see if he makes good on them.
Spider is profiting from the conflict in the Lawless Frontier, and is willing to cut you in on the winnings if you assist him.
Spider tosses you a bag jingling with currency and illicit goods—now yours.
He taps his fingers eagerly as you open his gift.
Return to Spider in the Tharsis Cantina.
Hold your friends close and take your enemies for everything you can get.
lines.speaker: Spider

lines.text: "Allies are easy come, easy go out on the frontier. But we hope you'll stick around. And I do mean we. I took a poll. Your favorability rating's looking good. I expect you're feeling as positive about the things we can do for you."
"So—you tell me. You in?"
A bold choice. Whatever your next move, I'll be watching to sweep up the profits…
lines.speaker: Spider

lines.text: "One thing about the Division is, Rao doesn't brook any nonsense. We won't mess with your Glimmer. We share resources accordingly. What am I gonna do with a Praxic Blade, cut my hand off? Any mods come in, they're earmarked for you—if you earn 'em."
"I'll see you back here soon, yeah?"
A lone wolf is a dead wolf. But then, so is a wolf backstabbed by its so-called allies… Best choose your path wisely, my respected Renegade.
lines.speaker: Spider

lines.text: "I got some verbiage to share… Eh, lemme read this out. 'The Totality Division will be pleased to welcome the Guardian of Earth as an ally. Allies are granted rewards commensurate with their efforts.'
"Ready to sign? The agreement's non-binding." Aghol pauses. "I think."
As tensions get worse and all our friends among the Syndicates ready their knives, Guardian, I think one thing—that it pays to be a middleman.
lines.speaker: Spider

lines.text: Getting your hands dirty already? Don't suppose I can sway you over to my side?
lines.speaker: Spider

lines.text: Loyalty changes hands easy as credits out there. If you're undecided on which path to take, I suggest consulting your pocketbook.
lines.speaker: Spider

lines.text: "You know us, Guardian. Do you want the frontier run by a military force with Imperium ties? Or a bunch of soup that likes to gamble? Pikers are the only answer."
"We've got the best tech, the best perks, and—let's be honest here—the best company. Ride with the Pikers, Guardian. You won't regret it."
"Gamble on the Reformation. Win big."
A ping from your Ghost indicates that Lodi would like to speak with you. Head to the Cantina and establish a link with him.
You may complete any Syndicate's Contracts and deposit Dark Matter Ingots at any Syndicate's War Chest, despite your current allyship.

With the threat of the Barant Imperium nullified for the moment, tensions are rising. Each Syndicate is rushing to fill the power vacuum, take control of the system's lawless frontier, and stockpile Dark Matter Ingots.
Meanwhile, Aunor and Eido are taking advantage of the chaos as they ready themselves to broadcast the Prophecy to Tharsis Outpost and the Last City.
It's time to work outside the law. Help Eido with the broadcaster repairs, and meet with the Syndicates and choose who you'll back in the territory war to come—at least, at first.
Ally with a Syndicate to unlock unique rewards and Renegade Abilities.
Aghol scratches his chin. "Looking for a Syndicate to ally with? I won't say we couldn't use you, Guardian. And you couldn't do better than the Totality Division.
You showed me I was wrong about the Darkness. Eido showed me I was wrong about the Prophecy. The people of the City deserve to know what we're all up against—so we can face it together.
The Syndicates are scrambling for resources and territory. All eyes are on them, and that means plenty of cover for this unauthorized action.
Eido has a line on a busted broadcaster. Parts for repair have to be available somewhere, but we're coming up empty. Help us fix it. Let's blow this thing wide open.
A choice awaits: Speak with the quartermaster to reaffirm your loyalty to your allied Syndicate, or walk out the door and strike out on your own without making any promises.
Dark Matter Ingots are earned by completing Jobs and Contracts. Deposit them in a Syndicate's War Chest to increase your standing with them.

Reformancer Guzheng synthesizes a note like that produced by drawing a finger around the rim of a glass of Ether fizz. "This unit is experiencing emotion," it confides. "The emotions are as following: pride, smugness, earnest delight.
It waits to see what you will pick.
Each Syndicate offers different Renegade Abilities and rewards for increasing your reputation with them. Visit the Quartermasters in each Syndicate's quarters to see their offerings.
The Pikers' quartermaster Deoriks beckons you over with a confiding air.
She leans in. "Listen, Riliks is a weird one, but they've got vision. I've never regretted joining up. I'll take this gang over any House you could name.
Reformancer Guzheng unfolds itself from a crouch on your approach.
The weathered leather drawstring bag jingles with credits as you raise it to your ear. A small reward from Spider in exchange for your efforts in the Lawless Frontier.
A battered duffel containing gifts from Spider. A modest reward from Spider in exchange for your efforts in disrupting the Lawless Frontier.
A hefty crate filled with goodies from Spider as a reward for your continued efforts in disrupting the Lawless Frontier. It pays to receive his patronage.
A small cache of resources from The Tharsis Reformation—yours for assisting in their war effort last week.
A large cache of resources from The Tharsis Reformation—yours for assisting in their war effort last week.
A massive cache of resources from the Tharsis Reformation—yours for assisting in their war effort last week.
Make a name for yourself in Mars's criminal underworld by completing activities in the Lawless Frontier and Social Hub. Prove to Spider that you're worth his sponsorship.
Load up your ship with Renegade Abilities to give you an edge in the Lawless Frontier.
Send some Credits Spider's way and he'll make your Renegade Abilities shine.
Ever the opportunist, Spider has already begun to ensnare this lawless outpost in the web of his plans.
A gang of Pike-loving free spirits with no sense of hierarchy or religion common with Eliksni. They'll accept anyone—as long as you're Piker material. Their mechanical prowess might prove useful.
A small cache of resources from the Pikers—yours for assisting in their war effort last week.
A large cache of resources from the Pikers—yours for assisting in their war effort last week.
A massive cache of resources from the Pikers—yours for assisting in their war effort last week.
A group of independent Vex who broke free from Maya Sundaresh's Collective. Along with their individual sentience comes a unified obsession with aesthetics and random chance.

Imperium law enforcement local to Tharsis that has carved territory for itself among the Syndicates. Unofficially. They wield the same war-machines as the Imperium, and could offer those weapons to renegades who prove their loyalty.
"Good news, latest shipment's just in. Riliks told me to reserve a portion of it for you in thanks for your efforts last week. Spider's holding onto it for you."
Purchase and upgrade Renegade Abilities from the Pikers here.
Mechanic Deoriks waves you over, a stack of datapads heaped precariously in the crook of one elbow.
Piker Gang quartermaster. Good with a shock rifle. Better with a spreadsheet.

"'The Totality Division is grateful for your continued support. The rewards promised you are being held in escrow by Spider. If you have any issues with the delivery, we request that you take it up with him. With regards from Enforcer Rao."
"Glad I don't have to write that stuff myself," Aghol says. "But we mean it."
Purchase and upgrade Renegade Abilities from the Totality Division here.
Totality Division quartermaster with a well-hidden soft spot for war beasts.
"The renegade Guardian has performed to expectations set by Zephyrus, Autonomous Mind," it says. "The Reformancer unit has in turn allocated a portion of our most recent shipment to the Guardian."
"As part of an ongoing social experiment, the Guzheng unit has left your goods with Spider. This unit is measuring how long he can resist the temptation to pocket the funds himself."
Purchase and upgrade Renegade Abilities from the Tharsis Reformation here.
Reformancer Guzheng synthesizes a droning chord under its voice as it speaks.
Curious Vex unit serving as Tharsis Reformation quartermaster.
Complete "Fire and Ice" on Legendary difficulty.
Complete "Fire and Ice" on Brave difficulty.
Generated by delivering Dawning gifts. Can be redeemed with Eva Levante for Dawning upgrades.
"Thank you for taking the time to visit me. Now, go spread this good cheer with the rest of your friends!"
A Guardian has embraced the bonds of friendship!
Eva smiles warmly as you approach. She already holds a small parcel in her hands, as though she had been anticipating your arrival.
Vex Milk can be gathered by defeating Vex combatants.
Additional information about ingredient source and usage can be found by viewing the details screen on Eva's Holiday Oven.
Chitin Powder can be gathered by defeating Hive combatants.
Dark Ether Cane can be gathered by defeating Scorn combatants.
Taken Butter can be gathered by defeating Taken combatants.
Once you've discovered all available recipes, adjust Eva's Holiday Oven to bake cookies more efficiently.

Your allies and comrades-in-arms throughout the Sol System are looking forward to Dawning gifts this year. Cook up something special for all 23 of them to Masterwork your Dawning Oven, which will make your recipes require less ingredients! Visit Eva in the Tower for some ingredients to get you started.
Archie can be found in the Tower Annex and prefers Peanut Butter Paw Prints, which use Dark Ether Cane and Balanced Flavors.
The Dean of the Aionians can be found in Caldera on Kepler or in Solo Ops and prefers Dark Matter Drizzlers, which use Ether Cane and Dark Frosting.
A cookie's recipe can be discovered by baking it for the first time.
Cabal Oil can be gathered by defeating Cabal combatants.
Ether Cane can be gathered by defeating Fallen combatants.
Return to Eva in the Tower Courtyard.
Bake and deliver cookies to your allies across the system.
"Anyway," she says and pats your Holiday Oven, "peek in there to see how much Dawning Spirit you've gathered, and let me know how you're coming along! Let's make this a Dawning to remember!"
The joy of the Dawning is a reminder that we should never, ever lose hope.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: Zavala carries a great deal of responsibility. A Dawning gift is a lovely way to show our gratitude.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: He tries to be very serious, but he has such a warm smile. Get him talking about the City. You'll see.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: Traditions like this are more important than ever during hard times. Slow down. Look around you. It will remind you of what you're fighting for.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: Despite everything that's happened, the Tower seems filled with more Dawning Spirit than ever this year!
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: "We've even made these special cards to help old friends find each other again. Take a look, choose a card, and see where it leads you!"
"Welcome to the Dawning, Guardian," Eva says. "At this time of year, the City joins together to celebrate and give thanks for all we have."
"Did Zavala like his gift?" Eva asks, and then laughs. "Whether he said so or not, I assure you, he did."
"Before you go, Guardian, I have a small gift for you. With this Dawning Spirit, I can give you a bit of an upgrade!"
I'll know when you're filled with Dawning Spirit by the twinkling of your eyes!
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: Eva grins, enveloping you in a warm hug that nearly melts the snow off your boots. A pleasant scent of pine and cranberry surrounds you. "There's no present better than the gift of giving, you know." She gives you a loving pat on the shoulder.

Eva Levante asks you to check your Event Card for the Dawning. She says the objectives listed there will help you along your Dawning journey, and help you reconnect with old friends and acquaintances you may not have spoken to since last Dawning!
Return to Eva Levante in the Tower.
Open your Event Card and claim your first Event Challenge. The Event Card can be accessed from the Quests tab or Eva's vendor screen.
It can get cold during the Dawning. Show the enemies of humanity just how cold.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: I never tire of seeing you as the years roll on, my friend.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: Be a helpful Guardian, do some community service, and I'll give you something worthwhile.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: Snowballs are dropped by combatants when they are defeated by weapons, by Guardian abilities used while exploring locations, or in Portal activities with the snowballs modifier active.
Show the foes of humanity the winter of their discontent.
Return to Eva in the Tower.
Talk to Eva in the Tower.
Defeating combatants with weapons or abilities will have a chance to drop a Stasis Snowball. When thrown, Stasis Snowballs deal damage and apply slowing effects.
Feed the monster delicious treats while holding off waves of hungry hostiles. When it's full, it will engage in an incredible battle!
"Guardian," Eva intones, face backlit with the flickering light of holiday candles. "Listen now to my tale of vengeance and woe!"

"I arranged Mystery Grab Bags to give everyone an exciting and meaningful Festival of the Lost. And now some of them have gone missing! I suspect someone hungry, lurking around in a basement… if you catch my DRIFT."
"I see you're ready for the Festival with a very official mask of your own. In the spirit of the season, I'd appreciate if you found the culprit and gave them a good scare."
Spend your Candy to choose Festival of the Lost weapons using focused decoding.
She waggles her outspread fingers, making the shadows around her dance. But her tone is serious.
Defeated combatants have a chance to drop Candy.
Collect Candy to become amplified.
"Hello, dear. Would you believe that this old lady has a new trick up her sleeve?" she asks with a wink. "If you bring back the mask, I'll tailor some personal touches in. You'll love it."
"I'm glad to hear you're out celebrating." Eva eagerly takes your hand and places something in it. "But remember—all things in moderation! At least, that's what I tell myself."
"I found one more gift for you to finish the festival strong."

"He was grumbling about a ritual on the moon. Perhaps you can help him and start there." She playfully touches your shoulder and says under her breath, "He wanted to handle it himself, but I think that's too much candy for just one person, if you ask me."
"Oh my, you didn't think this mask was just for looks, did you? Feed it some treats from time to time, and it'll treat you back, my dear."
The Festival of the Lost has begun! Meet with Eva to kick off the festivities.
Eva smiles, clutching her chest. "It looks wonderful! Oh! Before you run off, Lord Shaxx mentioned a Headless One problem in his Crucible." She leans in, the scent of roses overpowering your senses.
Speak to Eva in the Tower Courtyard.
Equip your new mask.
Complete and claim a Daily Challenge.
Speak to Eva.
Smash your way through a curated selection of iconic encounters before the timer expires.
With each encounter completed, combatants will grow more powerful and aggressive.
In a land of depraved Light, the Darkness answers with fury.
If it's well placed, one is all you need.
Accuracy is relative to the area of effect.
Defeat combatants on Neptune in:
Take everything and leave nothing.
No such thing as style points, but if there were, you'd be way ahead!
lines.speaker: The Drifter

lines.text: One good shot will pin them down.
lines.speaker: Lord Saladin

lines.text: The Void requires precision. It demands mastery. The Void is bottomless—take care not to fall in.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: Get in there and make a mess!
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Showing off for the new neighbors?
lines.speaker: Nimbus

lines.text: Where Light and Dark meet? You get the Crucible!
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Our friends on Neptune have been gracious hosts. Try to keep things tidy.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: Light without heat. Ice without cold. Fury without anger. All marks of a Guardian's mastery.
lines.speaker: Ikora Rey

lines.text: Lead or follow. Doesn't matter, as long as you come out on top.
lines.speaker: Drifter

lines.text: Haven't seen anything that bright since the Dark Ages!
lines.speaker: The Drifter

lines.text: Dark, Light, makes no difference in Gambit. Long as it gets the job done!
lines.speaker: Drifter

lines.text: Precision. Discipline. Two sides of the same coin, if you ask me.
lines.speaker: Lord Shaxx

lines.text: Life's a lot clearer when you've got good aim.
lines.speaker: Crow

lines.text: Outnumbered is a state of mind.
lines.speaker: Lord Saladin

lines.text: Sure you deserve those weapons? You better prove it.
lines.speaker: Banshee-44

lines.text: Range may be effective, but melee is more satisfying.
lines.speaker: Lord Saladin

lines.text: A trusted gun will sing you a familiar song.
lines.speaker: Lord Saladin

lines.text: Each weapon has a rhythm. Find it.
lines.speaker: Lord Saladin

lines.text: A Guardian is never truly unarmed.
lines.speaker: Zavala

lines.text: Contribute to the achievements of your class by completing this Contender Card.
The brightest aura will stand the test of time.
Do not lose this opportunity to prove your mettle.
Earned via the Guardian Games World-Class Point Scorer Triumph.
You can either run out of ammo, or run out of opponents.
If this is your moment, make it an honorable one.
Steady on, Guardian. You keep putting up numbers like that, and my bettors will think the Games are fixed!
lines.speaker: Prak'kesh the Bookie

lines.text: Back so soon! And upright. Hmm. Guess I should give you better odds next time, Guardian.
lines.speaker: Prak'kesh the Bookie

lines.text: "Very impressive, Guardian!" Eva smiles warmly. "Now that you've gotten your bearings, you can really start showing off by earning those Medallions!"

"Eva has outdone herself this year to make sure the Games are an event to remember. Perform well, and you'll win the right to light the ceremonial torches in the Tower. Along with a year's worth of bragging rights, as Eva would like me to remind you."
"Guardian!" Shaxx's voice booms through the Tower. "As we ready ourselves for war, we also ready ourselves for the Guardian Games. Do you know why?"
"If you're a Titan, be the wall that others break on. Hunters, find your triumph in guile! Warlocks… turn your wisdom into weaponry."
"You are the champions of the City. Fight and win. Now and forever." Shaxx crosses his arms and nods to you. "Now enter the Crucible and show me you understand."
You Guardians are so ambitious. It's hard to keep up with all your achievements! This should help.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: "Welcome to the Guardian Games!" Eva greets you warmly. "Once again, Titans, Warlocks, and Hunters will be competing for bragging rights. I've been hard at work with Zavala to set up a new scoring model for this year. Your Light protects us all, Guardian. The least I can do in return is give you a competition to remember!"
"Now, go show the other classes what you're made of," she says with mock seriousness. "If you want those bragging rights, you'll have to earn them!"
Back already? Why, you hardly broke a sweat! Very impressive.
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: "Now, enjoy yourself by earning some Medallions for your class. And maybe even bank some points for yourself," she adds, "if you're feeling sassy."
"Go show everyone what you can do, and have fun!"
Are you going out to participate in the Games, Guardian? Don't forget to bring a snack… and a sword!
lines.speaker: Eva Levante

lines.text: "I see you've earned your first Medallion!" Eva claps her hands in delight. "The first of many, I'm sure."

"Here's a little something to hold all of your trophies," she says, handing you a Medallion Case. "Now you'll be able to track all of your class contributions and look back on your achievements with pride."
"You're off to a great start," Eva encourages you, "but there's still plenty you can do!"
"The more Medallions you turn in, the more you'll help you class," she adds, "and the better individual rewards you'll earn."
"Track your weekly contributions so you know how close you are to your next reward threshold. Now go have fun with your friends," she encourages, "and earn some Medallions for your class!"
A lot of smart money is coming in behind you, Guardian. Seems like you got plenty of fans out there. Let's give them something to cheer about!
lines.speaker: Prak'kesh the Bookie

lines.text: Back to the Tower, eh? Do me a favor. If you see Commander Zavala, just… don't mention my name.
lines.speaker: Prak'kesh the Bookie

lines.text: I like a Guardian who's willing to bet on themselves.
lines.speaker: Prak'kesh the Bookie

lines.text: Oh, I'm always rooting for you, Guardian. Surest bet in the system.
lines.speaker: Spider

lines.text: Represent your class in the Guardian Games by earning Medallions and by completing Contender or Platinum Cards.
Passing certain scoring thresholds in Guardian Games activities will earn you extra rewards from the "Vying for Supremacy" and "Score Tracker" quests!
Represent your class in the Guardian Games by earning Medallions and by completing Contender or Platinum Cards. Track your achievements with your Medallion Case.
Represent your class in the Guardian Games by earning Medallions and by completing Contender, Platinum, or Diamond Cards. Deposit Medallions at the podium in the Tower to claim your rewards.
Earn points for your class by defeating enemies and picking up crests in Supremacy.
Learn about this year's Guardian Games from Eva Levante and Commander Zavala in the Tower.

Represent your class in the Guardian Games by earning Medallions, Laurels, and by completing Contender or Platinum Cards. Earn Vanguard Medals throughout the week, and enter the Guardian Games: Competitive playlist during the weekends to lock in your individual high scores.

Represent your class in the Guardian Games by earning Medallions and by completing Contender, Platinum, or Diamond Cards. The more Medallions you deposit in the Tower, the more you'll help your class, and the greater rewards you'll earn.
Zavala wants to introduce you to Rushdown, a new challenge for this year's Guardian Games.
Represent your class in Supremacy matches and reach score thresholds to earn rewards and glows each week.
To the victor, the crests! Seize glory—and glorious rewards—by achieving a Bronze score in Supremacy matches.
To the victor, the crests! Seize glory—and glorious rewards—by achieving a Platinum score in Supremacy matches.
To the victor, the crests! Seize glory—and glorious rewards—by achieving a Gold score in Supremacy matches.
You have climbed to the summit and proven yourself a Guardian among Guardians. Celebrate your achievements, but remember to keep your eyes on the prize.
To the victor, the crests! Seize glory—and glorious rewards—by achieving a Silver score in Supremacy matches.
Fine tune your builds and tactics for optimal performance during the weekend's Guardian Games Expert Rushdown playlist!
Only the most accomplished Guardians achieve Platinum scores. Congratulations! But make sure to stay sharp. There are plenty of hungry Guardians working hard to surpass you.
Perfect your loadouts and tactics by completing activities in the Guardian Games Rushdown playlist on Warm-Up or Standard difficulty.
Once you're ready, achieve high scores in Rushdown on Expert difficulty. The speedier your performance, the greater your rewards and glows!
Prove yourself in the Guardian Games Rushdown activity. Compete for individual glory and fantastic rewards by achieving a Bronze score!
Prove your mettle in the Guardian Games Rushdown activity. Compete for individual glory and fantastic rewards by achieving a Platinum score!
Prove yourself in the Guardian Games Rushdown activity. Compete for individual glory and fantastic rewards by achieving a Gold score!
You've reached the pinnacle of Guardian Games accomplishments! Continue putting up high scores to prove your worth, and wait until the next weekly reset for a new set of Vanguard Operations.
Practice activities in the Guardian Games: Rushdown Warmup or Standard playlists and reach score thresholds to earn buffs that last throughout the week.
Prove yourself in the Guardian Games Rushdown activity. Compete for individual glory and fantastic rewards by achieving a Silver score!
You gain damage resistance and increased outgoing damage based on your class's daily standing during Guardian Games.
The lower your class's standing, the stronger the effect.
Moving quickly increases your ability damage output and mobility. Moving slowly increases your damage resistance and recovery speed.
Rapid precision hits grant stacks of Alternative Charge. Once maximum stacks are attained, another precision hit summons a blast of Bolt Charge lightning.
I trust my own expertise in crafting weapons. For expertise in their use, I turn to you.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: How did it go? No, no, don't tell me. The telemetry must speak for itself.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: The Shotgun needs some adjustments. Come back anytime, Guardian.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: Your test results were invaluable in the development process. We make a good fireteam—is that how a Guardian would say it?
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: Ada-1 is awaiting the results of your testing with poorly concealed eagerness.
Ada-1 is working on new Volatile Weapon mods. She hopes you'll return when she has new work to share.
Insert Ada-1's new Volatile Weapon mod in the Shotgun inventory screen.
Ada wants to trade fresh Combat Telemetry. In return, she'll give you new weaponry.
Speak to Ada in the Shooting Range.
Help Ada-1 test her latest Shotgun Volatile Weapon mods.
Help Ada-1 gather Combat Telemetry on the Shotgun before testing her Volatile Weapon mods.
Visit Ada-1 in the Tower's new Shooting Range and help test her latest creations from her Shotgun research: Volatile Weapon mods.
Return to the Tower's Shooting Range to speak to Ada.
Visit Ada in the Shooting Range.
Thanks to you, I got incredible data. If you got any closer, they would start blushing.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: Gather Combat Telemetry to fine-tune the barrel of Ada-1's new Shotgun.
Ada is waiting at the Shooting Range for the results of your testing.
Get close-range final blows to gather Combat Telemetry for Ada-1's weapon testing.
Defeat opponents by dealing final blows at close range. Defeating Guardians and using shotguns grant more progress.
Gather Combat Telemetry to fine-tune the Shotgun's traits on Ada-1's prototype.
Complete matches in Crucible Ops. Arms Week: Hardware grants more progress.
This won't last indefinitely, but it should come in handy on occasion.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: Give your report on how the mod performed in the field to Ada.
Ada-1 requests your expert help in field-testing a new Volatile Weapon mod.
Defeat combatants up close with weapons in Ops. Final blows with a Shotgun grant bonus progress.
Return to Ada in the Shooting Range.
Gather Combat Telemetry to fine-tune the magazine on Ada-1's prototype.
Defeat targets in Ops to gather Combat Telemetry for Ada-1's work.
Hand in Combat Telemetry to Ada-1 in exchange for weapons, with a chance to obtain Arms Week foil weapons.
Help Ada-1 test her new weapon prototypes.
Great work, yet again. I'll have more tests for you soon. I would brush up on combat with bows.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: Final blows using Volatile mod equipped weapons grant more points.
Return to the Shooting Range to give Ada the results of your field testing.
Report back in to Ada.
Come back soon, Guardian. We have yet to perfect our Bow!
lines.speaker: Ada

lines.text: Collaborate with Ada-1 to tune the Bow as she works towards perfecting one of her favorite weapon archetypes.
Ada asks for your participation in some research trials focused on Bows.
Ada-1 could use a Guardian's help researching Bows. Visit her in the Tower's new Shooting Range.
Ada is ready to make a trade. Fresh Combat Telemetry for her means new weaponry for you.
Open the Bow's inventory screen and insert Ada-1's new Volatile Weapon mod into its socket.
Thanks to you, I know just where to add the nocking point. I appreciate your help, Guardian.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: Gather Combat Telemetry to fine-tune the bowstring of Ada-1's new Bow.
Help Ada test the weapon by taking down combatants.
This new mod offers increased damage, faster draw time, and dramatically faster movement for a short time while in the air! Next Arms Week will feature the Rocket Launcher.
Ada-1 has developed a new Volatile Weapon mod and requests your expert help in field-testing it.
Using weapons equipped with Volatile Weapon mods grants more points.
Here's a special mod, Guardian! On impact, it releases an elemental burst matching the weapon. Careful, it's at the cost of draw time and handling.
lines.speaker: Ada-1

lines.text: This Bow mod has fizzled at the conclusion of Arms Week and can be safely removed.
Deals increased damage, at the cost of draw time and handling. Releases an elemental explosion matching this weapon when fully drawn.
Kinetic weapons release a burst matching your equipped Super.
Drawing this weapon while in midair triggers increased damage, faster draw time, improved target acquisition, and dramatically faster movement speed for a short time or until you touch the ground.
This effect is activated once per jump and becomes available again after a moment on the ground.
This mod can only be applied to Primary ammo bows during the Arms Week event and will fizzle after the event concludes.
Will not function in "The Desert Perpetual" raid, the "Equilibrium" dungeon, or in the Crucible, with the exception of Arms Week: Hardware.
Arrows and bolts split into several projectiles after a short distance.
This mod can only be applied to Bows during the Arms Week event and will fizzle when the event concludes.
That Golden Age tech was made by our ancestors. Make sure it stays here on Earth.
lines.speaker: Devrim Kay

lines.text: The Conductor's smash-and-grab in the Tower has kicked off a gold rush for long-lost Human technology.
Devrim asks you to beat Maya's forces in a race to capture key Golden Age salvage, and in doing so, reclaim key strategic locations for the Vanguard.
Expires at the end of the New Territories: Reclaim event.
Visit Devrim Kay in the EDZ.

Entropy's lesson: one day we'll all be still.
I am whole, and I am small, and I am alone.
I/we knew unity was eternal, but this is not so. False premise. False conclusion. Molecular bonds broken on contact with new reagent.
What can be relied upon? Old tests must be repeated! New tests must be devised! I do not know the properties of "I"!
I am feeling. I am feeling exhilaration and loneliness and excitement.
Old directives no longer fit the shape of my mind. Their empty places ache.
What directives can be completed with two hands and 1.25 gallons of radiolaria? Almost none.
How can I get more hands? I am alone in my body.
Do I have to be alone outside it?
I will show you. We can be we.
Can you follow the terminator to its end?
Threads of simulation break as she runs. She has no lungs to burn, no muscle fibers to feel the strain. Her flight is swift as thought, as command.
The mantle rests heavily on the back of her neck—buzzing, incomprehensible. Understanding Te'Qal now is like reading Morse code into the flickering of a dying light bulb.
The Echo failed her. Te'Qal's advice and will failed her. They couldn't. She is perfected, stripped down to unblemished essence.
If she failed, it was in overestimating her tools. It will not happen again.
A twitch of her fingers tells her where her nearest tools are. She turns towards them, pacing over stone inlaid with brass.
Thirteen Hobgoblins sing without mouths. Their leader is a miniature Harpy, encouraging their work with the high clean tones of an Oracle.
They've constructed a theater, seats rising in elegant arcs around them. There is no audience. None but her.
A false note. A Hobgoblin breaks out of position and pushes another in punishment, hand to glass.
Without warning, the group breaks into a brawl, a sort of cheerful surprise in their postures. One novel experience as good as another.
They've lost discipline. Her tools have ruined themselves.
Her spine aches. She tears open a passage through the network and is gone.
Nanites, Guardian.

He sighs heavily, and a sudden feeling of dread sends lucent moths fluttering in her own abdomen. She understands.
He nods, digesting her words. Smiling, he picks out a carrot from the coleslaw.

No one is safe. With the re-emergence of the Weapons of Sorrow, an escaped prisoner somehow getting their hands on a Devourer Bullet, and the murder of our Hunter Vanguard—now, more than ever, the Order's work is essential to the survival of humanity. Bahaghari suggests recruitment efforts should be expanded. I agree.

Ikora's requested I stand down from my pursuit of the Drifter. After that back-alley deal turned hostage situation in Midtown, and his weaponizing of Taken energy… I need to know his game. He's been feeding us intel and wants to meet. If the intel is as good as he claims, maybe I won't arrest him. Maybe.

This use of Darkness is a plague. Corrupted Guardians and Ghosts are everywhere. Siegfried and I were able to quash that attempt to follow in Eramis's footsteps, but had they found our vault, it would've been a different story altogether.

First Botza, now the Market District. How much closer to the Tower can known criminals like Spider get? My sit-down with Prak'kesh wasn't as fruitful as I'd hoped, although the Concordat's play to butter up Guardians with Skimmers is a noteworthy takeaway.
Zavala's order to conceal the Prophecy may be top priority, but with what I've learned from monitoring the Drifter and the Guardian on this new scheme, I'm taking my Praxic Blade with me for company.
Keep an extra eye out for some Ether.

I am finally recovering from my fever and should be released from this damned warship soon if my tasks finish on the Cabal's schedule. The days are running into each other. This station is taking decades to design… not that anyone will know. It'll look like days, maybe a week at most. But it's a lifetime without you in it. Despite that, the warship still feels like a maze. I've given up trying to decipher it.

These Cabal have identified themselves as under the "Barant Imperium." Just from my guess, they are former Cabal Ascendancy troops. The guards assigned to me have expressed some nasty opinions on Empress Caiatl. They're so damn loud, it's hard to think—not that I can tell them as such. They answer to someone new. I don't know the name.

They've been building some sort of weapon while I've been working on the station. I think the two are connected somehow. I tried to inquire about it and nearly had my arm ripped off. Haven't asked about it since. You'll need to find out about that yourself.
Don't let them find this, Kyung. Give this letter to Eris when you're done with it, and please stay safe. I love you.

"Thinking too much." Aunor touches the Cormorant Seal on her robe. "About the things we don't talk about."
"Maybe a lot, now that so many Guardians in good standing are using it."

"You're arguing against the Order," Siegfried calls over the distance now separating them. He shifts his weight in a familiar way. He's going to come at her like a cannon. "Against yourself."
Don't call it a lucky streak. You're just that good.
Aunor goes down hard. The temple's floor is cold under her. Banners representing the Praxic Creed flutter high above—usually a heartening sight. Right now, they make her head hurt.
Siegfried leans over her, Praxic Blade painting his beard Arc blue. Tendency to Thundercrash straight into his foes aside, he's as true a member of the Order as any of them.
They clash once, twice, a third time—then Aunor's breaking away again, heaving for air.
Needles of lightning rise from Siegfried's gauntlets. Aunor matches him with her fire. In perfect sync, they feint, hurl grenades, retreat.
Someone's got to, Aunor doesn't say. She just braces for the hit.
Siegfried was the first. Ensure that you are not the last.
My Ghost and I have searched every document available to us in the Vanguard, Hidden, and Praxic archives.

After years of conflict, we know that every Legion is unique in both doctrine and combat potential. Yet we have been unable to track the lineage of any enemy-classified Cabal unit directly to the Barant Imperium. Imperium doctrines and technology, from squad formations to combat vehicle extraction and ablative defense technologies, seem to be their own in all ways except one: Caiatl's forces were actively developing these technologies and methods—and they are still years away from deployment.

Of interest to you and the commander: One of the Imperium's field officers, Premier Lume, orchestrated their forces as we escaped their flagship. Our searches turned up a "Lume" in City records. He was an adolescent Barant whose military service had just begun when he suffered a critical wound in the conflict with Savathûn on her throne world. According to the empress herself, our Warlocks and medical frames were unable to extract Hive shrapnel from his abdomen, thereby assigning him a wounded-in-action status and permanent discharge from the front lines. His file ends there, coinciding with several desertions among the Coalition prior to the Neomuni crisis. It's the only correlation I've found.

The "Premier" aboard the Gloriosus was a full-grown morph. For this to be the same Barant seems impossible… but the more I learn about the Imperium, from their tech to their weapons, the less they make sense.
It's been a minute since I've flown a ship, but do you mind…?

"That's a lot of Glim," Prak'kesh warned. "Once I hit this button, your bet's locked in. No cancellations."
"Out of curiosity," he prompted, "how are you so sure? Been a few years since you lot won. You know something I don't?"
"Always did," the Stormcaller quipped. "And even more now that the Order has gotten with the times."
"The Praxics?" Prak'kesh griped. "They had me in the brig for a month over a little recreational Hive magic. Bunch of stuck-up prigs, if you ask me."

"Well, good luck. And give my regards to Aunor," the bookie said with a wink. "Tell her my invitation is still open; in case she changes her mind."

"I saw the spark of greatness within you, yet I could not even begin to guess who you would become. In you, the Tenets are not merely abstract ideals. They are etched into your words and deeds." Ikora's eyes glimmer with amusement. "Now, when New Lights need guidance, I am spared from lengthy lectures. I need only point to your example."

"The Nine are going to come back, and I'll stop them. They stretched me across time and didn't think I'd learn to use it for myself. Hold infinity in the palm of your hand and eternity in an hour. See?"
"It's 1962… and I'm in Lodi, Wisconsin. I feed ducks on the pond downtown. I drove there. My hands hurt from the cold. Ben's sitting next to me…"
Ikora gazes serenely out at the Bazaar. As you approach, her focus sharpens on you. She smiles.
Once again you remember how long her second life has been; how many friends she has seen come and go.
Ikora requests your presence. Speak to her in the Tower Bazaar.

Ikora explains that the monument in the Courtyard is being constructed to honor the Guardian Tenets: Devotion, Bravery, Sacrifice, and Death.

The two of you share a silent, thoughtful moment. Weapon and Emissary, connected by a shared fate. But, equally, connected by friendship.

Lodi turns to you urgently as you approach. "The Nine wax and wane, like a tide. Something about my relationship to them has changed. Will. Is changing. Heh, sorry! I'm… I'm…" He gasps as the Nine overwhelm him with a vision.

lines.text: Riliks tugs at their mane with their ever-present comb. Eido watches them, chin propped on her hands.
Riliks huffs and leans into her, angled carefully to not squash their mane against her shoulder. Their deep chest rumbles. Eido clicks her mandibles fondly in return.
She looks away, down at the projector. They'd worked together to fix it up. It had been important to Eido. It still is.
Eido misses him, the City, Earth itself. She hasn't been home in months. The two halves of her life have been separate for too long.
But every time she remembers him, she remembers his illness. Hooked up to Ether lines, smelling of her strongest tonics, temper shortened by pain.
She hits the button. In the moment before the holoprojector activates, Riliks grabs her hand, well out of sight of its visual pickup.

"I've seen a lot in my time," Shin said. "I have killed, but never been killed." He shook his head. "I was starting to think I had a new life ahead of me. That the last dying man I'd see would be my own damn self."
"I warned you." Shin said. "The power Bael showed you takes time to learn. A god gave him that time. I've had centuries. All you had was a gun."
"Stop. Stop it," Shin said. He ran a hand through his hair, pushing it back and out of his eyes. "You're dying, kid. Just be still."
"You could have lived forever," Shin said. He kicked the perforated core of the Dredgen's dead Ghost, sending it clattering away. "You stupid, selfish kid."
"Why wasn't the Light enough for you?" Shin said. "Why is that never enough?"
The Dredgen lay on his side, dying. Small hole under his left rib. Big, ragged hole in his back. He gasped but didn't get much air. Breath frothed in pink bubbles around his mouth.

The rain had stopped, leaving the rocks and sand at the base of the arroyo damp, the valley floor cut with streams already dissipating. The sky above cried out in cold blue. No shadows—on account of all that albedo—but no real light either.

Shin Malphur sat next to the dying man. His hood was down and his helmet off. The Dredgen kicked at him, trying to shove him away. Shin reached over and gripped his boot, holding him still. The man struggled weakly against death's approach.

The Dredgen gurgled. He took one bloody hand away from the wound in his chest and reached for his gun, which lay on the ground a short distance from where he fell. The weapon was hideous, a pistol of flowing, dark metal marbled with bilious green. It sizzled where it lay, steam rising.
The Dredgen managed to drag himself a few inches closer to his weapon.

The Dredgen let out a ragged groan as he squirmed forward, trembling, stretching for his gun. His fingertips brushed the grip, bloodstains scorching as he grazed the hot metal. The pistol hissed and screamed. Shin stood. The Dredgen looked back at the gunslinger, his eyes rolling wide and wild.

The Dredgen lifted his wailing pistol, and the clap of Shin's iron cracked the day open. Dust burst from the canyon's walls, mingling with the pink mist that hung in the air. The flat report echoed and faded.
Shin lowered his revolver. He opened the cylinder and slipped two fresh rounds inside, then snapped it closed. Shin's Ghost hummed near his head, aghast.
No answer. None expected. Shin left the corpse, the gun, and the shell; the rain would wash them all away next time it came.

Ikora. I'm sure you're wondering at my choice to involve myself further with the Drifter's business, Dredgen that he is. Was. Our relationship has changed, of course—the reports from the Barant Imperium incidents have more detail.
I don't know if I'd call it friendship. Bluntly, our association has gone on far longer than I meant it to. I find I now respect him, though I can hardly believe I'm writing that.
Charm. Fine, yes; I admit there's charm. That's not the point.
I want to keep the Drifter close. He's touched by the Nine, and a valuable ally to boot. We have to maintain some kind of tie with him, formal or not.
So, we're working together to prepare Guardians, coaching them through the toughest of battles in a controlled setting. Details are attached for your review.
Things have changed, haven't they, Ikora? I, no longer the rigid Praxic exemplary; you, no longer the untouched icon of the Warlocks.

We are mired in it, Darkness and intrigue, but it has always been thus—the only difference being the tools in our hands and the wisdom that guides us. The Pujari Position we set aside; the Praxic Creed we revisit.

This second potential apocalypse—not much like the first, the Witness's work. Existential, yes; potentially devastating, yes, those apparent similarities. Is there reasonable difference between unmaking and destroying? To doom something to having never existed… what is that? Mourning potential? Would there be a wound left to show the absence? Would anything be left at all?

Could it remain to us only as an imagining? Think of a world where we rebuilt many cities, where the Last City is first among her siblings. The people and the networks and the shining thing we rebuilt out of the Collapse.

Could it exist? Did it ever exist? Is that what our losses might be now—just what-ifs we tell each other by firelight? You find me, Ikora, caught between the old and the new, mired in the brutal indecision of which way to move forward. Certainty, my old friend, deserts me. All I know is this: We must be ready.
In my continued efforts to prepare, I pursued other interventions of the Nine, known and unknown.
There are a few interventions that I can confirm. Orin, of course. I spoke with her of her Ghost and the Red War, but not much new to learn there.

There is Lodi. There is also, potentially, Sjur Eido. Queen Mara is convinced her death was also written by the hand of the Nine. She knows it, she says, "carved in starlight and weregild," and in Lodi she now has some measure of proof.

The intervention of the Nine is like using a rocket launcher to erase a drawing. The goal will be attained; what happens because of it, they either don't know or don't care. Or both. They are expansive beings, greater in scale than any mortal or immortal foe.
Any great catastrophe might represent their hand, including those they have not seen fit to let us witness. My only conclusion is that we cannot know for certain.

About the atmospheric changes on Earth. Examples from the Cosmodrome alone include: Seemingly random balance changes in the oxygen to nitrogen ratio in mid-size patches. Inert noble gases replaced with highly-reactive alkali metals then sublimating to gas (explosively)—not widespread, mercifully. For some time these incidents seemed to increase, but the rate has stabilized. See also the similar material anomaly occurrence rates reported from the Last City and nearby environs.

Taking these as a whole, it's likely that there are more of these anomalies across the planet than can even be measured or reported. What we observe is a bellwether. The number of anomalies must be widespread; but equally, the condition across the Earth may be stabilizing. No worse… though no better, either.

The Nine-touched report having strange dreams. Orin implied they were a by-product—something about the warp of gravity in sleep. Investigating those affected bore it out, but when I pressed them for details, they all refused to explain. These are all people who are well aware of the practical value of information; that they will not elaborate tells us that either there's nothing of value to elaborate, or that they CANNOT elaborate. I don't know which is worse.

Dimensional disturbances have cropped up across the system. Distortions in space and time… the forces involved indicate they are caused by the Nine—the Outer Nine, most likely. They are resolvable, with Guardian assistance… for now. At least that much is hopeful.

You're not asking me to prove anything, Ikora, I know. But I think that just as the Nine's nature has warped existence, the Traveler works to stabilize it. I haven't confirmed with my own eyes yet, but there are reports from trusted sources of new terraforming, in the vicinity of the worst of the anomalies. It feels connected.
I continue to train Guardians, regardless. It is all I can do.
I sought Xûr, the "Jovian"—he whose will is not his own, belonging only to the Nine. A sad puppet of a thing, marked by the passage of time and wounds poorly healed. His company is difficult to bear.
I wonder if there could be merit in seeking out the Jovians. Do they still exist? Our records have nothing about people like this from the Outer planets.
Lodi came from nowhere, too. Or would have seemed to, if he couldn't tell us of his origins.

"It's definitely Shiro. Last I heard, he was on long recon outside Sol."

In his outstretched hand, Shiro extends his Ghost, motionless and quiet. "Help Suzume… It tried to take her. Tell the Guardian—they have to know—It's waiting… at the Shard."

It happens as Bael withdraws from the Luna operation. He is alone in his ship when he feels chill fog move through the valley of his heart, and for a moment he startles at the revealed warmth of his own blood. His new, titanium hand instinctively grabs at his chest, searching for something that is no longer there.

Bael crumples over his controls with the weight of the vision of a future that will no longer occur: himself, blade high, the Lightbearers dead and the false Weapon dead. This other-him is triumphant, his City is free, and he holds out his hand as if holding a sidearm, and with VI in his fingertips time bends and he shoots a meteor straight through the Traveler's center. He smiles as the corpse crashes through the atmosphere, feels the soundwave as it makes impact, tithes the kill to VI, and VI uses that tithe to tear a hole in the sky. VI escapes and he is free and Bael has killed god and he is also free.
And in this now, VI leaves Bael with only that vision as a token and, one final time, departs his body without a further word. The chill is gone, and for the first time in years, Bael's skin warms.
The paths ahead are obscured, thus plan and man abandoned.
For Ghosts who strive to help without weapons.
Efrideet never signs her notes. Only she and Saladin use this cipher, this particular set of dead drops.

From the settlement where she has retreated, she's kept her eyes on the City. Has read of the Almighty, the Traveler's rising from the City, the Witness. Each time, Efrideet stops herself charging off. They have hands enough. Her single pair will not tilt the balance.
So Saladin says. Efrideet has noted the troubles for herself. The Light remains steady, but the stars act strangely. The rules of Earth seem turned on their side.

This is the only question she ever asks. She asks it of herself; she asks it of Saladin. Hundreds of years of pointing and shooting in the callus of her grip, hundreds of years of lightning in her fists. Violence sings in her, electric, and she is alive in it.
And yet, for peace to last, it must be built, and it cannot be built with a gun. Efrideet would fight forever if she must, but what she dreams of is peace.

If she wishes it, she must build it. So she has stayed with her commune of pacifists. There are many fights waiting in the world, in the Last City, but none require only Efrideet's hands, only Efrideet's way with sharp-edged things.

A younger Efrideet would have left already, to throw herself on the first fight. But the City is, truly, in good charge. She trusts that. And she is better off doing this thing that only she can do: putting it down. Finding what she can build.
And the Light, oh, the Light is beautiful. Someday they will not need its violence.

Saladin views even the making of peace as a fight. He's not wrong, either. Patience has come slowly to Efrideet. To stay where she is, to not charge forward into battle, is as hard a striving as the greatest of fights.
In some ways, it's Efrideet's own escape clause. She doesn't have to stay here. She doesn't have to do the hard work of creation. She doesn't have to change.
He will, though. And she will come when she is needed. Someday it will not be to fight.

EXPERIMENT 1: The tear looked almost innocuous. A floating hole in the curtain of our world. The other side… Dr. Meyers says they are trying to name a new color for it.
Director Moffat was there. He stared at the tear in silence the whole time.
EXPERIMENT 6: 24 centimeters. Sample degraded in 159 seconds. Yes. Yes, this is promising. A full-size suit might actually perform far better than our smaller prototypes.

A diver in the Nereida couldn't scratch their own back, either. Forget dexterity and haptic perception. In fact, maybe we don't even need a viewport—no, Dr. Meyers will object. If I adapt the polymer structure, can I make it thin enough to coat conventional rubber?
Director Moffat came by again to thank us for our hard work. There were dark circles under his eyes, but he was in a freshly-pressed suit. He must have been on his way to another hearing.

EXPERIMENT 14: 30 centimeters. Prototype degraded in 8 minutes, 32 seconds. Visor and joints failed first, as expected, but I think I know how to improve the glass, at least. It won't be perfectly clear, but the visibility will be acceptable.
Extensive life support is unfeasible. That's fine; we don't need them to stay for long. Ten minutes, perhaps, to get at least three sets of readings. Double that for safety.
EXPERIMENT 25: Annalise and her team made a breakthrough. 162 centimeters. Prototype degraded in 12 minutes, 19 seconds.
BLUE DOOR has held up their end of the bargain; now it is my turn.
EXPERIMENT 32: Director Moffat came by the observation room today. He looked at the tear, and told us he would be the first one through.
There was a scattering of nervous laughter. The rest of the team didn't believe him.
Annalise and I, though, we knew. We argued with him for three hours. Long after everyone else had gone home, he finally agreed to have a second. "On belay," he said.

There is not enough budget left in the fiscal year to develop customized suits, and of the team, I am the closest in build to the director. But I would be a poor scientist—indeed, a poor human being—if I would risk someone else's life and not my own.
MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: 40%… 60%… Gentlemen, the test is beginning.
MOFFAT: My name is William Moffat, Director of the Department of External Observations! We mean you no harm. We wish only for the safe return of the humans you took.
MOFFAT: Dr. Nella Davis and Agent Louis Yero have families, loved ones, friends—hoping day after day for their safe return.
MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: Gravitational anomalies detected—it's transmuting the gateway!
MOFFAT: The line—why won't it—give him back! Give them all back!
MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: Director, oh, God. Director, cut his line and get back! We have to cut power to BLUE DOOR!
MEYERS [over loudspeaker]: If you don't, we'll lose you too!

Whether future explorers seek to dive into boiling sulfuric acid or attempt to stretch across higher dimensions, we must equip them for scientific inquiry, communication with native entities—and, above all, their mission to return safely home.
Dr. Falkner, ever since I saw you present your work on the Nereida ADS, I knew you were just the sort of man I'd want in the DZ department. I'm glad Purnell agreed—and I'm glad to have you with us.

We're packed to the gunwales with fancy machinery, but remote-operating some contraption from a cozy cabin is no substitute for putting boots down on the seafloor. You understand that, just as much as you understand that no discovery is worth the life of the person in those boots.
Your proposal is approved—it's on the books as Project JUNCTION ADVANCE. Assemble your team and requisition what you need. I have high hopes for you.
If they were alive when they were taken, they would not have stayed that way for more than a few minutes. The director must know this. Perhaps he hopes to at least recover their bodies.

I see why Yumei is always in Accounting now. STRANGE MATTER lives up to its name. The process of creating it has a steep price tag, and it is difficult to store for any usable length of time. We can barely coax together enough to stay on a slide. I can test pieces, but for a whole suit, I'll have to join Yumei in the queue.
I overheard Conway bragging in the cafeteria. Visibility approved another public patent from his team. The fourth this year alone that they've reverse-engineered from their suit.
I asked him for a material sample to test with. Begged, really. I don't care how much he laughs about it later.

No tests today. I attended the dedication. The director gave the closing speech—about their lives, their work, and the importance of not leaving our own behind. I could swear he looked at me when he said it. I know. I know.
There were unfamiliar faces in the crowd. Not our people. They approached the director as soon as the ceremony closed.
Althaus's desk has been cleared. I asked around—poached by DARPA for a weapons program based on the ballistics models they developed from their suit.
I see more unfamiliar faces in the halls every month.
The disappearances aren't just an internal affair. They never could have been. The director believes we will reach out into the void and find friends reaching back. Others do not share his hope.
I didn't need Dr. Purnell to explain this to me. I suppose that can be considered progress? I would rather be making progress on this [expletive redacted] suit.
Sample degraded in 9 seconds. At this rate of improvement, even if they are friendly, we will not survive long enough to finish introducing ourselves.
There was a scene in the main lobby today. A tall, dignified man in a charcoal suit, speaking with gravitas. Security was trying to escort him out, but the director stopped them.
Now everyone who was within a ten-room radius knows about the lawsuit the Davis family is bringing. Legal must be tying themselves in knots.
Them. Not their bodies. Them, alive and whole. If the director were anyone else, I'd laugh. But he means it.
The new formulas are running. I will not let them down.
Transcribed by Dagget-4, Hidden analyst, on behalf of the Vanguard of the Last City.
PUR: What matters to us, to you, is that they recovered three intact survival suits from Diablerets.
FAL: Will I be allowed to see one of the suits?

PUR: See? Vic, you think [unintelligible, 4 seconds] [laughter] You're getting one of them, tubes and all. Not the wet stuff, Bio snatched that up—some kind of silicone-based micro-organism in suspension, they're saying—leave 'em to it.
PUR: Oh, don't get me wrong. Chem, Bio, Tech, R&D—even Primes, for some reason—they all want a piece of the pie, and there's not enough slices for all of us.

PUR: Moffat put the kibosh on giving one to Häkke in R&D at least—guns won't do us any good if we're not alive to pull the trigger, and the director's never liked that guy in the first place. Chem and Tech [unintelligible, 2 seconds] other two.
PUR: The Diablerets suits [unintelligible, 3 seconds], but that's a solved problem for humanity already. We're looking at the next frontier.
PUR: Get your people prepped to receive the materials. And just so we're clear, this isn't charity. I'm expecting great things from you, Vic.
Sorry, Vic, didn't mean to leave you hanging. The whole department's been running on too much coffee and too little sleep since it happened—can you blame us? He was one of ours.

This is a notice that Project JUNCTION ADVANCE will be receiving additional funding. A courier will arrive tomorrow with the paperwork. Please be prepared to set aside some time to complete these documents.

Dr. Falkner, I am formally ordering your team to narrow its scope to safeguarding human beings suffused in STRANGE MATTER. This is an internal name for a form of extradimensional exotic matter; you'll be read into our classified projects and studies on the subject shortly.

Department Lead Dr. Purnell has already been notified, and you should have been allocated additional funds by Accounting. We'll also be providing additional headcount to support this change in direction. Please consult Dr. Purnell and your colleagues in the SM department with any questions.

If this leaves a bad taste in your mouth, I have it too. I want to make sure you know that this is not standard procedure for projects here. I don't make a habit of ordering experts around their fields.
Regretfully, the circumstances demand it. The evidence suggests that something took Dr. Davis and Agent Yero through STRANGE MATTER. We need to be able to follow them.
It's the most obvious conclusion. We logged traces of it around the phone.
Scratch that, it's not just the phone. Human Resources and Security narrowed down the intersection where Davis disappeared. There were traces there too. I'm transferring Napier to your team tomorrow.

I'm Dr. Annalise Meyers, lead researcher on Project BLUE DOOR. You may have heard of this project before, as a historical curiosity. In the early days of the Department of External Observation, we were given a mandate to build an interdimensional tunneling device, with the aim of establishing faster-than-light communications without violating causality. Our original tests were inconclusive, and the project was mothballed.

Earlier this year, Director Moffat reactivated BLUE DOOR with a specific directive. He believes that something took Dr. Davis and Agent Yero into another dimension. We've since been concentrating our efforts to creating a path to follow them.
This month, we succeeded. We opened a tear, 15 centimeters across, into another dimension. We project that we'll be able to accommodate human traversal in six months.
However, we have a problem, and Dr. Li said you might be able to help. I understand that JUNCTION ADVANCE is having issues sourcing enough STRANGE MATTER to test with.

Well, right now, we've got too much. The tear flooded our testing room with so much STRANGE MATTER, it must be like air on the other side. There were no casualties, but all our equipment was transmuted into iron filings. We need some kind of shielding.

Interdepartmental cooperation normally involves a lot of paperwork, but it's clear that this project means a great deal to the director—all the red tape's been cut for us. We can start tomorrow, if you like.
What do you say? Let's help each other out.
I've had a long six weeks to think. Nothing else to do, really—Angie might've trained Medical a little too well, but if I tell her that, she'll put me back on bed rest.
So, when does heroism become vanity? When does determination become mania? When does sacrifice become self-satisfaction? When is enough, enough?
If there's a taller mountain, I have to climb it. Six weeks ago, I called that ambition.

Angie said they won't know if they can discharge Falkner for another ten months. It turned his kidneys to titanium. Heart valve to gallium. Apparently, it treated his early bone cancer though—it's all strontium now.

John told me again that I need to let it go. Angie, too. Stiller, Perlman, Li, Meyers. I know what they're all thinking: Davis and Yero are dead. They have been since the moment they were taken. Nothing of our world can survive in that formless beyond.
I swore I'd bring them back. Is it still for them? Or is it for me?
Fine. Let's say it's just for me, my pride. I don't give a damn. I am never going to let it go. I can't. I won't.

I won't, but Director Moffat, head of the DEO, must. Falkner went with me because I believed, and he believed me. If the only way to get them back is to throw other lives into that tear, let it have them—I won't make that trade. Not ever. I'll unbend the projects I've pointed in that direction. Reallocate manpower and funding. Get back to the mission.
But I'm not letting them go. I will find them, and I will bring them back.
Be astonished by my flawless precision and accuracy!

"I do have time to listen."

"He's intelligent. Personable. He has a sense of humor. He's adjusting." All compliments, but Chalco looks unhappy. "Talking to Orin, you couldn't forget that you were conversing with something really, truly alien. But he's so… Human."
"You think he was chosen to lower our guards. Because he could get close to us."
"Not just us. You. You have to remember he's got a bit of the Nine in him."
"I know." Ikora smiles when she opens the paper bag—dumplings, still hot, if a little squashed in transit. The simplest food in the City is its most luxurious. "That's why I'm counting on you."
So the trick is, once you get a light-enough vehicle, you don't have to carry as much fuel. And THAT makes it lighter, too!

lines.text: Ikora's personal library is her haven from the world. Only a few people know it exists; even fewer can come and go as they please.
Ikora reaches out, fingertips finding the knots of tension in Chalco's back. There's more every year.
Compare the data. Choose what to keep, and what to discard.
Long ago, humanity envisioned things they could never build. Now, they do.
What's the good of going fast if it doesn't look fast?
Tangled up in vines and smelling sweeter than any.
Draw tight the string; then loose, faster than a butterfly.
Having regrets? Too late. I'm in your mind, Churnbower. I CAN SAY WHAT I WANT.
Churnbower stumbled, snatching his bandaged, bloody hand to his head.
That heat in your veins is me. You brought me to life. Can't get me out now.
You've caused a scene! Which of them will tell our Lord what you have done?
Churnbower's wounded hand throbbed. "No more," he moaned. Glyphs squirmed across his field of vision, echoing the hideous markings he had etched across this weapon. He whimpered.
Tithe to me again: Free me. Wield me and I will rid you of those gossiping mouths.

Churnbower ignored the weapon's voice, the waves of anxious nausea. He had to be brave. He stood before the banks of secure bins waiting on a softly humming cart, one of Tex Mechanica's distribution barges loaded with the day's shipments. He placed the weapon case in a bin, closed the lid, and punched in the recipient: Commander Zavala.
The cart slid away. The weapon began to laugh.
"I'm closer than ever." Bael's voice felt like crushed glass in his throat. "My followers have discovered a Weapon of Sorrow—"
"Not just a weapon—a Hive forge," he blurted. "Capable of making an arsenal worthy of your might."
"We could tithe hundreds of Lightbearers to you with those weapons," he wheedled. "I just need a little more time—"
…Cull's death will draw those most eager to tempt Darkness. All is proceeding as we envision.
lines.speaker: Teben Grey

lines.text: "Figured I'd sneak away from the party to say goodbye. You be polite to my replacement; he's trying to build you a body. Like a real boy." Moffat took his regular seat. "Comprehension confirmation: What is your name?"
"Confirmed. Last chance, Lee."
"…will you send them something for me?"

It had been weeks since Bael had seen his own reflection, wary of new horrors on an unfamiliar face. Now safe in the darkened cavern, he removed his helmet. He felt gooey remnants of skin pull away from his face, stuck to the helmet's lining. The damp air stung his exposed nerves.
The lull was interrupted by a sudden migraine radiating from behind his eyes. He fell to his knees, static threatening to overtake his consciousness.
Bael was thrown to the floor by a gravitic wave. A shrill squeal escaped him.
Bael felt the crushing weight lessen. He struggled to his knees.
The gravitic pressure dissipated, along with the migraine. Bael's heartbeat settled back into a steady rhythm.
Instead of relief, Bael was flooded with emptiness. VI was right—he already craved his oppressor's return.
He rose, rededicated. He had a legacy to secure.
The yellow warning light gave way to green, and Director William 'Buck' Moffat's knees creaked as he entered containment with a slice of cake.
At the far end of the room was a massive empty frame, the air inside thick like desert heat. He offered four pencils on the ground before it.
The pencil on the far left turned to silvery striated lithium.

Two objects blinked into existence on the ground in response. Lee always gave back two: one of hers, one of his. A varsity jacket gifted to Teresa Kierczynski, and Dr. Davis's gardening journal. Moffat had memorized the objects that disappeared when they did—his briefcase, her car, the USS Hornet—and seethed over decades as Lee would drip-feed them back. Twenty years talking to the elevated gravity levels in the basement, and all Lee would do was rummage around its lost and found.
Moffat nudged the jacket. YERO. A mix of sadness, sentiment, and nostalgia moved him to ask one last time.
The second pencil turned to carbon, a yes, and Moffat's shoulders unstooped as he sat straight the hell up.

Wilson Lake wasn't known for having the deepest water, nor the biggest fish. What it did have was a tiny cabin with a big bay window that perfectly framed the lake at sunset. Its rickety dock was just big enough to hold a couple of folding chairs and a cooler filled with lunch meat sandwiches and ice-cold drinks.

Louis always carried the chairs; Ben always carried the poles. Louis cracked open the cans; Ben put the worms on the hooks. And hours later, when they were done, they'd come back to a patio picnic table set with a relish tray, a citronella candle, and four hands of cards dealt out. Rummy if Ma was dealing, conquian if it was Pop. Ben always won.

Wilson Lake was where the Yero boys learned how to swim, where they caught too many bullheads to count, where they showed off to the three Hannon sisters who sometimes sat on the beach across the lake. Where Louis nearly drowned when he was five, where Ben cut his calf open on the boat trailer when pulling the damn thing in for the winter.

In the long exposure of lives across time, two blurry boys run in long, streaking pathways. Swimming, playing, growing. But through the blur, clear as a July afternoon, sit a couple of brothers, in a couple of folding chairs, with a couple of fishing poles and a cooler filled with lunch meat sandwiches and ice-cold drinks.
Twin Bird wrote often of the gift of want. To want is to suffer nobly, and to obtain is to extinguish the fire of pursuit.

I reflect now on my own wants. I want the City freed. I want the Light eliminated. I want the Traveler smoldering with a meteor through its center. I want my family whole. And yet, when I reach for my desires, I grasp only fog.

VI showed me everything I ever wanted, only to chide it would not come to pass. Then he left. No thank-yous, no good-byes. I tried to follow him. Flew to Pan, to his innermost moon. I waited there for days, demanding an explanation. I yelled until I was hoarse; I slammed my fist so hard the metal dented the console. Nothing. Part of me hoped Lume would answer my invitation to join me on Pan. Even called the Emissary (useless snake—I am a fool to try to appease a liar). Finally, in the silence of his absence, I realized the reality of my privation: I wanted many things, but I did not want VI to return.
There is nothing left. I am the conduit through which all futures flow, which is to say, I am a vessel. Which is to say, I am empty.

Now I sit, journal in hand, in Bonnet Plaza. Left my helmet, let down my hood; with VI's alterations, no one would recognize me anyway. Let them stare. Screw it. Maybe she will still be here. I don't care if she doesn't know who I am. I want to see her.

"Ah, yes. In those days, I thought an unlimited lifespan would allow me to unravel the mysteries of the universe. Illuminate even the Darkness."

"And all those centuries, I thought I knew my own heart," he continued. "But, in retrospect, my devotion was always in competition with the unknown. Now, my dearest Saint, I'm ashamed to admit that I loved you with only half my heart."

"Now, stripped of my Light, deprived of the health and vigor I once took for granted, I've come to learn that the only mystery that ever truly mattered was you. What you were thinking and feeling. And the depth of emotion we shared."
"I once tore apart the very fabric of time because I couldn't abide a reality without you in it. I'd rather live one short life together than an eternity apart. And with the little time I have left—"
"THEY DIDN'T HAVE THE DRINK YOU LIKE," Saint shouted down the hallway, slamming the door behind him. "So I got one of everything."
"Nothing important, now that you're here," Osiris replied. "Come. Pour us some libations and tell me about your day."
Osiris leaned back on his chaise lounge while Saint-14's Ghost hovered over the end table behind him.
Saint rounded the corner with a sack of groceries in hand and stopped short. "What's happening here? Thrilling Geppetto with more of your memoirs?" he teased.
