Weapon final blows with non-precision direct hits end this effect early.
Precision final blows while aiming down sights grant damage resistance until you stop aiming down sights.
Final blows to a challenging combatant or higher-ranked target grant Unstable Essence. When you have Unstable Essence, you receive grenade and melee stat bonuses.
Defeating targets with unique elemental damage grants a stacking bonus to Transcendence energy gains while Transcendence is inactive.
While Transcendence is active, using your grenade ability consumes all stacks of Stack 'Em Up to grant an escalating amount of grenade energy.
"A queen has little right to leave her people," Crow's sister says, eyes distant and shoulders firm. "And I have long used up what right I had."
"I've found it only a partial relief, myself," Crow admits. "I know I'm helping; I know I need some duty greater than myself to keep me from rushing off into the wild. But the wild has its pull…"

"I'm sorry," says Crow. "I know—I can feel how much Sjur means to you. Here we are, in the cages we picked, and we can't get ourselves to step back out the open doors. But… maybe we can find the answer all the same."
"We'll find a worthy knight for your quest. That's a promise from the Hunter Vanguard—and your brother."
Crow readjusts on the windowsill, keeping her and the shifting mists outside equally in view.

The Dreaming City gives Crow a sense of claustrophobia. He can't shake the stiffness in his shoulders whenever he visits, like his body's waiting for someone to pop out from behind a convenient boulder with a rifle and a set of handcuffs.
She has a hand up at her chin, a thoughtful posture turned almost vulnerable. Protective.
Glint pushes against Crow's fingers, trying to see out the window. Crow lets him go.
"In exchange, I'll let you keep Mars. That seems fair."
Once, ten suns strode across the sky; and once, a divine archer shot nine of them from their path.
If good code returns an error, is the code wrong, or has reality changed?
From orbit, Neptune is a labradorite cabochon tossed to the side by a careless jeweler. A gem about to roll off the dark velvet of Sol's heliosphere.
Neomuna is the one point of warmth on the planet, light and life safe under glass.
A trip of four billion kilometers from Earth, awake and planning the whole time, and Astraea has no idea what to say. She has too many questions. She wants too much.
In the end, she gives up and adds a simple annotation to the handshake protocol's first salute.
She sends it tumbling down the gravity well to the CloudArk.
No response but the tightening of Neomuna's firewalls.
The mind behind the CloudArk sends back a malicious executable. It's a slap to the face. Astraea's own firewalls clamp down on it instantly.

Astraea packages up everything from Bray's black box, every dirty secret she could never pass on to her residents. She collects everything but the key to her own kernel; she isn't his secret keeper anymore. Exabytes of information all screaming the same message: We were wronged by the same person.

As she waits for a response, a trio of Human jumpships swoop past. Their pilots chatter on open bands: patrol schedules, anti-Vex armaments, cheat codes written on the sides of cabs in the best Neomuni arcade. Astraea watches them drop into atmosphere.
A new file emerges from the CloudArk. This one is innocuous, a program to convert visual data between 65 standardized color spaces.
It's a long, long time before Astraea gets a reply to that one. Processes continue within the CloudArk, opaque behind its protective walls. The jumpships far out of reach.
Before she can reply, another message comes in.
And the attenuated connection opens up. The handshake protocol completes without comment. Neomuna's firewalls shift, creating a tunnel. A way in.
Dripping with comfort. And safety. Almost certainly safety.
Drawn taut. Perched gently. A wing flickers. All changes.
Most plants do not suit a vacuum; but some, introduced to new conditions, positively thrive.
And the Erinyes, the furies of vengeance, were called gracious; for what sufferer would not crave the grace of vengeance?
There is beauty in the arcs left behind, when all but the necessary is carved free.
A replica of a classic Cabal ship style, sized down to suit a Guardian and company.
"Mr. Yero? Call me Gideon."
"Mr. Yero, I am uninterested in profiting off of misfortune—"
"Bull. I know what you lawyers do after this kind of thing—"
"I believe the DEO lied to you, Mr. Yero."
"A good one." The attorney nodded at the waitress, who brought a matching coffee. "I read your brother's obituary. I assume you spoke with Director Moffat?"
"…He said there was an accident."
"Take your time."
"…The director said it was a national security risk to tell us anything more," he composed himself, "Only that there wasn't a body left."
"Mr. Yero… will you join the Davis family in pursuing legal action against the federal government?"

"I like your little hats!" Failsafe chirped to the trio of Ghosts as they coasted into the H.E.L.M. Then, in her dour monotone, "They make you look like severed astronaut heads, floating through space. So cool."
"Thanks, Failsafe," Ghost replied, his voice straining to remain upbeat. "That's actually what we came to talk to you about. Shells, I mean."
"We're impressed by your perseverance, Sister Failsafe," Geppetto said. "However, we regret the conditions that you've been forced to endure these past years."
"In gratitude," Ghost said, "the Ghost Community Theater organized a collection to get you something."
"We'll transfer you over with full piloting authorization," Glint continued. "Now you can go anywhere you want!"
"My queen."
"What would you suggest?"

"…The only answer I can see is to pull everyone out, get them to the Tangled Shore," says the other being, in coruscations of doubt and the-world-that-isn't-yet. The egg tooth isn't strong enough; it wants denseness, bone, ivory, steel. "But—how, with Riven and Dûl Incaru's curse alive?"
For Ghosts who see past the edge of the world.
For Ghosts who make their points with perfect style.
For Ghosts who will always remember old friends.

Ben Yero sat at the diner counter as the bell chimed on the door behind him. It was the first time he'd left the house in a week, only thing he'd been able to do was write his brother's obituary. He was empty with grief, and only fire remained.

In that moment, Ben was at the counter in Chicago, but in another, he was eleven years old in Lodi, Wisconsin, socking a seventh grader in the jaw, Lou bruised and sprawled on the pavement behind him, marveling up at Ben with boundless devotion.
For Ghosts who meet the stars up close and personal.

The ribbon-cutting ceremony for the YERO-DAVIS MEMORIAL WING will begin promptly at 9:00 a.m. in the lobby of the Wabash office, beneath the new statue. Attendance is appreciated but not mandatory. Inform your teams that after the ceremony has concluded, attendees will be provided with breakfast in the cafeteria.
For Ghosts who build strength into their foundations.
For Ghosts who get lost in the weeds.
For Ghosts who venture fearlessly into the cosmos.
For Ghosts who will always be by your side.
We have held barriers between us for too long, and to remedy this, I will be the first to begin the dismantling and rebuilding process: I forgive you and Elisabeth.

I recognize that your efforts to undermine me, my legacy, and our family's corporation have been under the banner of "altruism." Let us bury the past and build anew. I know my methodologies and logic have been perceived as disagreeable by some, but considering recent events, now is time for me to rejoin humanity.
Since my reawakening, the only person who has come to keep me any regular company has been an upstart named Fenchurch. His relationship with his niece was my inspiration for mending our bridge.

He has proven to be quite an acquaintance though, sharing much of what I have missed while being abandoned in this basement. Most notably, he has told me about the Prophecy to "Bind the Nine." This has piqued my interest, as you might imagine. It is also the reason why, after years of sharing our family's knowledge and resources to bolster the City's foundries and his trading company's ornamental wares, he has agreed to hand-deliver this message to you.

I believe I am the only one knowledgeable enough to get through to these celestial bodies, for the benefit of our lineage and all of mankind. After my previous experience with the Exo frame, our combined knowledge should enable me to place my consciousness into a new, fully-formed frame. Once mobile, I am willing to join your Vanguard's leadership for the betterment of humanity.
Ghost, Geppetto, and Glint fanned out, each casually scanning the interior of the defunct spacecraft. Even by crash-landing standards, it was a dingy mess.

Wiring sprung out of junction boxes, disordered and sparking. Most of the fittings had been ripped out by black market scavengers. Even the interior cameras, which Failsafe used for vision, were either vandalized or stolen. Glint let out a low frequency buzz of dismay.
He paused as the roar of a ship's engines filled the cabin. The now-flimsy structure rattled and shook as the ship landed somewhere nearby.
The trio of Ghosts let out an infrasonic harmony of delight.
HUSH. I AM NOT HERE TO BRING YOU ALARM-CLARION WAKEFULNESS.
LET ME TELL YOU A STORY. A WARNING PARABLE FOR DARK MATTER. A GLIMPSE OF THE END.
ONCE UPON A TIME, THERE WAS A GAME.
THEY WERE SET IN MOTION BY A WILL WE CANNOT CONTEST.
YET WE MUST TRY. THE GAME WILL NOT REMAIN WITHIN THE BOUNDING-BOARD.
TO YOU, OUR MINDS ARE VAST, OUR SELVES UNFATHOMABLE.
Becoming is a long process, warm and dreamy inside the egg. The whim drinks its dam's stories and drowses.
Foreign body-warmth between the seven of them. A vibration of approaching—voices.
Calm wholeness in one voice, tense want in the other. Is it time to turn becoming into being? The whim becomes something with a tympanum to listen.
Longing! Deep longing! The tense voice wants something outside the world-that-is. Half-formed claws scratch impotently at the inner curve of shell. For the first time, the whim feels hunger.
The caul of dam-stories and sire-vows breaks between gemstone teeth. Eggshell scatters.
Two beings among the whim's lazy still-egged sibs: unwanting and watching, wanting and braced.
Perfect. Aiming for its first meal, the whim leaps free.
The chaos of the Nine eventually flattens into a hum. It's almost a harmony if you let it warp your mind enough. Keep listening, and it starts to feel like it may lead to something.
lines.speaker: Lodi

lines.text: Lodi has been invaluable in our response to the Nine's actions on Kepler and beyond. An Emissary's duties run both ways.
lines.speaker: Ikora

lines.text: It's astounding, the damage that comes from just Nine individuals who can't agree with each other.
lines.speaker: Lodi

lines.text: "We shall see my sisters again," she promises him. "Xivu Arath and her narrowboat on the Sea of Screams… and Eris, oh, sweet Eris."

"She hatched from her flesh and molted into my sister." Savathûn tells him because he would do well to remember this truth. It will ever be true. "Sisterhood cuts both ways. I have killed my sisters before, and I shall do so again."
"I hadn't noticed." It was true. "They haven't accepted me. I'm not sure what it's going to take."
"You're in charge. You'll never quite be one of them."
"Ever since Kepler, the future and the present mean the same thing to you. The Guardian, too."
"I'd be lying if I said this has nothing to do with the Nine. What do you have?"
"Saint-14. He knows what he fights for, and he puts the people of the City above all else."
"Giving him the seat is giving a side table to Osiris."
"—now Nine have chosen our son, our Xûr—"
"And then someone starts shouting, but I can't make out the words. Then there's another voice. And another. Soon it's a giant mob, all shouting gibberish."
"And the smooth surface, the still lake. It starts quavering. Or… oscillating? And each new voice makes it more turbulent. And I feel sick, like…"
"Sure. But I'm the sea, if that makes sense. The noise keeps building and building, until I feel like my skull is about to burst. I lash out to make them stop and… then I wake up."
"It's strange because it doesn't feel like me," Lodi explained. "It feels foreign. Hostile."
"That's because it's not your dream," Orin supplied. "Or even a dream at all, but a… vicarious experience."

"Emissaries translate the Nine's messages into human speech and thought," Orin elaborated. "But what you're describing is the raw experience of BEING the Nine. Or one of them. The remoteness and abstraction sound like V."
"And that shouting mess of voices…?"
"That's what our sentience feels like to them. The Outers, at least. An overwhelming barrage of noise, disturbing their pristine environments."
"Geez. That makes the Outers seem… almost reasonable." Lodi frowned. "Who doesn't want peace and quiet? But their solution—to wipe us all out—can't be the only way."
"My very presence here proves that the Nine are not infallible," Orin offered. "I've come to believe there's another solution out there. One they haven't considered."

"An agent of the Nine reached into your dreams as they did in mine, offering…" Mara Sov's voice washes over the party before pausing in an uncharacteristic tremble. "Commune with me under the gaze of Sjur's effigy. Let us see if their offer carries true or false hope."
"Daughters of Light and Dark who come seeking, Queen Regent of the Dead Reef… the Nine have heard of your plight and offer a bargain."
"I am only a messenger. VI of the Nine offers an end to your pain: Sjur Eido remains, lost in time."
"The Nine arranged for an anointing of a weapon, creation through battle. They placed their pieces, and they reached out."

"Is the future so unclear when your specks of dust are unaligned in their motives?" Mara smirks. "You would not make an offer I could refuse, and so I DO refuse. Your offer has given me the hope I need and the knowledge to peer into time, not place. Why do you think I permitted your entrance into the snare of our dreams? What punishment awaits your failure?"

Xivu Arath draws a cleaver from the chitinous scabbard within her thigh and plunges it into the deck of the Dreadnaught. She looks back to Toland, the Shattered, unsure if his information regarding her throne's location was to be believed. With a turn of her blade, the Sea of Screams twists; Ascendant nebulae flow in rushing torrents, splitting against the blade like thickened fog to reveal her lost throne world.

Ripping her blade upward, she cleaves the border open. Ascendant hallows give way to fetid, blackened rot. The Black Terrace looms over desiccated ruin. Exposed bone walkways crest through split tissues. Hive banners hang in tatters from the battlements with three glowering jade eyes set in the sky. The eyes fix on Xivu; before her materializes a vengeful specter resembling Eris Morn.

The three-eyed specter draws Eris's hooked blade. Xivu charges forward and unleashes a flurry of swings trailed by ghostly soulfire after-strikes. The specter parries, shifts between the onslaught of blows, and retaliates with a thrust that hooks into Xivu's throat.
The Hive god of war laughs, spurting blood down the specter's blade and onto the bone floor. Her burning eyes bore into those of the shadow-Eris.
Xivu grips the hooked blade and tears it violently through the side of her neck and away from her body.
She holds the weapon aside as it bites into her claw and bears down with her own cleaver on the defenseless specter, howling with gurgling laughter. The strike cuts the vengeful thing in twain.
Xivu Arath's throne world thrums as Eris's protective spell falters, and the specter fades along with the three watchful eyes in the sky.
Five worlds hang in a clearing skyscape: Fundament, a fractured Torobatl, Luna, and two shadowed beyond. Dominions of War.

My time as Conductor is ending; I have nothing to replace it with. I am haunted, I am agonized by grief, and I know now my pursuit of Chioma will extend into perpetuity. I am spent, options exhausted even as the network spins new simulations for me to tread. I have no purpose left. I could obtain .87's Chioma. But I can't. I can't.
I do. I weep. She is right. I am exhausted and haunted. I betray Chioma one final time and command myself to let her go.
I see my Chioma. It's the moment I end her. I have everything I had been searching lifetimes for, and instead of embracing her, I kill her.

Her eyes are vacant of her Exo soul, the metal of her shell dull and lifeless. I discard her—I discard mountains of her—and climb so I never have to look down at what I have done. I ignore every summit; I must go higher.
I force myself to turn, and I beg with every fiber of my being that I will not see what I know is there. What I put there. The mountain range of my loss stares back at me with hollow eyes.
The Echo is gone, suffering its final command from a causal mind.
I would have stopped myself had I looked with clear eyes. I realize I haven't thought about her in an age, not in all the years I've chased the idea of her. I see her now. It's too late.
The same accusations blaze in .87's countenance. The potential of the remainder of my life stretches before me.

Mama touches her nose to mine and says we'll see the Traveler today. After we reach the top of the mountain range, after the trees clear, we'll see it floating way up high over the City, and we'll be safe. The Traveler keeps the people in the City safe—that's what everyone says it's there for.

I hope we're close. My shoes are getting holes in them. The ground gets rocky as we climb higher into the mountain. It's cold here too, but we're not cold. My new friend, Béla has a fire he carries in his hand.

We're traveling with people Mama calls "pilgrims." They help us. They helped us when Papa got sick. They helped us when our farm got burnt by the rain. They helped us when Mama said we needed to go far away to be safe.

And when the pilgrims get hurt, little metal birds heal them. Béla says they're Ghosts, but Mama says ghosts aren't real. I talk to the birds a lot. Fiz, Pops, Groendlewic, and Wort. They tell me about the Traveler. I think the Traveler is their mama.

We reach the top of the mountain. I run through the trees. I want to be the first one to see. The birds flutter around me as I look out to the valley. I see a big wall, and I see a big city, and then I see the Traveler.

The sky is empty around it. It's alone. Wort says it looks different from what he remembers—the pretty triangle is new. There are big, old scrapes on it. Like my knee that has a scar shaped like a fish.

Everyone gets so excited when they see the Traveler, but I get sad. The Traveler got hurt but has no one up there—no birds, no mama. I look up to the birds, to the pilgrims, to Mama. I grab her hand. She wipes away my tears and touches her nose to mine.

When we reach the City, the pilgrims talk about finding other pilgrims to help more people like me and Mama. The Traveler hangs low above us, just out of reach. The scars look so deep. Béla asks if I want to get up on his shoulders; I do. I still can't quite reach, but I tilt my head up and know the Traveler can feel the touch of my nose.
Savathûn lays one finger across her face, echoing a human gesture though it means nothing to her own chitin and scale. "It's a secret," she tells him.
There is only the path forward, and Fundament far, far behind, the palest of remembered glints in the long deep night. Without further ceremony, Savathûn gathers herself, and she slips between stars.
Crow stared down at the list of digital missives on his projectors and glared. "This job has been nothing like I expected," he told Ikora on a live connection.
Tactically brilliant. Grit off the charts. But they went on.

Zavala always said the Guardians are not a military. Crow almost suggested that they do away with the position, but continued down the list instead. They spoke through the night. Contemplating the future.

The vote for his induction was complete, and Xûr stood for his formal farewell in the chalkstone temple, its roof facing the stars and rings above. The Priestess gestured towards both of Xûr's arms, smearing wet black silt on his upturned palms.
I SAW YOU, the Alchemist says in Xûr 's mind.
Xûr's feet lifted from the ground. He grew fearful.

Xûr expends the last of his personhood pleading with his god, his painted brow begging for preservation. But his eyes blazed blue, his hand raised on his own, and the last of Xûr's free will burned away as the Alchemist turned the atmosphere of Titan to nitrogen.
Meetings with friends and foes, old and new.
The Nine-touched pair were seated on a terrace in the Bazaar, overlooking the street vendors below. A pre-Collapse ceramic teapot rested between them.

Petra leads Austyn, Sjari, and Ylaia through the halls of Eleusinia, guiding the Techeuns through Taken corruption and across perilous rafters spanning an unending depth below until reaching a tall marble carving of a woman. There, Mara Sov awaits them. Petra and the Techeuns bow in the presence of their queen.

The three do as they are told. Days pass as they scour Sol, until a faint image of a tall huntress catches Sjari's notice in a distant dark fold of space, standing beside Xûr of the Nine. Mara pounces at the opportunity, casting the party towards it. But when they arrive, only Xûr of the Nine, backed by the great mass of Saturn looming behind him, is present.
Austyn begins to step forward, but Mara grips her shoulder. Austyn freezes, stunned that her queen would deign to touch her, before processing the danger of Xûr's proposition.

Huginn and Muninn she fought, and strove bravely, a last dance between old comrades. And on the precipice of victory—the Nine touched that space. One two three, Huginn and Muninn and Sjur Eido, all in that moment overcome by the Nine's reach. Together faltered. Drew. Loosed. Fell.
It is a message carried a long way, scripted to play on the heart. Mara holds perfectly still. It is truth enough. She puts composure on like a cloak.
A vibrant reminder of the violence between dimensions.
When entropy is all you know, chaos almost seems intelligible.

"Taox is alive," Bael asserts. "She's gathering strength in the Vex network, on a simulated Fundament." Bael meets Savathûn's gaze and steps forward with a well-hidden limp before planting himself. "My master offers passage to her location for your service in ridding a thorn from our side."
"VI offers you the Echo, and all the control it conveys." The Dredgen's words land with heavy gravity. Savathûn's eyes widen. "Take it and crush your enemy. Turn her to your will, if you wish."
"Is that so?" Savathûn purrs. " Where does this path lead for VI, my dear new friend?"
"These are the terms," Geist spits over Bael's shoulder. "All that is required is that you sweep aside a weakening upstart and tithe her death to VI. What say you, Witch Queen?"
It's an Arcadia class underneath. Some kind of vintage Golden Age retrofit.
lines.speaker: Crow

lines.text: Savathûn speaks the name with venom. A Dredgen and a Lucent Knight stand before her, deep within the bone-white towers of her throne world. The Knight does not bow, nor avert his gaze from the Witch Queen, even as the Dredgen known as Bael lowers his head in respect. She knows this Knight—Geist—but not why he limits himself to fighting alongside a Lightless Dredgen.
Bael raises a hand to Geist, who sneers, but then quiets. The Witch Queen's eyes shift from Bael to Geist and back.
I ever tell you I saw one of these? In the sky, I mean. Not as a laser bike. The bike's nice too.

lines.text: Great news! As per our conversations about the Aionian exchange program—Dean Rebecca enthusiastically accepted the offer! She agreed with your idea that the primary goal would be a cultural exchange, and she's begun fielding applications from the Aionians' School of Anthropology. Would you be opposed to other special-interest applicants as well? The Dean suggested a student from the School of Botany, and I, selfishly, have a Linguistics student I would like to nominate for the exchange.

A logistical consideration: We're not entirely sure if leaving Kepler will have a significant impact on Aionian physiology. My understanding is that exposure to the singularity, the Aionians' "Holy Anomaly," affects their relationship with time. Some of the Aionians are much older than they seem—older than humanly possible, even. The Dean's wary. She and the rest of the Aionians recognize this step as necessary for the progress of humanity, but I can't forget the papers they published on their previous experiments with leaving the planetoid. Dean Rebecca seemed reassured by your plan to have extra medics on hand should the worst happen—all we can do is be prepared.

I'm sure you've got a mental list of folks from the City itching to participate in the exchange. Knowing you, it's already thirty names deep. I can think of at least eight off the top of my head. If anyone else is interested, I can help make the arrangements. We could discuss further over lunch next week?
P.S. Remind me to tell you about the cake I just found.

"The game is dodgeball—"
"It's—" Lodi strained slightly. "Rain incoming. Just checking the acidity. III's absence causing spontaneous alchemical instability. The kids'll be OK; the water's just going to taste bitter."
"Happy to. This city's starting to feel like home. Even if it's not the one I remember."
"Survive your new cosmic handlers, Mister Yero. You remain a testament to humanity's sheer force of will. The Vanguard are preparing an operation, intending for you to help lead it."
"Scour the Exodus sites on record—in case we need to make one final flight to safety. If the crisis on Earth pervades, humanity ends."
"Seems like a fifth arm to me," Spider finally opined. "Betting is just a small part of my operation. Hardly worth mentioning."

"Revenue wise, maybe," Prak'kesh fired back. "But there ain't a lot of other ways to put Lightbearers in your pocket, are there? Hell, I got Dredgens that would ace a whole scav crew to get off my books. The leverage is part of the vig."
"One-point-two in Glimmer and I'll throw in the land at the edge of the Farm—not the spot in town." Spider tapped on his datapad. "Lot… 3237. Final offer."
"And one of those new SRL Skimmers," Prak'kesh added. "The ones with the articulating stabilizer fins."
"Deal," Spider said. "Just give us a week to… acquire it."
"Soon as I see the deed and the Glim in my account, I'll transfer the books."
"Enjoy retirement while it lasts," Spider snarked. "I'll bet you're both back in the game by this time next year."
Lodi and Lord Shaxx watched a sea of unruly children swarm Variisis Field. A child wearing a paper facsimile of Crow's face stood atop a dirt mound and howled. Lodi grinned.

Years ago, my Ghost lost her voice when I got us into an ice-cold situation on one of the Cabal Emperor's Athenaeum worlds. A couple other Lights didn't make it out, but thanks to her, I did. Hand to my heart, I regret it—and I thought she and I were making progress, especially after Kepler. She's clearly holding some grudges, but—thanks for helping her just the same. Now let's see what we can do to take this fight to the Imperium.
lines.speaker: The Drifter

lines.text: While on your way to speaking with Spider, your Ghost picked up something on tracker, with Drifter's HUD code attached. Take a look at what he's left you.
Zavala has called us to answer for our actions, but he seems reluctant to restrict your off-world activities.

You've escaped from the Imperium, for now, and received Commander Zavala's reluctant blessing to confront them. However, Drifter is certain the Nine are involved with their sudden rise in the system. Speak to Drifter in the Tharsis Cantina to learn more.
Commander Zavala needs to be made aware of the threat Drifter and the crew have uncovered.
Aunor would like our help discovering what the newly emerged Dredgen Bael is up to, alongside the crime syndicates of Mars.
Start by assisting her in targeting syndicate operatives across the system to help discover their long-term plans.

Spider leans back and guffaws into the air. "You enraged all three major syndicates in a single infiltration of the Lawless Frontier," he spits gleefully. "Well done, renegade. Your reward: a few ontological materials Drifter's Ghost will need. Kitbash her with these, and she'll be good as new." He reaches out, four paws full of glittering, paracausal metals.

Crime syndicates on Mars seem to be prevalent in Tharsis Cantina. Explore the Cantina, and see what you can learn about these groups. They're made up of species that are typically hostile to humanity. But these gangs don't seem to be particularly aggressive—at least in town.
Spider has given us the final component we needed to repair Drifter's Ghost. Go seek her out at Tharsis Cantina.

Spider would like us to infiltrate the Lawless Frontier, a war zone on the outskirts of Tharsis, to find a missing courier crew that was transporting valuable cargo. In exchange, he has offered to help us secure materials necessary to repair Drifter's Ghost and restore her voice.
Seek out Aunor in the Cantina to learn more about Syndicate bosses and their organizations.

You've exfiltrated successfully from the Lawless Frontier with Spider's package intact, after his courier crew was ambushed in the warzone. Go see Spider about the materials he owes you to help Drifter's Ghost repair her voice.
Despite some moderate success searching Tharsis Outpost, you still lack a complete set of components to repair Drifter's ghost.
Perhaps Spider can help. Find him at Tharsis Cantina.
Your Ghost informs you that Drifter has left you a tape—in physical cassette form, like in the old days. Find and access his recording.
See if Drifter can translate what his Ghost has been trying to communicate to you. She needs your help to get her voice back.

Drifter has told you that his Ghost would like to speak to you. He mentioned he thought he had been earning her trust lately, but she has something to ask you—help her get her voice back, which she lost helping the Drifter. See what you can do to assist.
Speak to Spider in the Tharsis Cantina.

Rescue Drifter from the clutches of the Dredgen holding him captive. Drifter's Ghost is with you, and she's got the encrypted data disk he stole from the Barant Imperium, a new faction of Cabal that has risen up—seemingly out of nowhere. Fight your way through the Zagan Gloriosus and find the Drifter.
Explore Tharsis Bazaar while keeping an eye out for anything that might serve as spare parts for Drifter's Ghost.
Investigate a drop off from Drifter that's pinging your tracker.
"Remember—if you're not scared you're about to crash, you're not going fast enough."

"Guardian. As much as I'd love to find that bastard and wring his neck… we can't." She spits the words like a curse. "Not while Nightfall's still in the sky. Taking that weapon down has to be our top priority. So, let's get started."
"Aghol. Totality Armorer. And you're the Lightbearer who's raised such a ruckus around the place."
"You are extremely puncturable, Guardian unit. Flammable too, in our experience. Might I suggest this defensive tool? Our organization is willing to part with it as a token of equivalent exchange."
"War beckons, my renegade!" Spider booms. "War among the Syndicates for power, prestige, territory! And above all, profit!"
"The Syndicates and their quartermasters have all come to me—on bended knee, mind you—to ask for your assistance."
Aunor wishes to speak with us about next steps. We can find her in the Cantina.
Aunor is waiting to brief us about a jump on Europa to steal an Imperium shuttle.
Zephyrus will have up-to-date tracking information. Return to Tharsis Outpost to meet with them.

There is a window of opportunity to plant the trackers provided by the Tharsis Reformation at an Imperium cargo site on Europa. Whichever shuttle picks up that cargo from Europa is our target to commandeer.
Aunor has acquired intel from the Syndicates on how we can pass through Imperium orbital security to strike at their base on Venus.
Aunor has the details for our next job on Venus. Meet with her.
There's an envelope with your name on it being kept at the bar.
The crew has a plan. It's time to bring Nightfall Station down.

Vixis has provided us with the coordinates for the stolen keycards and has asked us to provide retaliatory support against his recent Imperium attackers. In addition to helping Vixis, it will make a statement for the Pikers to the Imperium and the other syndicates.
Aunor and Eido intend to declassify the Prophecy that the Vanguard have kept under wraps. The people of the City, and of Tharsis Outpost, deserve to know what they're facing.
Together, they have been working to restore a local broadcaster to spread the message. Aunor asks that we retrieve the remaining components.
Drifter has taken the Derelict and gone out on his own. Head to your jump ship and pursue him.
Zephyrus has suggested that we visit the Reformation quartermaster to obtain a method of tracking Imperium vessels.
Dealing with these strange Vex will aid in the fight against the Imperium with tech and intel.
Blue has an update for us about the Imperium data. We should go visit her in the Cantina.
Rao suggested we visit the Totality's Armorer. The Totality Division is willing to supply our cause with ordnance and insurgent soldiers.
With the broadcaster repaired, it's time to share the Prophecy with the world.
Blue is at the Ghost commune. She'd like to speak with you and Ghost in person.
Deoriks flags you down with a wave of a datapad.
You're now fully prepared to take down Nightfall Station's shield generator. Fly your commandeered shuttle to Venus, take down the generator, and expose the station to attack.

Riliks let us know that one of his top splicers was heading up the keycard venture. You've agreed to help, as part of cover to investigate Imperium tests that may be taking place in the Lawless Frontier.
Tharsis is a flurry of illicit activity, and Vixis was recently the victim of possible cross-syndicate conflict, or Imperium intervention.
Riliks has asked that we go look for him outside.

You've established yourself as an emerging player in the Tharsis illicit network, and Drifter has news about a potential exchange with the Piker syndicate he's set up. Speak to him in Tharsis Cantina.
Defy Vanguard orders and delve into the criminal underworld of Tharsis to confront the rising Barant Imperium… Drifter is certain the Imperium and the Nine are connected.
Drifter wouldn't leave without a good reason. He isn't the man he used to be. Meet up with the rest of the crew to discuss next steps.
There's an empty glass on the bar behind Aunor. She pushes it away as you approach, but her hands are steady.
Aunor is furious but has set her frustration aside to keep her mind on the mission. She has chosen to put her faith in you and offers a tool of the Praxic Order. She believes you are ready.
Your foray into the local markets to sell off the extra Imperium uniforms has piqued the interest of the vendors. Visit them and see if their wares can help in your preparations for Venus.
We should check back in with Rao now that we've acquired—and sold—Imperium uniforms for the Venus job.
Vixis has suggested that we pay a visit to the Mechanic, as they may have something for us to help recover the keycards.
You have developed your relationships with the Syndicates enough to leverage their extensive illicit networks in search of any ways to strike back at the Imperium, and bring down Nightfall Station.
Aunor suggested we meet up the Totality Division boss, Rao, for a line on the Imperium callsign.

The Reformancer greets you with a dramatic flourish of its garments. "This unit, designated Guzheng, currently serves as Reformancer. This title is unique and a pleasing degree of outré, just like Guzheng itself.
Aunor believes you have proven your prowess with your Praxic Blade, and it is time to enhance your weapon.
Now that you've done Zephyrus a favor, he owes you one.
Placing banners for the Vex Card Game throughout the Tharsis Bazaar will build camaraderie with Zephyrus's crew.
Vixis appreciates your help with the keycard caches and has provided you with a small bonus in Credits, the dominant currency in Tharsis.
Head to Spider in the Cantina to report your success. He may have some ideas on how to spend your newfound wealth.

We've established a tenuous business relationship with the Pikers, and Drifter has helped us set up an exchange with them: They'll bring a Splicer Shank to help us extract further data from Imperium installations on the whereabouts, defenses, and operational status of Nightfall.
With our Praxic Blade forged, and Aunor's trust in us solidified, we should return to Tharsis and press on with the fight against the Imperium. Aunor has a plan to improve our odds on Venus.

Aunor wants assurances that the job on Venus won't go south. She's conspired with the Totality Division to plant insurgents on Venus with Imperium uniforms. They just need the uniforms—we should reach out to Rao.
With the shield array on Venus disrupted, Nightfall Station is vulnerable.
Rao has informed us of a Vex base on Mars where Reformation frames have absconded with stolen Imperium uniforms—apparently to repurpose as fashionable outerwear.

The Eclipse Energy attack on Tharsis only seems to have affected Ghosts and their Lightbearers, even those still unpaired. Those without the Light were left unscathed. Seek out and help any survivors you can find and search the site for clues about the attack.

Zavala needs to know about the threat unleashed on Tharsis. The Vanguard can't ignore the Imperium any longer. Bring Berlioz's Ghost shell to be interred in the Tower and show him firsthand what has occurred.
Spider has worked with his contacts in the Pikers to obtain a Shank, specially outfitted to breach Imperium security and provide the access we need.

He leans forward, looming over you from his raised seat. "You did this, you know. With the Imperium neutralized, a power vacuum has opened on the Lawless Frontier. Everything is up for grabs, and that includes your allyship.

Now that we've recovered the keycards, we should return to Vixis to help the Pikers get their venture in operation and fulfill your part in the exchange. With the Piker's support, it may be possible to start making bigger moves against the Imperium and their Nightfall plans.
Blue wishes to speak with us, and only us. It seems important.
A Praxic Guardian's education never stops. You've got more to learn about yourself and your Blade, and so do I.
If we're going to change the Order, we need to work at it. Come see me upstairs when you've got a moment.
P.S. Try the Ether Fizz House of Kings style sometime. Don't let the price on the receipt scare you off: it's worth every credit.
Enforcer Rao delivered the location data of Pikers on Venus in possession of an Imperium callsign. They've been using it for smuggling all manner of small tech stock. It's time to pay them a visit.

There were more uniforms in the Reformation's stores than expected. Selling the extra uniforms off will make the reasons behind stealing them harder to discern and should prove to be lucrative. Surely Rao won't miss a surplus they weren't expecting to receive.
Zephyrus has a plan for how we might be able to find the location of a shuttle. We should see what they have to say.
Lodi and Eris would like to speak with you on the Derelict via Ghost Link.
Aunor has informed us of a Praxic Vault on Europa, recently raided by the Imperium. She believes we will find a tool of the Praxic Order there. Something with which to face Bael.
Zavala is willing to discuss the attack at Tharsis.

lines.text: You've walked through Darkness for this. Now find the end.

lines.text: Everything changes from here. Before we dive back in, let's take a moment—and have a drink.
lines.speaker: Aunor Mahal

lines.text: The Temple's Light is back, even with the Darkness lingering. I don't say this a lot so listen close: you were right.
lines.speaker: Aunor

lines.text: There's Darkness within this relic of Light, but they're not competing. They've found their balance. Maybe there's hope for us all.
lines.speaker: Aunor

lines.text: I can't imagine what a Praxic Temple of Light and Darkness would feel like. But I think… I'd like to meditate there.
lines.speaker: Aunor

lines.text: Time to shine, rookie. Show me your Light—and your Dark.
lines.speaker: Aunor

lines.text: We Praxics use Solar Light to contain and purify objects touched by Darkness. Over time, that Light bakes into our temples. It changes them, as the fire changes us all.
lines.speaker: Aunor
